fields.title: Assuta introduces Israel's most advanced radiotherapy technology
fields.bodyHtml:
Radiation has long been used to destroy cancer cells. The process also disrupts the oxidation and reduction reactions inside the cells, which leads to a build-up of incompletely oxidised free radicals. Where irradiation once reached healthy tissue as well and caused complications, treatment today is aimed at the tumour as precisely as possible, so that the surrounding healthy tissue is spared any significant damage.

Radiotherapy technology keeps improving. Newer and more refined systems deliver a stronger and more accurate dose to the tumour, which minimises the effect on healthy cells. These methods are built on computing technology that makes treatment more precise and more effective. Assuta works to maintain high standards and therefore actively adopts advanced technology in its oncology treatment.

Modern radiation therapy is delivered in three dimensions, but the Institute of Radiotherapy in Israel has already developed a four-dimensional format, in which the fourth dimension is the duration of the session. With the new technology the patient no longer has to hold their breath during the procedure. The computing system works by the Monte Carlo method, which is widely used in the space industry and at NASA in particular. Using it, the system calculates the exact position of the tumour and redirects the beam onto its contours as the tumour shifts. Errors and side effects of radiation therapy are offset by continuous real-time monitoring by a Varian system.

The new radiotherapy technology has proved its advantages not only through excellent treatment outcomes but also by shortening the procedure itself. A session now takes no more than ten minutes, and the overall course of treatment is four times shorter. This shortens treatment for the individual patient and also makes radiation therapy available to a greater number of patients. That is why Assuta continues to adopt the newest technologies, to make treatment more effective still.

fields.title: Israel is one of the world's leading countries in cancer treatment
fields.bodyHtml: Detecting a cancer as early as possible with the help of biomarkers is the basis for starting treatment in Israeli clinics in good time. Every year new multi-million grants fund research into fighting cancer. Through the hard work of Israeli oncologists and scientists, cancer therapy is becoming steadily more targeted and more selective. Selective internal radiation therapy is the newest method of treating cancer: nanoparticles that capture malignant cells destroy only the tumour cells and leave normal tissue untouched. The biomedical company Vacciguard continues to develop new methods of cancer immunotherapy.

fields.title: Israel is one of the leading developers of modern diagnostic equipment
fields.bodyHtml: Digital mammography, refined by Israeli radiologists, sharpens the imaging of breast tissue down to the millimetre, which makes it possible to spot the smallest growths at the earliest stages. Three-dimensional coronary angiography gives a detailed spatial image of the vessels of the heart for a more accurate diagnosis of coronary artery disease. The first CT scanner built specifically for the full examination and imaging of the heart was created here. Laboratory systems for studying and sorting cell material and chromosomes in order to diagnose genetic abnormalities have no equivalent anywhere in the world. Scientists from Haifa have created a non-invasive breath test for the early detection of cancer, before the first symptoms appear. A microcamera from the Israeli developers at Given Imaging fits inside a capsule and is widely used for video capsule endoscopy, the most effective method of examining the digestive tract even in places that are hard to reach, such as the middle sections of the small intestine.

fields.title: Israeli doctor: smokers do not simply give up cigarettes, they need an alternative
fields.bodyHtml: Smokers often suffer the consequences of their habit, yet they do not simply stop, even when doctors insistently advise them to. So says Dr Dov Gavish, an atherosclerosis specialist at the Shaare Zedek hospital. In his own column in the newspaper Israel Hayom, Gavish explains that he has often asked patients to stop smoking, but many of them never did, however much he frightened or pleaded with them. He points out that the «official» share of smokers in the Israeli population has not changed for ten years, holding at 20 per cent. In practice this means that the absolute number of smokers is rising, because the population keeps growing. As the doctor notes, many countries, among them Britain, New Zealand and Japan, are officially introducing an «alternative» to tobacco products (electronic cigarettes, apparently). In those countries the share of smokers really is falling. In Israel, by contrast, officials hold that all smoking products are equally harmful, and the very idea that ordinary cigarettes might be replaced by other nicotine options is repugnant to the civil servants leading the campaign against smoking. Because the state fights smoking through prohibition alone, that fight is bearing no fruit, Dov Gavish believes, and what is happening with cannabis proves the point once again. Only when smokers are given an accessible alternative will there be results. He therefore urges the authorities to change the record and stop treating the very idea of an «alternative» to smoking as being as sacrilegious as smoking itself.

fields.title: The beauty of your skin depends entirely on the health of your gut
fields.bodyHtml:
Did you know that problems with your skin are an indicator that your gut is not working as it should?

We are ready to spend a great deal of time and money fighting a dull complexion, spots, irritation, dryness, flaking and so on. Yet even the most expensive branded cosmetic preparation will be powerless if the problem lies inside the body.

The skin is a kind of mirror in which everything happening inside the body can be seen, and the digestive organs in particular. The condition of the skin is affected by various environmental influences and also by irregular eating, which disturbs the gut microflora: disease-causing micro-organisms multiply unchecked, release toxins and pass through the intestinal wall, spreading to the body's other organs. The result is dysbiosis or intoxication. As an organ of elimination, the skin is the first to respond to unfavourable processes in the body, and as a consequence it loses its natural qualities, becoming oily and vulnerable and difficult to care for.

Skin problems may be accompanied by constipation, one of the principal and most unpleasant symptoms of a disturbed gut microflora. Constipation can lead to irreversible health problems. Because of the prolonged delay, the stool sets off pathogenic processes in the body which reach the bloodstream, and this too shows in the condition of the skin.

To restore the health of the gut and, along with it, the condition of the skin, it is necessary to take preparations containing lactulose, a prebiotic that encourages the development of a healthy gut microflora. On reaching the intestine, lactulose feeds the beneficial lactic acid bacteria and stimulates their growth.

Before taking any preparation, however, the digestive organs should be examined in order to identify the cause of the imbalance, assess the state of health and determine the most suitable treatment.

fields.title: An innovative method of treating rectal cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
The present level of medicine gives grounds for hope in a healthy future. Many conditions once considered incurable hold no fear today. That progress rests on the unceasing work of scientists, Israeli ones among them.

In recent years Israeli clinics have made increasing use of minimally invasive techniques with endoscopic and laparoscopic equipment. These developments have reached the standard programmes for treating tumours of the rectum. Where an open operation was once required, hard for the patient to bear and carrying a high risk of injury, the same work can now be done in a far gentler way.

Transanal endoscopic microsurgery (TEM) is an innovative method of treating rectal cancer. Israeli specialists observe that TEM is marked by rapid recovery, because it enters the body as little as possible. The procedure is carried out with a rectoscope through the anus, and no additional openings or incisions are made.

The method is widely used at the Assuta hospital for the resection of large polyps and malignant tumours. Compared with a conventional operation, TEM has substantial advantages:

  • There is no need to form a colostomy, or to cut the rectal sphincter during the procedure;
  • Less pain;
  • A low rate of complications after surgery;
  • A short stay in hospital.

Patients who undergo this procedure generally recover faster and are discharged sooner.

fields.title: Radiation therapy in the treatment of breast cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
The Assuta medical centre in Israel has introduced a change to its breast cancer treatment programme. The change concerns radiation therapy, which works by delivering the dose to a single point during the removal of the growth.

Patients no longer have to go through a long course lasting a month after surgery. The innovative technique makes it possible to deliver the dose precisely while the tumour is being removed, which considerably shortens recovery and spares the patient the side effects of radiation therapy.

According to Dr Dafna Barsuk, a senior specialist at the hospital, this treatment has considerable advantages: the tumour is irradiated precisely, and the beam does not extend beyond its edges. A great many post-operative processes are reduced to a minimum, which shortens the stay in hospital. The patient can return to her home country within a few weeks.

The innovative procedure can be carried out for any indication, whatever the size of the tumour and the age of the patient. The decision to use the method is taken on the basis of the diagnostic results and with the patient's consent.

fields.title: The TEM method: a new technology for treating rectal cancer in Israel
fields.bodyHtml:
TEM, or transanal endoscopic microsurgery, is a new and revolutionary method of treating rectal cancer in Israel. When operating to remove a malignant tumour, most Israeli clinics normally use the minimally invasive laparoscopic method. That technology allows the patient to recover quickly after the intervention, because the entry into the body causes little injury.

Recently, however, doctors at the Assuta clinic have begun removing tumours of the rectum by the TEM method. This method treats the cancer through the anus, without additional incisions, so recovery is faster still. TEM is used to treat cancer at an early stage and also to remove large polyps. The operation is performed with a rectoscope.

Advantages of the TEM method:

  • Less pain
  • A short period of required hospitalisation
  • A low rate of complications
  • No need to cut the rectal sphincter during the operation
  • A low proportion of operations that end in the formation of a colostomy

Many doctors at the Assuta clinic already perform operations by the TEM method, working to give patients treatment of the highest quality and effectiveness. Every patient of the clinic receives qualified care, round-the-clock attention and comfortable rooms while being treated in Israel.

fields.title: Darling, I want a boy — take an aspirin
fields.bodyHtml:
Taking aspirin raises the likelihood of having a boy. That is the conclusion of a study reported by The Daily Mail.

The study involved 1,228 women who had previously had miscarriages.

All the participants intended to become pregnant again. The researchers asked the women to take either low doses of aspirin or a placebo (folic acid) before sex.

As the newspaper reports, the authors of the study suggested that the miscarriages were linked to a high level of inflammation in the womb. One of the versions considered was that the immune system perceives the developing embryo as a foreign body and reacts aggressively to it.

The researchers proposed that inflammation reduces the chances of having a boy, given that male embryos are considered more vulnerable.

The study data allowed them to state that women who took aspirin before sex gave birth to boys more often than the participants who received the placebo (31 per cent against 23 per cent).

The checks also established that the level of inflammation fell in the women who took aspirin.

Original source: 9tv.co.il

fields.title: Ministry of Health: Israel to lift quarantine for those infected with coronavirus in June
fields.bodyHtml: Israel may lift quarantine for coronavirus patients altogether in June. That forecast was given by Professor Salman Zarka, the coordinator of the campaign against coronavirus and director of the Ziv hospital in Safed, at a briefing on Tuesday 31 May. He stressed that a decision to lift quarantine could be taken closer to the end of the following month.

fields.title: How effective is neoadjuvant chemotherapy in ovarian cancer?
fields.bodyHtml:
The standard programme for treating advanced ovarian cancer today consists of cytoreductive surgery and chemotherapy that includes platinum-based drugs. A number of clinical studies carried out in earlier years show, however, that overall survival among patients who received neoadjuvant chemotherapy is no lower than among those who underwent cytoreduction.

These results considerably influenced how often neoadjuvant chemotherapy is used in hospitals in many countries. In the United States, however, the choice between neoadjuvant chemotherapy and cytoreductive surgery has always remained a matter of debate.

To settle the question, a number of further studies were carried out weighing the advantages and drawbacks of neoadjuvant chemotherapy for patients with ovarian cancer. This time the results proved rather contradictory. The assessments show that in patients with stage 3 ovarian cancer overall survival is lower than in patients who did not undergo this form of chemotherapy.

Studies were carried out on overall survival in patients with stage 3 and stage 4 cancer treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Here favourable outcomes were seen in patients with stage 3 disease: a considerable reduction in the tumour, and no need for hospitalisation.

From these observations it may be concluded that neoadjuvant therapy is indicated for patients whose cancer is at a less advanced stage. Before choosing treatment, however, the patient's medical history and the results of diagnostic investigations should be taken into account. Even so, the frequency with which neoadjuvant chemotherapy is given to patients with ovarian cancer has risen noticeably.

fields.title: A new method of restoring cartilage tissue
fields.bodyHtml:
Indian scientists are doing a great deal of work on a new method of restoring cartilage tissue and advancing regenerative medicine. The field is also developing actively in Israel.

Over the past few years many methods have been developed, each raising the figures for effectiveness and safety, though each came with certain reservations. Scientists in different countries nevertheless continue to work on improving orthopaedics.

One international association of engineers has developed a high-quality alternative to the ink used in three-dimensional bioprinting, making it possible to produce cartilage patches that may solve the problem of worn joints. The resulting cartilage tissue is convenient to print, consists of a single cell type and has no blood vessels.

The new technology requires no scaffold and is produced from alginate and seaweed extract. According to the specialists, the resulting thread of cartilage tissue will serve well as a replacement for bio-ink.

fields.title: A discovery in the treatment of breast cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Breast cancer is a pressing problem that takes the lives of a great many women every year. A still greater number need breast reconstruction, which carries a psychological cost of its own. Cancer researchers in every country have been working to address this for many years. Their work involves deep investigation not only of the causes of the disease but also of the structure of the breast itself.

Recently, experts at one Western university identified within the structure of the breast a particular group of bacteria that encourage malignant processes in the organ and are also capable of halting cancer. For the purposes of the research, the structure of the breast was studied in women with cancer and in healthy women. It emerged that all the women had the same micro-organisms in the breast, and that the difference lay only in their quantity.

The findings gave rise to a number of further questions: for instance, whether these bacteria provoke cancer or begin to multiply as the malignant process develops. The question of how beneficial bacteria might halt the development of cancer also remains open.

Despite the ambiguous results, the scientists have set out a plan for the coming few years and intend to carry out experiments that will either clarify or refute the proposed theory.

fields.title: PCR tests on entry to Israel abolished with effect from 21 May 2022
fields.bodyHtml:
The Ministry of Health announces: from 21 May 2022, PCR tests on entry to Israel will be abolished for Israelis and foreign nationals alike.
Foreign nationals will also no longer need to take a PCR test or an antigen test before boarding a flight.

Following the fall in coronavirus cases, from 21 May 2022 (at midnight between Friday and Saturday, Israel time) the requirement to take a PCR test on entry to Israel will be lifted, at Ben Gurion airport and at land and sea crossings, for Israelis and foreign nationals alike.

The requirement previously placed on foreign nationals to take a PCR test or an antigen test before boarding a flight or crossing into Israel by land or sea will also be lifted, as will the requirement to be tested before a cruise departing from Israel.

Passengers must still complete an entry declaration for Israel within the 48 hours before boarding a flight or vessel.

The Ministry of Health will continue to update this information should the guidance change further.

fields.title: Precancerous conditions: how they are treated
fields.bodyHtml:
A precancerous condition is a process in which the body's tissues change abnormally, with a high probability that they will subsequently turn into cancer cells. When the body is entirely healthy, the likelihood of cancer arising is minimal. One illness or another may, however, act as the catalyst for a malignant tumour. Healthy cells are transformed in several stages, which can be identified during examination.

Several kinds of precancerous condition are distinguished: facultative, obligate, pre-invasive and invasive. A person diagnosed with a precancerous condition enters the group at high risk of developing cancer. With such a diagnosis the patient should remain under medical observation. It is important to note that a patient diagnosed with a precancerous condition will not necessarily go on to develop cancer. Modern treatment methods help to reduce the risk of cancer to nil.

One of the most effective ways of dealing with a precancerous condition is a bone marrow transplant. The treatment is aimed at improving the blood counts and preventing the cells from transforming. With constant monitoring of health and timely diagnostic investigations, it is possible today to rule out the development of cancer entirely.

fields.title: A breakthrough in the treatment of leukaemia
fields.bodyHtml:
The Assuta medical centre hosted an international symposium on oncohaematology. It presented the results of clinical trials of innovative treatments for leukaemia, among which the discovery by the leading professor Kanti Rai stood out.

For fifty years the professor has studied the nature of malignant blood diseases, work for which he has received honours and awards. One of his achievements is a set of highly effective long-acting biological drugs. According to the professor, drugs based on these active components make it possible to cure lymphocytic leukaemia at every stage of the disease, with no side effects.

The discovery was indisputably a revolution in biological and targeted therapy. On the basis of the present results, Israeli specialists nevertheless plan to broaden the range of action of biological drugs and to refine the technique of targeted therapy in the treatment of oncohaematological diseases.

According to Professor Yehoshua Shemer, specialists at the Assuta hospital continue to develop methods of treatment and diagnosis, to introduce unique treatment programmes and to improve how patients are received at the hospitals.

fields.title: A breakthrough in cancer treatment: a new device at the Assuta hospital destroys tumours four times faster
fields.bodyHtml:
Five radiotherapy sessions instead of twenty — such is the effect of the new device

A breakthrough in the treatment of tumours of the prostate, pancreas, liver and lungs: the Assuta hospital in the Ramat HaHayal district of Tel Aviv has begun delivering focused radiotherapy using a linear accelerator combined with MRI. The new device makes it possible to irradiate diseased areas without damaging healthy tissue. «We are the first oncology department in Israel where this procedure is carried out. Worldwide there are only thirty such clinics,» said Professor Merav Ben-David, a radiotherapist and head of the hospital's oncology clinic. «This method offers hope to many cancer patients in Israel and around the world. Medical tourists come to us from Russia, Armenia, Uzbekistan and other countries.»

The MR Linac device, made by the American company ViewRay, is an accelerator combined with MRI. It produces a guiding image during irradiation, which makes it possible to track the position of the tumour precisely. As a result, tumours can be irradiated with greater accuracy than before.

Obtaining an MRI image while the accelerator is working makes it possible to see the movement of the organs in real time; irradiation is interrupted and resumed automatically as the tumour returns to the treated area.

fields.title: Radiotherapy in Israel as the principal method of treating cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Earlier methods of radiotherapy involved irradiating the diseased area with high doses of radiation energy. Under the strong beam, the tumour processes were destroyed. The destructive effect, however, also reached neighbouring healthy tissue, which led to complications.

Modern radiation technologies using linear accelerator particles are designed to affect healthy cells as little as possible while acting more powerfully on cancer cells. Even so, this design of irradiator is not the last word in medicine.

Despite the results already achieved, Israeli scientists work constantly on improving treatment methods and the technical characteristics of medical equipment. Their contribution to modern engineering is already plain to see.

Until recently the three-dimensional radiation system was a revolution in medicine. Today Israeli engineers have developed a four-dimensional format of irradiation. The newest development makes it possible to treat hard-to-reach, mobile tumours that move to their own rhythm, shifting the focus of the disease.

The new system is built so that the patient need not hold their breath during a session of irradiation. The equipment can locate the tumour precisely and change the direction of the beams by itself as the tumour moves.

Scientists consider this technique the most effective of those available and regard it as the one method capable of defeating cancer. Judging by the many reports, the technology rules out errors and side effects and does not damage neighbouring organs and tissue. What is more, because the dose is higher, the number of sessions and their length are considerably reduced, which allows the patient to recover sooner and makes the procedure available to a greater number of patients.

fields.title: Cancer is afraid of a healthy lifestyle
fields.bodyHtml:
We are told about the benefits of a healthy lifestyle, but few people keep to one.

A healthy lifestyle means more than giving up alcohol and nicotine. It includes a proper diet, regular physical activity, a sensible working pattern, rest and much else. But the question arises: how does all this affect the development of cancer?

A large number of cancer cases are linked precisely to an unhealthy lifestyle and to environmental factors rather than to genetic causes, in the view of scientists at Arizona State University in the United States.

The experts analysed twelve studies examining the link between lifestyle and death from cancer. The participants ranged in age from 25 to 79.

It was established that when cancer prevention recommendations were followed, the risk of developing the disease fell from 10 to 45 per cent, and the likelihood of death from 14 to 6 per cent. The incidence of breast cancer fell from 60 to 19 per cent, of endometrial cancer from 60 to 23 per cent, and of bowel cancer from 52 to 27 per cent.

Dr Lindsay Kohler, the author of the new study, said: «Failure to follow a proper diet, lack of physical activity, alcohol consumption and smoking are the cause of the disease in more than 20 per cent of cases, so by changing one's way of life one can reduce the likelihood of illness.»

It follows from these figures that one cancer patient in five brought the malignancy upon themselves.

Original source: 9tv.co.il

fields.title: Once and for all: which free tests in Israel save people from cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Early diagnosis improves the outlook for survival, and even for a full recovery

At what age should a woman have a mammogram? What is the difference between a colonoscopy and a faecal occult blood test? Can fifty diseases be detected by a simple blood test? Which examinations make it possible to find tumours at an early stage and save a life? Let us look at each in turn.
Early diagnosis of cancer of the cervix
In 99 per cent of cases cervical cancer is caused by the human papillomavirus (HPV), which is transmitted sexually. There is now an examination that looks for the DNA of this virus (HPV DNA). If the results call for further investigation, a PAP smear is taken. The combination of these two diagnostic methods makes it possible to detect precancerous changes in the cervix. The Ministry of Health recommends that women aged 25 to 65 have a cervical smear once every three years, or as directed by their doctor. Sadly, only 50 per cent of women in that age group attend for this examination.
Early diagnosis of breast cancer
The well-known screening examination that makes it possible to find a tumour at an early stage is mammography. For women with no family history of the disease and no particular risk factors, mammography is recommended between the ages of 35 and 74, once every two years. A mammogram is a quick X-ray of the breast tissue. It makes it possible to detect growths in the breast at a very early stage, when they still cannot be felt. Take-up of mammography is higher than for other screening examinations. Awareness of the procedure has grown in recent years, but not all women come forward, and there are groups of the population where the proportion who do is very low.
Detecting breast tumours early saves the lives of women in 90 per cent of cases or more.
Early diagnosis of lung cancer. Many methods of treating this disease have been developed in recent years, particularly at the early stages, so early diagnosis considerably improves the chances of survival. At present, in most patients the tumour is found only once it has already spread.
From 2022 the Ministry of Health, together with the health funds, began a trial of early lung cancer diagnosis. This is an examination based on low-dose computed tomography (CT) of the chest. It is intended for smokers, or for those who previously smoked a packet of cigarettes a day for twenty years or two packets a day for ten. It should be noted that an important measure for preventing lung cancer, as for a number of other tumours, is giving up smoking.
Early diagnosis of bowel cancer. Among the important forms of examination is the faecal occult blood test. This simple examination can save a life. Hidden bleeding is often the first symptom of an early-stage bowel tumour. Finding precancerous growths (polyps) in the bowel makes it possible to remove them before they turn malignant. It is important to remember that early diagnosis of bowel cancer considerably improves the likelihood of a cure. The Ministry of Health recommends this examination for people aged 40 to 74 who have no additional risk factors. In certain cases — where there is polyposis, inflammatory bowel disease, or first-degree relatives (parents, siblings, children) with a bowel tumour — a colonoscopy is recommended, which allows examination of the rectum and the rest of the bowel. A flexible tube with a camera at the end is passed into the bowel through the anus. This examination is not recommended for the population as a whole: it is considered invasive and requires preparation. Take-up of early bowel cancer diagnosis stands at only 66 to 68 per cent.
According to the Israel Cancer Association, a third of those with a positive faecal occult blood test do not follow it up with a colonoscopy, which raises their risk of developing a bowel tumour, and of dying from it, by tens of per cent. Delaying a colonoscopy after occult blood has been found in the stool raises both the risk of the disease itself and the risk of a fatal outcome: a delay of two months by 33 per cent, a delay of a year by 66 per cent.

fields.title: A new type of vaccine has been developed that is capable of defeating any disease
fields.bodyHtml:
The Massachusetts Institute of Technology has developed a new type of vaccine that can be adapted within a short time to fight any epidemic.

As reported in a paper published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, the scientists obtained antigens against the agents of Ebola, swine flu and toxoplasmosis, among others. Their effectiveness approaches 100 per cent.

The method consists in «programming» the structure of messenger RNA to synthesise proteins that activate the immune system to fight a particular disease. As the means of delivering the RNA structure into the cell, the scientists propose using nanoparticles.

RNA-type vaccines can be given intramuscularly. So far they have been tested successfully in mice. A series of experiments recorded resistance to the Ebola virus, swine flu and toxoplasmosis in the laboratory mice.

The scientists note that RNA vaccines are less harmful than conventional DNA vaccines, since they do not alter the genome of the cells and do not lead to subsequent mutations.

Original source: 9tv.co.il

fields.title: A revolution in the treatment of leukaemia
fields.bodyHtml:
Not long ago, scientists developed a way of dealing with cancer that sets the body to fight the malignant process by itself. The technique began to attract close attention when more than 90 per cent of terminally ill patients were found to have entered remission.

The treatment involves taking white blood cells from the patient's blood, modifying them and returning them to the bloodstream. To be precise, the immune cells affected by the viral or malignant process are taken (T-killer cells).

These cells are then modified, and in this way reprogrammed to recognise and block the disease process. The reprogrammed cells are introduced into the bloodstream and begin to act naturally, without outside intervention.

For the time being the technique is used in clinical practice as experimental and is offered in cases where other forms of treatment have brought no result. The outcome is striking in its effectiveness: more than 90 per cent of cases showed complete remission, with no cancerous cells remaining.

Leading scientists internationally note that the technique gives grounds for optimism, but that this is only the beginning. According to the specialists, the main task today is to work out how to adapt this principle of treatment to other forms of cancer.

fields.title: A robot instead of a scalpel
fields.bodyHtml:
The fast-developing field of surgical robotics is changing the face of modern surgery before our eyes. Israel is one of the world leaders in this field, and that is no accident.
Of all the surgical robots ever developed, only a handful of devices have been certified to date. Three of them were developed by Israelis.

According to Alon Wolf, founder and director of the Biorobotics and Biomechanics Laboratory at the Technion, Israel's institute of technology, the idea of surgical robotics arose from the need to give immediate medical help to soldiers on the battlefield without putting the surgeon at risk: ideally the intervention would be carried out under remote control from a bunker. That concept has still not been fully realised, but it gave a powerful impetus to the development of medical technology in this direction and is being used successfully in ordinary civilian medicine.

«Israeli developments, like American ones, are built on a body of knowledge from the military field,» explains Ziv Tamir, the first distributor of the Da Vinci surgical system in Israel. «That is what fundamentally distinguishes them from surgical robotics projects in other countries, which grow out of academic research and are not always directed at specific practical needs.»

Meet the certified Israeli inventions

Mazor Robotics of Caesarea is one of the world leaders in pioneering work on robot-assisted neurosurgery and spinal surgery. Its first product, SpineAssist, received FDA certification back in 2004. The next-generation device developed from it, the Renaissance Guidance System, is now in use in nearly 100 medical centres in various countries. The robot is used to take biopsies, for reconstructive operations, for the surgical correction of scoliosis, for spinal fusion and for other procedures demanding the highest precision.

The Flex Robotic System from MedRobotics, based on Alon Wolf's «snake robot», can reach cavities of the body that the surgeon cannot see directly. This matters particularly in head and neck surgery.

MST (Medical Surgery Technologies) makes AutoLap, a video-guided system for positioning the laparoscope optimally, which helps the surgeon orient themselves and steadies their movements. The surgeon wears a wireless ring-shaped device on the index finger that communicates with the AutoLap system. Dedicated software captures and interprets the visual information coming from the laparoscope and manoeuvres in step with the surgeon's hand signals in real time. «We compare this system to an Xbox in clinical practice,» explains Moti Frimer, the company's director. «The system understands gestures. Where most robotic systems are controlled with joysticks or other devices, MST responds directly to the movement of the surgeon's hand.»

Now a look into the near future of medicine worldwide: four Israeli inventions, one of them going through certification and three still in development

Human Extensions has developed an ergonomic bionic surgical glove that improves the precision and smoothness of movement. The device is currently going through FDA certification in the United States and CE certification in the European Union. According to Tami Frenkel, the company's director, it can be fitted to a particular surgeon and a particular task. «This pioneering solution will for the first time allow surgeons to perceive the patient's anatomy directly, in the way it is understood during open surgery,» Frenkel stresses, «as though the surgeon's hands were inside the patient's body.»

Microbot Medical, founded in 2010, is developing two pioneering devices, ViRob and TipCAT. ViRob is an autonomous micro-robot, rather like a submarine, that allows the surgeon to send a video camera, a drug or a shunt into the narrowest and least accessible places in the body (blood vessels, organs of the digestive or respiratory system) and to carry out minimally invasive interventions under MRI or CT guidance. TipCAT is a flexible self-propelled endoscope for use in the colon, the blood vessels and the urinary tract. Safe, quick and gentle movement inside the structures of the body is achieved by inflating and deflating the «balloons» — the sections of the probe — one after another.

XACT Robotics is currently developing a robotic system for inserting and steering a needle precisely during minimally invasive procedures under CT guidance, such as a lung biopsy. Any departure from the planned path, however small, is detected immediately and corrected without the need to reinsert the needle or reposition the patient.

Original source: https://www.doktorisrael.ru

fields.title: Expert advice: how to get better without spending on expensive medicines
fields.bodyHtml:
Summer is over and the cold weather is already closing in fast. The arrival of autumn always brings a weakening of the immune system and, as a result, colds and flu. How can the illness be kept from taking hold without spending on expensive preparations? A group of medical experts has the answer: «Do not rush to take expensive antibiotics at the first stage of the illness.»

Taking antibiotics for a cold is a very common mistake among people in almost every country. Even where there is a viral infection, it is not advisable to take them at the initial stage. The only exception may be an advanced illness or complications.

Nor is it advisable to combine preparations with similar effects. One antipyretic, one nasal preparation and tablets for a sore throat are enough. It should be noted that a person with a cold needs plenty of vitamins. They need not come in the form of preparations, since we obtain most beneficial substances from fresh fruit and vegetables.

To avoid seasonal illness, doctors recommend giving time to preventing viral infections through vaccination, which removes the risk of falling ill and saves money on treatment.

fields.title: Life in Israel after the events of 7 October 2023
fields.bodyHtml:
Against the background of the recent events of 7 October 2023, when clashes took place on Israel's southern borders and in the Gaza Strip, life in the central regions of the country, Tel Aviv among them, continued at its usual pace.

Events in Gaza did not affect life in Tel Aviv, where the peaceful atmosphere was not disturbed by the tension in the south. City services, including educational institutions and commercial premises, operated as normal, and residents continued to enjoy the benefits of civilised life, including access to medical care of the highest quality.

The airlines connecting Israel with the world, Russia among them, confirmed that their schedules remained stable, maintaining a reliable connection between the countries.

We are following the situation closely in order to provide up-to-date information on the state of affairs in Israel, particularly as regards the provision of medical care. A detailed analysis of the situation and its possible consequences for healthcare and for patient safety is set out in our most recent publication.

Dr Cohen is an orthopaedic surgeon specialising in the treatment of conditions of the hip, knee, ankle, shoulder and elbow joints, and of fractures of the limbs. Professor Dan Grisaro is recognised in the international medical community as one of the leading experts in cancers of the female reproductive organs. In Israel he is a key figure in this specialisation and has left a marked imprint on the treatment of many women.

Professor David Luria is an outstanding cardiologist whose reputation in cardiology and electrophysiology is impeccable. His experience spans more than 35 years, which forms an important foundation for his deep professional knowledge and skill.

  • Fellowship at the Mayo Clinic: the Mayo Clinic is one of the finest medical centres in the world. Completing a three-year fellowship there gave Professor Luria the opportunity to work with, and learn, the most modern methods of diagnosis and treatment alongside the world's best specialists.
  • Treatment of atrial fibrillation and ventricular tachycardia by ablation: ablation is a minimally invasive procedure in which small areas of heart tissue producing abnormal electrical impulses are destroyed. The method helps patients avoid surgery and prevents the arrhythmia from returning.
  • Implantation of pacemakers and defibrillators, such as ICDs: an ICD (implantable cardioverter defibrillator) is a device that monitors the heart rhythm and, where necessary, restores it automatically by delivering an electrical impulse.
  • Closure of the left atrial appendage: this method is used to prevent blood clots forming in the left atrial appendage, which reduces the risk of stroke in patients with atrial fibrillation.
  • Transcatheter radiofrequency ablation with CARTO: an innovative technology that uses three-dimensional imaging to locate and destroy the areas of tissue causing the arrhythmia precisely.
  • Ventricular pacing for the treatment of heart failure: a technique that helps improve the work of the heart by correcting the electrical activity between the right and left ventricles.

Professor Luria is a master of all these techniques, and his skill and knowledge make him one of the leading cardiologists in the world. His approach to treating each patient is an individual one, which produces excellent results even in the most complex cases.

He is senior endocrinologist in the department for the treatment of endocrine disorders and diabetes at a children's hospital. He also gives consultations on childhood illnesses, including allergic and infectious diseases.

Dr Oren is known well beyond Israel for his professionalism and his attentive care for the health of young patients. He has some 15 years of experience. He favours a multidisciplinary approach and the combination of different treatment methods in the therapy of endocrine disorders.

Alongside his daily clinical practice, Asaf Oren is actively engaged in academic work. He is a well-known and much sought-after lecturer and has organised seminars in endocrinology for students at the medical university in Toronto. He currently lectures at the Sheinborn School of Nursing to students and to nurses taking advanced courses in neonatal intensive care in Tel Aviv. He also teaches paediatrics in the faculty of medicine at Tel Aviv University.

Together with colleagues, Dr Asaf Oren has published more than 20 research papers on paediatric endocrinology.

Summary: Dr David Sarid is a leading oncologist in Israel, a doctor of international standing and a specialist in chemotherapy and radiotherapy. He is an expert of world class who applies the most modern methods to the treatment of all forms of cancer and of metastatic disease.

Dr Sarid specialises in the diagnosis and treatment of a wide range of cancers: cancer of the breast, of the uterus and its appendages, of the prostate, of the digestive tract, of the lungs, of the kidney and bladder, and growths on the skin. His professional interests include chemotherapy, radiotherapy, biological cancer therapy, and the rehabilitation of patients after treatment. He has more than 30 years of clinical experience.

An excellent diagnostician, Dr Sarid combines many years of professional experience with the highest level of skill, which allows him to give effective help each year to thousands of patients from almost every country. His fluent Russian gives patients from the former Soviet states the added opportunity of closer contact, and of discussing every detail of the proposed treatment and its possible consequences.

David Sarid is also a much sought-after teacher, lecturing to students in the faculty of medicine at Tel Aviv University and to colleagues on continuing professional development courses. He has been awarded a prize for the best academic lecture.

Alongside his clinical and teaching work, Dr Sarid is actively engaged in research. He regularly presents the results of his clinical investigations at international oncology congresses and conferences. He is the author of 30 research publications in leading professional medical journals.

David Sarid is a recognised specialist who enjoys well-deserved respect among colleagues not only in Israel but far beyond it. His expert opinion is valued highly by oncologists internationally.

On completing it she was offered a post at the National Oncology Institute based at the Assuta medical centre.

Her next placement was in the geriatric oncology department of the European School of Oncology, followed by advanced courses in the postgraduate education department of the National Oncology Institute.

By that time she was already working as a senior physician in the oncology department at Assuta, where she continues to work today.

Dr Matceyevsky's research is published regularly in medical journals. Her best-known papers have described:

Dr Levin is known for his achievements in diagnosing and treating a wide range of complex and chronic blood disorders in newborns, children and adolescents. Dr German Gandelman is one of the most respected cardiologists in Israel, specialising in invasive cardiology. The term describes cardiac catheterisation, a procedure in which a range of surgical interventions on the heart are carried out by means of a narrow catheter passed through the blood vessels.

Using this technique Dr Gandelman is able to:

  • Widen narrowed coronary arteries;
  • Treat arrhythmias;
  • Implant artificial heart valves.

He also has deep expertise in diagnostic cardiac catheterisation, including coronary angiography, and in stenting.

Dr Gandelman also treats a range of conditions conservatively, such as the diabetic heart and heart failure. Patients from various countries can come to him for high-quality treatment using reliable Israeli medicines whose authenticity is guaranteed.

Every stenting and catheterisation procedure performed by Dr Gandelman meets the highest international standards. Thanks to his many years of experience in the field, every stage of the procedure has been honed to perfection. Russian viewers of the television programme «Zhit zdorovo!» had the opportunity to see Dr Gandelman's skill during this delicate operation.

Dr Gandelman is an active member of the Israel Medical Association and the Israel Heart Society.

Summary:

Professor Haim Gutman is an internationally known cancer surgeon and an exceptional specialist in the diagnosis and surgical treatment of melanoma, basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma of the skin, soft tissue sarcoma, and tumours of the digestive tract and breast. He has more than 40 years of clinical experience.

The professor's main area of specialisation is the treatment of melanoma, the most aggressive of all tumours known today. In Haim Gutman's view, accurate diagnosis is one of the most important factors in a patient's prompt recovery. He continually refines and develops his skill: he was among the first in the world to introduce sentinel lymph node biopsy. This procedure makes it possible to determine the extent of surgery reliably and to remove the growth while taking the least possible healthy tissue. To reduce the risk of recurrence the professor uses innovative methods, including neoadjuvant therapy with the newest drugs. The advanced technology of intra-operative isotope treatment helps the surgeon rule out side effects and complications as far as possible: a preparation is introduced into the patient's bloodstream and carried to the affected organ or tissue, where it irradiates the diseased area locally.

Professor Gutman is a proponent of organ-preserving surgery. In his practice he makes active use of minimally invasive laparoscopic and endoscopic methods, which reduce the patient's recovery time to a minimum. In difficult cases of breast cancer he resorts to partial or complete removal of the breast. Haim Gutman is also known as an excellent plastic surgeon who performs breast reconstruction after mastectomy with great skill. Preserving the appearance of the breast helps patients overcome psychological difficulties and return to a full life.

Professor Gutman graduated with distinction from the Sackler Faculty of Medicine at Tel Aviv University, becoming a certified specialist in surgery and basic sciences and, at the end of his training, in general and cancer surgery. He studied various surgical methods and cancer research at medical centres in the United States, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom. He currently heads a department of cancer surgery.

Professor Haim Gutman is actively engaged in cancer research. He lectures on courses in cancer surgery at various institutions, including universities in the United States. He has published more than 100 papers in the professional literature and is the co-author of numerous research works and publications in cancer surgery. Haim Gutman has received many awards and fellowships for his scientific achievements.

Summary:

Professor Moshe Papa is an excellent breast surgeon, a specialist with enormous experience and the highest professionalism in breast surgery. He carries considerable authority among colleagues far beyond Israel.

In his daily practice Moshe Papa successfully applies the newest technologies and techniques for diagnosing breast cancer at the earliest stage. He uses the Tomosynthesis three-dimensional mammography system, which allows breast tissue to be examined in 3D. He uses the highly advanced MarginProbe device, which allows the edges of a tumour to be removed with great precision and considerably reduces the risk of repeat operations. He also actively promotes and uses the new technique of gentle targeted radiotherapy, Intrabeam. The Intrabeam system delivers radiation only to the area where the cancer is located, without damaging healthy tissue.

Professor Papa has thousands of successful operations and saved patients from all corners of the world to his name. His priority is organ-preserving surgery for breast tumours, in the knowledge of how important preserving the breast is to every woman. Where the breast cannot be preserved, he carries out reconstruction during the operation, fitting an implant at the same time. He performs such operations with masterly skill, preserving the best possible cosmetic and aesthetic appearance of the breast, which spares the patient a second period of distress.

The development of new techniques and operations in breast medicine and oncology has brought Moshe Papa international renown. The professor has many publications and takes an active part in many international medical societies. He passes his many years of experience and skill on to colleagues, trains younger specialists and lectures to medical students.

He is a member of the editorial board of the well-known medical journal Surgical Oncology.

In his surgical practice Dr Dotan uses advanced transurethral techniques, through which patients are given a chance of full recovery. His unquestioned professionalism draws patients not only from Israel but from around the world.

Zohar Dotan takes an active part in research aimed at improving and introducing the newest minimally invasive technologies in the treatment of tumours of the prostate and kidneys. His gifts and his continuing achievements in uro-oncology have been recognised with many prestigious awards.

His academic contribution to medical science includes more than 50 publications in leading journals. Dr Dotan is also an active participant in both national and international scientific forums.

EDUCATION

  • Sackler School of Medicine, Tel Aviv University, Israel
  • Specialisation in genetics at Tel Aviv University, Israel
  • Internship at the Sheba medical centre, Ramat Gan, Israel
  • Fellowship in urology at the Kaplan clinic, Rehovot, Israel
  • Fellowship in uro-oncology and laparoscopic and endoscopic surgery at a memorial cancer centre in the United States

LANGUAGES

  • Hebrew
  • English

MEMBERSHIP OF INTERNATIONAL ASSOCIATIONS

  • Head of the Israel association of uro-oncologists
  • Israel Surgical Association
  • European Association for Endoscopic Surgery
  • European Society of Oncological Urology
  • American Society of Clinical Oncology
  • Society of Urologic Oncology, USA

fields.title: Cardiac ablation
fields.bodyHtml:
Introduction

Cardiac arrhythmias are serious disturbances of the heart rhythm that can affect quality of life and even lead to severe complications such as stroke or heart failure. Over recent decades medicine has taken significant steps in developing innovative treatments for arrhythmia. One such turning point has been cardiac ablation, an innovative procedure that opens a new era in the treatment of heart rhythm disorders.

Methods of diagnosis

Accurate diagnosis is the foundation of successful treatment for cardiac arrhythmia. Modern diagnostic methods allow doctors to determine the type and mechanism of the arrhythmia precisely, which helps in choosing the best approach to treatment. The main methods of diagnosing arrhythmia include:

  • Electrocardiography (ECG): one of the most widely used methods, recording the electrical activity of the heart and revealing abnormalities in its work.
  • Holter monitoring: continuous ECG recording over a long period (usually 24 to 48 hours) to detect infrequent arrhythmias that an ordinary ECG may miss.
  • Echocardiography: an ultrasound method that allows the structure and function of the heart to be examined and possible anatomical causes of arrhythmia to be identified.

Methods of treatment

Traditional treatment for arrhythmia may involve drugs such as antiarrhythmic agents, or the use of an implantable cardioverter defibrillator for severe arrhythmias. In recent years, however, cardiac ablation has become the preferred treatment for many arrhythmias.

  • Drug treatment: in milder forms of arrhythmia the doctor may prescribe medicines such as antiarrhythmic agents, beta blockers or other drugs to stabilise the heart rhythm and prevent arrhythmia.
  • Implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD): a device used to detect and stop life-threatening arrhythmias. An ICD can automatically return the heart to a normal rhythm or perform cardioversion, in which a controlled electrical discharge resets the arrhythmia.
  • Continuous patient monitoring: for patients with infrequent or symptomatic arrhythmias the doctor may decide to fit a continuous monitor, which records the heart rhythm over a long period and allows arrhythmias to be detected and analysed.
  • Catheter ablation: a minimally invasive procedure carried out with catheters passed through the blood vessels into the heart. By applying controlled heat (radiofrequency ablation) or cold (cryoablation) to the abnormal areas of heart tissue, the specialist destroys the sources of the arrhythmia and restores a normal heart rhythm.
  • Surgical treatment: in some cases, particularly where the arrhythmia is linked to structural abnormalities of the heart, surgery may be needed, such as major surgical ablation or the implantation of marker electrodes.
  • Pacemaker implantation: a pacemaker may be fitted to maintain an optimal heart rhythm in patients with arrhythmia or bradycardia.
  • Implantation of a cardioverter defibrillator (ICD): in cases of serious arrhythmia or a risk of cardiac arrest, the doctor may recommend an ICD to detect and stop life-threatening arrhythmias automatically.
  • Cardiac surgery: in some complex arrhythmias, particularly alongside other heart disease, surgery may be needed to eliminate the sources of the arrhythmia and restore normal electrical activity of the heart.

Every treatment for arrhythmia is chosen individually, depending on the type of arrhythmia, its severity, the patient's general condition and other factors. A combination of methods may be used to achieve the best results in treating arrhythmia and preventing complications.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • Israel is widely recognised as a medical centre of world class, and its cardiology departments are equipped with the latest technology. Treatment of arrhythmia, including cardiac ablation, in Israel has a number of advantages:
  • Highly qualified specialists: cardiologists and electrophysiologists at Israeli clinics have many years of experience and extensive training, which ensures that procedures are highly effective.
  • Use of advanced technology: medical institutions in Israel make active use of advanced technologies and treatment methods, which improves the results of cardiac ablation.
  • An integrated approach: Israeli clinics bring together various fields of medicine, which allows patients to receive comprehensive and individual care for arrhythmia.

Conclusion

Cardiac ablation is a revolutionary approach to treating heart rhythm disorders that can considerably improve patients' quality of life and reduce the risk of complications. Modern methods of diagnosis and treatment make the procedure safer and more effective. Israel is considered one of the leading countries in cardiology and cardiac ablation, which makes it an attractive place for the treatment of arrhythmia. If you have problems with your heart, do consult a cardiologist and ask about the possibility of ablation to restore a normal heart rhythm and improve your health.

fields.title: Pituitary adenoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Pituitary adenoma: advanced treatment in Israel

A pituitary adenoma is a benign tumour of the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland that can affect the production of hormones regulating important functions of the body. In Israel patients receive a comprehensive and individual approach to the diagnosis and treatment of pituitary adenoma, including modern methods of investigation and therapy.

Diagnosis of pituitary adenoma:

  1. Hormone tests
    Measuring hormone levels in the blood to identify disturbances linked to the work of the pituitary gland.
  2. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    The main imaging method for studying the adenoma in detail and assessing its size and shape and its effect on the surrounding tissue.
  3. Ophthalmological examination
    Assessment of the visual fields and other eye functions to determine the effect of the adenoma on the optic nerve.
  4. Angiography
    Examination of the blood vessels of the brain, which may be carried out to rule out other vascular conditions or in preparation for surgery to remove the adenoma.

Methods of treating pituitary adenoma in Israel:

  1. Drug treatment
    The use of medicines to reduce the size of the tumour and correct the hormonal balance.
  2. Surgery
    Transsphenoidal adenomectomy — minimally invasive removal of the adenoma through the nasal sinuses. This method is used most often because of its effectiveness and safety.
  3. Radiotherapy
    Including the Gamma Knife and proton therapy, used where surgery is not possible or the adenoma has not been completely removed.
  4. Targeted and hormonal therapy
    For the treatment of certain types of adenoma that actively produce hormones.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An individual approach
    The treatment plan is drawn up taking account of every aspect of the patient's health, including the size and type of the adenoma, its hormonal activity and the patient's general condition.
  • A multidisciplinary team
    Endocrinologists, neurosurgeons, ophthalmologists and radiologists work closely together to ensure a comprehensive approach to treatment.
  • Access to advanced technology
    The use of the most modern medical technologies and treatment methods, minimising risks and side effects.

Treatment of pituitary adenoma in Israel is aimed at removing the tumour or controlling its growth, restoring normal hormone levels and preserving the patient's quality of life.

fields.title: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
fields.bodyHtml:
Benign prostatic hyperplasia: modern treatment in Israel

Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), also known as an enlarged prostate, is a common condition among men over 50. Israel applies the latest advances in medicine to treat it effectively, improving patients' quality of life.

Diagnosis of benign prostatic hyperplasia:

  1. Physical examination,
    including a rectal examination of the prostate.
  2. PSA blood test
    (prostate-specific antigen) to assess the risk of prostate cancer.
  3. Ultrasound examination
    (transrectal ultrasound) of the prostate through the rectum to determine the size of the gland.
  4. Uroflowmetry
    — measurement of the rate and volume of urine passed, to assess the degree of obstruction of the urinary tract.
  5. Questionnaires, such as the IPSS symptom index, to assess the severity of symptoms.

Methods of treating benign prostatic hyperplasia in Israel:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Alpha blockers to relax the muscles of the bladder neck and prostate.
    • 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors to reduce the size of the prostate and lower the PSA level.
  2. Minimally invasive procedures:
    • Transurethral microwave thermotherapy (TUMT).
    • Transurethral needle ablation (TUNA).
  3. Surgical treatment:
    • Transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) — relief of obstruction of the urinary tract.
    • Laser enucleation of the prostate — a modern method with minimal blood loss and rapid recovery.
    • Adenomectomy (open prostatectomy) — used where the prostate is very large.
  4. New technologies:
    • Aquablation — the use of a high-pressure water jet to remove prostate tissue.
    • Prostatic urethral lift — a newer treatment aimed at reducing pressure within the prostate and improving urine flow.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • Highly qualified doctors: Israeli specialists have extensive experience and an international reputation in urology.
  • Innovative medical equipment: clinics are equipped with the latest technologies for diagnosing and treating BPH.
  • An individual approach: every patient is given a personal treatment plan that takes account of his circumstances and preferences.
  • Comfort and support: patients receive full support through diagnosis, treatment and recovery.

Treatment of benign prostatic hyperplasia in Israel allows men to regain comfort in daily life, reducing symptoms and preventing the possible complications of this condition.

fields.title: Adenomyosis
fields.bodyHtml:
Adenomyosis: advanced treatment in Israel

Adenomyosis is a gynaecological condition in which tissue resembling the endometrium (the lining of the uterus) begins to grow within the muscular wall of the uterus. It can cause severe pain and heavy periods. Modern methods of diagnosing and treating adenomyosis are available in Israel, allowing women to restore their quality of life.

Diagnosis of adenomyosis:

  1. Ultrasound examination:
    Transvaginal ultrasound is the main method of diagnosing adenomyosis, allowing the structure of the uterus and any abnormal areas within the muscular wall to be seen.
  2. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    Used to obtain more detailed images of the uterus, particularly in complex or unclear cases.
  3. Laboratory tests:
    Although there is no specific test for adenomyosis, tests may be directed at assessing general health and identifying associated conditions.

Methods of treating adenomyosis:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Hormonal therapy: the use of oral contraceptives or hormonal intrauterine systems to reduce menstrual bleeding and ease pain.
    • Antigonadotropins: drugs that suppress ovarian function and reduce the growth of endometrial-like tissue.
  2. Surgical treatment:
    • Conservative excision: removal of areas of adenomyosis while preserving the uterus, used where a woman wishes to retain her fertility.
    • Hysterectomy: removal of the uterus may be recommended in severe cases or where other treatments have not worked.
  3. Minimally invasive procedures:
    • Uterine artery embolisation: a procedure that blocks the blood supply to areas of adenomyosis, causing them to shrink.
  4. Physiotherapy and supportive treatment:
    • Programmes for managing pain and stress, physiotherapy exercises and relaxation techniques can help improve general health and reduce symptoms.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An individual approach: every patient receives a personal treatment plan based on her particular clinical picture.
  • Use of the newest technologies: access to advanced medical innovations and treatment methods.
  • A multidisciplinary team: gynaecologists, fertility specialists, endocrinologists and others work together to ensure a comprehensive approach to treatment.

Treatment of adenomyosis in Israel is aimed at minimising symptoms, preserving reproductive health and improving the quality of life of women affected by the condition.

fields.title: Obstetrics (childbirth)
fields.bodyHtml:
Obstetrics in Israel: advanced methods and technologies

Israel is known for its achievements in medicine, obstetrics among them. Innovative technologies and methods of managing pregnancy and childbirth are used here, which ensures a high level of safety and health for both mother and baby.

Diagnosis and management of pregnancy:

  1. Prenatal diagnosis:
    • Ultrasound examination:
      Regular scans at various stages of pregnancy to monitor the development of the baby.
    • Non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT):
      A blood test for the mother to detect genetic abnormalities in the baby at an early stage.
    • Amniocentesis and chorionic villus sampling:
      Carried out to obtain foetal cells for genetic analysis where there is a high risk of inherited disease.
  2. Specialist consultations:
    • Consultations with a geneticist, endocrinologist or cardiologist:
      In cases of high risk or where chronic conditions are present.
    • Psychological support and nutritional advice:
      To provide complete care for the mother's health.

Childbirth in Israel:

  1. Natural birth and birth with minimal intervention:
    • Professional support from a midwife and the option of natural methods of pain relief.
  2. Caesarean section:
    • Carried out for medical reasons or at the mother's request, using modern methods and equipment to minimise risk and speed recovery.
  3. Birth with analgesia:
    • Epidural analgesia: widely used to relieve pain during labour, allowing the mother to remain active and in control of the process.

Care after birth:

  • Neonatal screening: testing the newborn for metabolic, hormonal and genetic conditions.
  • Breastfeeding support: consultations with lactation specialists to help breastfeeding succeed.
  • Postnatal rehabilitation: recovery programmes for mothers after birth, including physiotherapy and psychological support.

Advantages of giving birth in Israel:

  • Highly qualified medical staff: obstetricians and gynaecologists in Israel have international experience and access to advanced research.
  • An individual approach: every pregnancy and birth is treated as unique, with an emphasis on the woman's individual needs and preferences.
  • Modern equipment: ensures accurate diagnosis and safety during birth.

The management of pregnancy and childbirth in Israel aims to provide the greatest possible comfort, safety and health for mother and baby alike, using the most modern medical practices and technologies.

fields.title: Coronary artery bypass grafting
fields.bodyHtml:
Introduction

Coronary artery disease is one of the most common cardiovascular conditions. It arises when the coronary arteries that supply blood to the heart muscle become narrowed or blocked. An inadequate blood supply can lead to stable angina or even to acute coronary syndrome. In this article we describe the methods of diagnosis and treatment and the advantages of coronary artery bypass grafting, particularly in the context of treatment in Israel.

Methods of diagnosis

Diagnosing coronary artery disease involves a range of methods that establish the extent of damage to the coronary arteries and allow the best treatment plan to be chosen. The main methods include:

  • Electrocardiography (ECG): a non-invasive method that records the electrical activity of the heart. An ECG can reveal abnormalities of heart rhythm and signs of ischaemia.
  • Stress testing: doctors carry out tests using physical exercise or pharmacological agents (dobutamine, for example) to assess the heart's response to stress and detect ischaemia.
  • Coronary angiography: an invasive method in which a contrast medium is introduced into the coronary arteries, allowing doctors to establish precisely where and how severely they are narrowed or blocked.

Methods of treatment

Treatment of coronary artery disease aims to restore a normal blood supply to the heart and prevent complications. One of the most effective treatments is coronary artery bypass grafting. The method involves the following stages:

  • Creating the grafts: during the operation the surgeon creates bypass routes, known as grafts, which go around the narrowed or blocked sections of the coronary arteries. The grafts may be made from the patient's own vessels (usually a vein from the leg) or from artificial materials.
  • Preparing for surgery: before the operation the patient undergoes thorough preparation, including assessment of general health and all necessary tests and diagnostic investigations.
  • The operation: during surgery the surgeons carry out the bypass grafting, creating the grafts and restoring a normal blood supply to the heart muscle.
  • Recovery: after the operation the patient goes through rehabilitation and a period of recovery, including monitoring of the heart rhythm, adjustment to a new way of life and advice on changes to diet and physical activity.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

Israel is a world leader in cardiac surgery and in the treatment of coronary artery disease. The advantages of coronary artery bypass grafting in Israel include:

  • Experience and expertise: cardiac surgeons at Israeli clinics have extensive experience and exceptional expertise, which ensures good surgical results.
  • Use of advanced technology: medical institutions in Israel are equipped with advanced technologies and innovative equipment for accurate diagnosis and successful surgery.
  • An individual approach: doctors in Israel take an individual approach to every patient, taking account of his or her particular circumstances and needs.

Conclusion

Coronary artery bypass grafting is an innovative and effective treatment for coronary artery disease that restores a normal blood supply to the heart muscle and prevents complications. Israel is considered one of the best countries for this operation, thanks to the experience of its surgeons, the use of advanced technology and the individual approach taken to every patient. If you have problems with your heart, do consult a cardiac surgeon and ask about the possibility of bypass grafting for the sake of your health and wellbeing.

fields.title: Arrhythmia
fields.bodyHtml:
Arrhythmia: advanced treatment in Israel

An arrhythmia is a disturbance of the rhythm of the heartbeat, which may show itself as a fast, slow or irregular heartbeat. In Israel, advanced medical technologies and methods are used to diagnose and treat arrhythmia, allowing patients to return to a normal rhythm of life.

Diagnosis of arrhythmia:

  1. Laboratory tests:
    Full blood count
  2. Electrocardiogram (ECG)
    The main method for determining the type of arrhythmia and its characteristics.
  3. Holter monitoring
    Continuous ECG monitoring over 24 hours or several days to detect episodic arrhythmias.
  4. Exercise testing (treadmill test)
    Helps assess the heart's response to physical exertion and reveal hidden rhythm disturbances.
  5. Electrophysiological study
    An invasive test that establishes precisely the mechanisms behind the arrhythmia and where in the heart it originates.

Methods of treating arrhythmia:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Antiarrhythmic drugs: used to restore and maintain a normal heart rhythm.
    • Anticoagulant therapy: drugs that prevent blood clots forming, particularly important in atrial fibrillation.
  2. Cardioversion:
    • Electrical cardioversion: a procedure in which brief electrical discharges help restore a normal heart rhythm.
  3. Catheter ablation:
    • A minimally invasive procedure in which radiofrequency or cryogenic energy destroys the abnormal areas of heart tissue responsible for the arrhythmia.
  4. Implantation of pacemakers and defibrillators:
    • Pacemakers: devices that regulate the heart rhythm in slow arrhythmias.
    • Implantable cardioverter defibrillators (ICDs): devices that monitor and correct potentially life-threatening arrhythmias.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An individual approach: every patient is given a personal plan of diagnosis and treatment based on their particular medical needs.
  • A multidisciplinary team: cardiologists, arrhythmia specialists and cardiac surgeons work together to achieve the best results.
  • Access to advanced technologies and treatments: the use of the latest research and innovative medical equipment.
  • A high standard of medical care: Israeli clinics are known for their high level of patient care and the effectiveness of their treatment.

Treatment of arrhythmia in Israel is aimed not only at relieving symptoms but at minimising health risks in the long term, helping patients lead an active and healthy life.

fields.title: Arthritis
fields.bodyHtml:
Arthritis: comprehensive treatment in Israel

Arthritis covers a group of conditions marked by inflammation in one or more joints, leading to pain, swelling, stiffness and reduced function. In Israel patients have access to advanced methods of diagnosing and treating arthritis, including rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, psoriatic arthritis and other forms of the disease.

Diagnosis of arthritis

  1. Clinical examination
    Includes assessment of symptoms, medical history and the physical state of the joints.
  2. Laboratory tests
    Blood tests for markers of inflammation (C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate), for antibodies characteristic of rheumatoid arthritis (rheumatoid factor, anti-CCP) and other specific tests.
  3. Imaging
    • X-rays: help establish the stage of the disease and the presence of deformity and erosion.
    • MRI and ultrasound: used for more detailed imaging of the soft tissues, the synovial membrane, the cartilage and early erosion.
    • Arthroscopy: a minimally invasive procedure to assess the inside of the joint and obtain tissue samples for histological examination.

Methods of treating arthritis in Israel

  1. Drug treatment
    • Disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs to slow the progression of the disease.
    • Biological agents and JAK inhibitors to control the inflammatory process in rheumatoid arthritis.
    • Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) to reduce pain and inflammation.
  2. Physiotherapy and rehabilitation
    Individual exercise programmes to maintain and improve joint function, reduce pain and prevent further damage.
  3. Diet and lifestyle
    Advice on nutrition and lifestyle changes aimed at reducing inflammation and improving general health.
  4. Surgical treatment
  5. Includes arthroscopic cleaning of the joint, synovectomy, osteotomy and joint replacement where damage is severe.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach
    A team of doctors including rheumatologists, orthopaedic surgeons and physiotherapists works together to draw up a comprehensive treatment plan.
  • Advanced treatments
    Access to the newest drug therapies and innovative surgical techniques.
  • An individual treatment plan
    Treatment is adapted to each patient's needs, taking account of symptoms, the stage of the disease and their way of life.
  • Comprehensive support and rehabilitation
    Extensive rehabilitation programmes help speed recovery and improve patients' quality of life.

Treatment of arthritis in Israel offers patients wide scope for controlling the disease effectively, reducing pain and inflammation, preventing further destruction of the joints and improving quality of life.

fields.title: Osteoarthritis
fields.bodyHtml:
Osteoarthritis: advanced treatment in Israel

Osteoarthritis is the most common form of arthritis, marked by the gradual thinning of the cartilage in the joints, which leads to pain, stiffness and reduced movement. Israel offers innovative approaches to its treatment, combining international experience, highly qualified specialists and the latest advances in medical science.

Diagnosis of osteoarthritis

  1. Clinical examination
    The doctor assesses the patient's symptoms and medical history and carries out a physical examination to identify painful joints and those with restricted movement.
  2. X-rays
    Allow the extent of joint damage to be assessed, along with the presence of erosion and bony outgrowths (osteophytes).
  3. MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)
    Used for a more detailed assessment of the cartilage, the joint capsule and the surrounding soft tissue.
  4. Laboratory tests
    Blood tests may be ordered to rule out other forms of arthritis, such as rheumatoid arthritis.

Methods of treating osteoarthritis in Israel

  1. Conservative treatment:
    • Drug therapy
      The use of NSAIDs, chondroprotective agents and corticosteroid injections to reduce pain and inflammation.
    • Physiotherapy
      Individual exercise programmes to strengthen the muscles and improve joint movement.
    • Orthopaedic aids
      The use of braces, orthoses and specialist footwear to reduce the load on the affected joints.
  2. Minimally invasive procedures:
    • Intra-articular injections of hyaluronic acid
      Improve lubrication of the joint and its mobility.
    • Arthroscopy
      Minimally invasive surgery to remove damaged cartilage and osteophytes.
  3. Surgical treatment:
    • Joint replacement
      Replacement of the affected joint with an artificial implant, recommended in severe osteoarthritis.
    • Osteotomy
      Surgical realignment of the limb to redistribute the load on the joint.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • Advanced medical technology
    The use of the most modern methods of diagnosis and treatment.
  • Experienced specialists
    Leading orthopaedic surgeons and rehabilitation specialists of international standing.
  • An individual approach
    Every patient is offered treatment adapted as closely as possible to their needs and way of life.
  • Comprehensive rehabilitation
    Integrated rehabilitation programmes help achieve the best possible recovery of joint function after treatment.

Treatment of osteoarthritis in Israel gives patients the chance of considerable relief from symptoms, an improved quality of life and a return to an active life.

fields.title: Astrocytoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Astrocytoma: advanced treatment in Israel

Astrocytoma is a type of glioma — a tumour arising from the glial cells of the brain. These tumours vary in how malignant they are, from slow-growing to highly aggressive forms.
