Hypospadias is usually diagnosed when a newborn boy is examined by a doctor. Although some forms are apparent immediately after birth, doctors often need further investigation to establish the exact position of the urethral opening and the degree of the abnormality. The main diagnostic methods are:

  • Visual examination: the doctor examines the urinary and reproductive organs to establish where the urethral opening lies on the penis.
  • Ultrasound examination: may be carried out for a more detailed study of the anatomy of the urinary tract and to assess the degree of hypospadias.
  • Urethrography: an X-ray method used to image the urethra and determine the exact position of the opening.
  • Consultation with a geneticist: in some cases hypospadias may be linked to genetic abnormalities, so a genetic consultation may be needed.

Methods of treatment

Hypospadias is usually treated surgically. The aim of the operation is to correct the position of the urethral opening and restore the normal anatomy of the penis. The particular approach depends on the degree of hypospadias and the patient's age. The main treatments are:

  • Corrective surgery: carried out to move the urethral opening to its correct position on the head of the penis.
  • Reconstructive surgery: in complex forms of hypospadias, or where there are additional abnormalities of the urinary tract, reconstructive surgery may be needed to restore normal anatomy.
  • Treatment in adults: in some men hypospadias remains uncorrected from childhood. Surgical correction can then be carried out in adulthood to improve function and appearance.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

Israel is a world leader in medical tourism, attracting patients from around the world with its high standard of medical services and advanced technology. Patients who choose Israel for the treatment of hypospadias gain the following advantages:

  • Experienced specialists: Israeli surgeons who specialise in hypospadias have extensive experience and professionalism. They trained at leading medical institutions and have high expertise in this field.
  • Innovative treatments: medical centres in Israel use advanced methods of diagnosing and treating hypospadias. This allows the best results to be achieved and minimises the risk of complications.
  • An individual approach: Israeli doctors understand how important it is to treat every patient individually. They take account of the particular features of each case and draw up the most effective and safest treatment plan.
  • Comprehensive support: patients who come to Israel for treatment receive full support at every stage of the trip. Coordinators help with travel arrangements and interpreting and provide the information needed.

Conclusion

Hypospadias is a serious congenital condition that can be corrected successfully by surgery. The operation improves quality of life and restores normal function. Thanks to its medical expertise and advanced technology, Israel offers patients the best conditions for successful treatment. If you or your child has been diagnosed with hypospadias, you should consult a qualified specialist and consider treatment in Israel to achieve the best results.

fields.title: Glaucoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Glaucoma is a group of eye conditions marked by damage to the optic nerve, often associated with raised pressure inside the eye. It is a progressive condition that can lead to loss of sight and even blindness if left untreated.

Diagnosis of glaucoma

  1. Ophthalmoscopy: allows the doctor, using special instruments, to assess the state of the optic nerve, the vessels of the fundus and the retina.
  2. Gonioscopy: a method in which the doctor uses a thick contact lens with mirrors to examine the structure of the angle of the anterior chamber of the eye, through which fluid drains. This establishes the cause of any problem with the eye's drainage system.
  3. Visual field test: carried out with a computerised perimeter to check peripheral vision.
  4. Optical tomography: allows the extent of damage to the optic nerve and the tissues of the eye to be assessed.
  5. Laser scanning: produces a layer-by-layer image of the eye.
  6. Ultrasound examination of the eye: doctors use this to assess the optic nerve, the posterior chamber and the retina.
  7. Doppler examination of the vessels of the eye: often used together with ultrasound to assess the blood supply to the eye.

Methods of treating glaucoma

  1. Drug therapy: used at an early stage of the condition. It includes eye drops to lower the pressure inside the eye, stimulation of the blood supply to the optic nerve and the inner coats of the eye, and restoration of metabolic processes in the tissues of the eye. The newer medicines used in Israeli clinics are highly effective with minimal side effects.
  2. Laser treatment:
    • Laser trabeculoplasty: creating microscopic openings in the drainage system of the eye to improve the outflow of fluid.
    • Laser iridotomy: creating a small opening in the iris to improve the circulation of fluid in closed-angle glaucoma.
    • Cyclophotocoagulation: laser treatment to reduce the production of fluid inside the eye.
  3. Surgical treatment:
    • Trabeculectomy: creating a new channel for fluid to drain, which lowers the pressure inside the eye.
    • Drainage implants: fitting small tubes to improve the outflow of fluid.
    • Minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS): newer technologies, such as micro-shunts, that make treatment less traumatic.
  4. Iridectomy: removal of part of the iris to improve the outflow of fluid in closed-angle glaucoma.
  5. Cyclophotocoagulation: a laser procedure to reduce the production of fluid inside the eye.

Advantages of treating glaucoma in Israel

  1. Highly qualified specialists: Israeli ophthalmologists have great experience and are recognised worldwide for their work in treating glaucoma.
  2. Modern equipment: clinics are equipped with the newest diagnostic and treatment devices, which ensures accuracy and effectiveness.
  3. An individual approach: every patient is given a personalised treatment plan that takes account of all aspects of their health.
  4. Interdisciplinary collaboration: doctors of various specialities work closely together to achieve the best treatment results.
  5. High standards of safety and quality: Israeli clinics adhere strictly to international protocols and standards of medical care.

Treatment of glaucoma in Israel gives patients access to highly qualified medical care, improves their quality of life and helps preserve their sight for many years.

fields.title: Glioblastoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Glioblastoma: advanced treatment in Israel

Glioblastoma is one of the most aggressive and common forms of primary brain tumour in adults. It grows quickly and tends to recur, which makes it particularly difficult to treat. In Israel, patients with glioblastoma have access to advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment aimed at extending life and improving its quality.

Diagnosis of glioblastoma

  1. MRI of the brain
    The key method in diagnosing glioblastoma, establishing the position and size of the tumour.
  2. Biopsy
    A biopsy or surgical removal of the tumour for histological analysis, which allows the type of tumour to be determined precisely.
  3. Laboratory tests
    Include blood tests for particular markers and general tests to assess the patient's overall health. These can help detect inflammation and assess kidney and liver function, which matters in planning treatment.
  4. Genetic testing
    Analysis of the tumour's DNA to identify particular mutations that may affect the choice of treatment.

Treatment of glioblastoma

  1. Surgery
    The aim of the operation is to remove as much of the tumour as possible with minimal risk to critical brain functions.
  2. Radiotherapy: used after surgery to destroy remaining cancer cells, often in combination with chemotherapy.
  3. Chemotherapy
    Temozolomide is the standard drug for treating glioblastoma during and after radiotherapy.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    Newer treatments directed at specific molecular targets in the tumour or at activating the immune system against the cancer cells.
  5. Tumour treating fields
    An innovative technology that uses electrical fields to suppress the growth of cancer cells.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach
    Leading specialists in neurosurgery, oncology and radiotherapy work together to develop an individual treatment plan.
  • Advanced treatments
    Patients have access to the latest advances in treating glioblastoma, including the newest drugs and technologies.
  • Individual treatment
    Treatment programmes are developed with the genetic features of the tumour and the patient's general health in mind.
  • Comprehensive support
    Psychological, social and rehabilitation support is provided for patients and their families at every stage of treatment.

Treatment of glioblastoma in Israel combines the high expertise of its medical specialists, access to innovative therapies and close attention to each patient's needs, which helps achieve the best possible results against this difficult disease.

fields.title: Optic chiasm glioma: diagnosis and treatment in Israel
fields.bodyHtml:
An optic chiasm glioma is a tumour that develops in the area of the optic chiasm, where the optic nerves cross. It occurs most often in children and adolescents and can considerably affect sight, leading to its gradual deterioration.

Diagnosis of optic chiasm glioma

  1. Detailed review of the medical history:
    • The doctor gathers information about symptoms such as deteriorating sight, headaches and changes in the visual fields, and reviews the family history.
  2. Visual examination and eye tests:
    • Assessment of visual acuity, visual fields and other visual functions to identify abnormalities.
  3. Ophthalmoscopy:
    • Examination of the fundus to identify changes associated with the tumour.
  4. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    • The main diagnostic method, producing detailed images of the structure of the brain and the visual pathways.
  5. Computed tomography (CT):
    • Used for detailed study of the bony structures and where MRI cannot be used.
  6. Optical coherence tomography (OCT):
    • An examination to assess the state of the optic nerve and retina.
  7. Electrophysiological tests:
    • Include visual evoked potentials and electroretinography to assess the function of the visual pathways and the retina.

Treatment of optic chiasm glioma

  1. Drug therapy:
    • Corticosteroids: used to reduce swelling and inflammation around the tumour.
    • Cytotoxic drugs: used in chemotherapy to shrink the tumour and suppress its growth.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • Conventional radiotherapy: aimed at destroying cancer cells with minimal effect on healthy tissue.
    • Proton therapy: a more precise method that minimises damage to the surrounding healthy tissue.
  3. Surgery:
    • Resection of the tumour: carried out where the tumour can be reached and surgery does not present a significant risk to the patient's health.
    • Shunting: where the tumour causes hydrocephalus (a build-up of fluid in the brain), a shunt may be needed to drain the excess fluid.
  4. Hormone therapy:
    • Used where the tumour affects the function of the pituitary gland and causes hormonal disturbance.
  5. Supportive treatment:
    • Includes treatment of symptoms such as pain and nausea, and support for the patient's mental health.

Advantages of treating optic chiasm glioma in Israel

  1. A high level of professionalism:
    • Israeli doctors have deep knowledge and many years of experience in treating gliomas and other brain tumours.
  2. Modern equipment:
    • Clinics are equipped with advanced diagnostic and treatment devices, which allows highly accurate investigation and effective treatment.
  3. An individual approach:
    • Every patient is given an individual treatment plan that takes account of the nature of the condition and their general health.
  4. Innovative treatments:
    • The use of the most modern methods and medicines, including proton therapy and the newest cytotoxic drugs.
  5. Comprehensive support:
    • Covers not only treatment of the underlying condition but also support for the patient's mental and physical wellbeing during treatment and recovery.

Treatment of optic chiasm glioma in Israel gives patients access to high-quality medical care and considerably improves their quality of life.

fields.title: Optic nerve glioma
fields.bodyHtml:
Optic nerve glioma: advanced treatment in Israel

An optic nerve glioma is a rare tumour arising from the cells surrounding the optic nerve, which connects the eye to the brain. This kind of tumour can affect sight. Depending on how far it has spread, it calls for an individual approach to treatment. In Israel, patients with optic nerve glioma are offered modern methods of diagnosis and treatment aimed at preserving sight and controlling the growth of the tumour.

Diagnosis of optic nerve glioma

  1. MRI of the brain
    The main diagnostic method. It allows the tumour to be seen and its size and effect on the surrounding tissue assessed.
  2. Ophthalmological examination
    Includes testing of sight, examination of the fundus and assessment of the visual fields to determine the tumour's effect on vision.
  3. Biopsy
    In some cases a tissue sample may be needed to determine the type of cells precisely and how aggressive the tumour is.
  4. Genetic testing
    May be recommended to identify genetic mutations associated with the tumour.

Treatment of optic nerve glioma

  1. Observation
    Where the tumour is slow-growing, causes no symptoms and does not threaten sight, active observation with regular MRI scans and eye examinations may be recommended.
  2. Surgery
    An operation is considered to reduce the size of the tumour or relieve pressure on the optic nerve, where this is safe and appropriate.
  3. Radiotherapy
    Used to control the growth of the tumour, particularly where it cannot be removed surgically. Israel uses precise methods of radiotherapy that minimise the effect on healthy tissue.
  4. Chemotherapy
    May be prescribed to shrink the tumour, particularly in children, to avoid the side effects of radiotherapy.
  5. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    Being studied as potential treatments for particular genetic subtypes of optic nerve glioma.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach
    A team of oncologists, neurosurgeons, radiologists and ophthalmologists works together to develop an individual treatment plan.
  • Advanced technology
    The use of the newest methods of diagnosis and treatment, including precision radiotherapy and minimally invasive surgical techniques.
  • A patient-centred approach
    A focus on preserving the patient's quality of life as fully as possible, including protecting sight and minimising long-term side effects.
  • Individual treatment programmes
    Treatment is designed around the particular features of each case.

Treatment of optic nerve glioma in Israel offers a comprehensive approach that combines a high level of medical expertise with access to advanced treatments, giving patients the best chance of a good outcome and of keeping their sight.

fields.title: Hiatus hernia
fields.bodyHtml:
Introduction

A hiatus hernia is a condition in which part of the upper stomach moves through the diaphragm into the chest cavity. It can cause unpleasant symptoms such as heartburn, chest pain and difficulty swallowing. Diagnosing and treating a hiatus hernia calls for specialist care. In this article we look at modern methods of diagnosis and treatment and the advantages of treatment in Israel.

Methods of diagnosis

Diagnosing a hiatus hernia can be difficult, as the symptoms may resemble those of other conditions of the digestive tract. The following methods may be used to reach an accurate diagnosis:

  • Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy: an endoscopic examination that allows the doctor to see the oesophagus and the upper part of the stomach directly and identify the hernia.
  • Barium X-ray: the patient swallows a substance that makes the organs visible on X-ray, which allows the hernia to be identified and its nature assessed.
  • Oesophageal manometry: a test that measures pressure in the oesophagus and identifies problems with its function.

Methods of treatment

Treatment depends on the size of the hernia and the symptoms the patient has. The main treatments include:

  • Lifestyle changes: moderate physical activity, reducing intake of spicy, fatty and acidic foods, and avoiding meals before bed can help ease symptoms.
  • Medicines: acid-suppressing drugs can help control heartburn and reduce the acidity of the stomach contents.
  • Surgery: in some cases, where conservative measures are ineffective, surgery may be needed to restore the organs to their normal position.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

Israel is a medical centre of world class providing high-quality medical care. The advantages of treating a hiatus hernia in Israel include:

  • Experienced specialists: medical institutions in Israel work with experienced surgeons and gastroenterologists who specialise in this condition.
  • Modern methods: doctors in Israel use advanced methods of diagnosis and surgery, which helps achieve the best results.
  • An individual approach: treatment in Israel is adapted to each patient's particular circumstances, which produces the best outcome.

Conclusion

A hiatus hernia is a condition that calls for careful diagnosis and effective treatment. Modern diagnostic methods, changes in lifestyle and surgery can help patients cope with the symptoms and improve their quality of life. In Israel patients can receive high-quality, individual treatment thanks to experienced specialists and advanced medical technology.

Managing a hiatus hernia effectively allows patients to return to ordinary life without pain and discomfort. By consulting experienced doctors and using advanced treatments, patients can regain their health and comfort in daily life.

fields.title: Erectile dysfunction
fields.bodyHtml:
Erectile dysfunction: understanding, diagnosis, treatment and the advantages of treatment in Israel

Introduction

Erectile dysfunction, also known as impotence, is a common medical condition in men in which it is difficult to achieve or maintain an erection sufficient for intercourse. It can seriously affect quality of life and relationships between partners. In this article we look at the methods of diagnosing and treating erectile dysfunction and the advantages of having it treated in Israel.

Methods of diagnosis

Diagnosis begins with a detailed discussion with the doctor about the patient's symptoms and medical history. The doctor's main task is to establish the possible causes and draw up the best treatment plan. The main diagnostic methods are:

  • Medical history and physical examination: the doctor interviews the patient to identify risk factors and possible causes, and carries out a physical examination to detect any abnormalities.
  • Hormone testing: erectile dysfunction may be linked to a hormonal imbalance. Measuring testosterone and other hormones can help establish the cause.
  • Testing for diabetes: diabetes may be one of the causes, so blood glucose may be measured.
  • Ultrasound examination: may be carried out to assess the blood supply to the genital organs.

Methods of treatment

Treatment may involve several approaches, and the choice depends on the cause and severity of the condition. The main treatments are:

  • Lifestyle changes: in some cases erectile dysfunction is linked to the way a person lives. The doctor may recommend changes to diet, more physical activity and reducing stress.
  • Medicines to improve erections: drugs such as sildenafil (Viagra), tadalafil (Cialis) and vardenafil (Levitra) may be prescribed to improve blood flow to the genital organs and help achieve an erection.
  • Injections or medicines administered into the urethra: the doctor may recommend injections into the penis or medicines placed in the urethra to improve erections.
  • Penile prosthesis: where other treatments are ineffective, surgical fitting of a penile prosthesis may be needed.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

Israel is one of the leading countries in the treatment of erectile dysfunction, offering patients high-quality medical services and advanced technology. Treatment in Israel offers the following advantages:

  • Experienced specialists: medical centres in Israel work with highly qualified doctors and surgeons who specialise in this field and have extensive experience and knowledge.
  • An individual approach: doctors in Israel understand how important it is to treat every patient individually. They take account of the medical history and the patient's particular circumstances and needs in drawing up the best treatment plan.
  • Innovative treatments: medical centres in Israel use advanced treatments, including innovative medicines and surgical techniques.
  • Confidentiality and comfort: patients who come to Israel for treatment can count on a high level of confidentiality and comfort during their stay.

Conclusion

Erectile dysfunction is a common medical condition that can be treated successfully by various means, including lifestyle changes, medication and surgery. Treatment in Israel offers patients a wide choice of options and a high level of medical expertise. If you have problems with erections, it is important to consult a qualified specialist for professional help and to determine the best treatment plan for a full and satisfying sexual life.

fields.title: Patient-specific joint planning
fields.bodyHtml:
Patient-specific joint planning: an innovative approach in Israeli orthopaedics

Patient-specific joint planning is an advanced approach in orthopaedics based on the use of personalised implants and technologies to achieve the most precise and effective joint replacement possible. In Israel this method is beginning to play a key part in the surgical treatment of joint disease and injury, allowing patients to restore joint function and quality of life to a new standard.

How the method works

Patient-specific joint planning involves creating unique implants and surgical instruments fully adapted to the anatomy of each individual patient. This is achieved through careful prior analysis of MRI and CT images of the joint, on the basis of which specialised software creates a precise three-dimensional model of the future implant and a plan for the operation.

Advantages of patient-specific joint planning

  • High precision and fit
    Implants are created individually for every patient. They fit perfectly and match the anatomical structures of the joint as closely as possible.
  • Shorter operations and recovery
    The precision of preparation and planning shortens the operation and speeds recovery afterwards.
  • Minimised risk of complications
    Individual planning reduces the likelihood of implant rejection and of infection and other complications after surgery.
  • Better functional results
    Patients report a greater degree of restored joint function and greater satisfaction with the results of surgery.

Where the method is used

Patient-specific joint planning is used successfully in the replacement of various joints, including the knee, hip and ankle. The approach is particularly valuable in complex cases where standard implants cannot provide the necessary precision and function.

Leading clinics and specialists

Many leading clinics in Israel have already introduced patient-specific joint planning into their practice. Israel has highly qualified specialists and modern equipment for this. Every patient can count on a detailed consultation and a comprehensive approach to treatment.

Patient-specific joint planning in Israel opens new prospects. Patients with joint disease and injury are offered a higher standard of personalised medical care and a better chance of recovery.

fields.title: Myocardial infarction
fields.bodyHtml:
Myocardial infarction: advanced treatment in Israel

A myocardial infarction, or heart attack, is an acute condition caused by a disruption of the blood supply to the heart muscle, which damages the heart tissue. Israeli medical centres offer a comprehensive approach to the treatment and rehabilitation of patients after a heart attack, using the most modern technologies and techniques.

Diagnosis of myocardial infarction:

  1. Electrocardiogram (ECG): the main tool for diagnosing a heart attack quickly.
  2. Laboratory tests: measurement of cardiac markers (troponins, CK-MB) in the blood, which indicate damage to the heart muscle.
  3. Echocardiography: ultrasound examination to assess the function of the heart and detect areas where the walls move less well.
  4. Coronary angiography: an invasive investigation that allows the coronary arteries to be seen and areas of narrowing or blockage identified.

Methods of treating myocardial infarction:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Anticoagulants and antiplatelet agents to prevent blood clots forming.
    • Beta blockers, ACE inhibitors and statins to reduce the load on the heart, improve its function and lower the risk of a further heart attack.
  2. Interventional treatment:
    • Stenting: a catheter with a balloon at its tip is passed into the vessel and guided to the narrowed section. The balloon is inflated to widen the narrowing, after which a stent — a metal mesh — is placed in the vessel to hold the artery open and maintain normal blood flow.
    • Coronary artery bypass grafting: an operation that creates a bypass route for blood to reach the part of the heart receiving too little because the coronary arteries are blocked. The patient's own vein or artery is used to create a graft that bypasses the blocked section.
  3. Rehabilitation:
    • Covers a range of measures, from exercise and changes to diet through to psychological support. These programmes aim to aid recovery after a heart attack, improve general health and prevent further cardiovascular disease.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An individual approach: every treatment plan is drawn up with the patient's personal needs and state of health in mind.
  • An interdisciplinary team: cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, rehabilitation specialists and others take part in treatment.
  • Access to innovative treatments: patients have access to the most modern stenting and bypass technologies, including biocompatible stents and minimally invasive surgical techniques.
  • A high standard of post-operative care and rehabilitation: particular attention is given to recovery after treatment, which helps patients return to normal life quickly.

Treatment of myocardial infarction in Israel combines effectiveness and safety with a focus on restoring heart function as fully as possible and improving patients' quality of life.

fields.title: Stroke (ischaemic and haemorrhagic)
fields.bodyHtml:
Ischaemic stroke: advanced treatment in Israel

Diagnosis of ischaemic stroke:

  • Medical examination and history taking.
  • Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain.
  • Echocardiography to assess the work of the heart and identify possible sources of clots.
  • Doppler examination of the vessels of the neck and brain.
  • Laboratory blood tests.

Treatment of ischaemic stroke:

  • Thrombolytic therapy to dissolve the clot that blocked the vessel.
  • Anticoagulant and antiplatelet therapy to prevent new clots.
  • In rare cases stenting of the vessels of the brain may be recommended to restore blood flow.
  • Early rehabilitation, including physiotherapy and speech and language therapy.

Haemorrhagic stroke: an integrated approach to treatment in Israel

Diagnosis of haemorrhagic stroke:

  • Medical examination and history.
  • Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to identify the bleeding.
  • Echocardiography to assess the risk of cardioembolic bleeding.
  • Angiography to assess the vessels of the brain and find the source of the bleeding.
  • Laboratory tests, including clotting studies.

Treatment of haemorrhagic stroke:

  • Control of blood pressure to minimise the risk of further bleeding.
  • Surgery to deal with the source of the bleeding, for example removal of a haematoma or reinforcement of a vessel wall.
  • Neurosurgical operations where urgent intervention is needed to reduce pressure inside the skull.
  • Rehabilitation aimed at restoring lost function and adjusting to changes in daily life after a stroke.

Treatment and rehabilitation after a stroke in Israel involve individual programmes based on the latest research and clinical experience, which gives patients the best possible recovery and a return to an active life.

fields.title: Coronary artery disease
fields.bodyHtml:
Introduction

Coronary artery disease is a chronic condition that develops when the heart muscle does not receive enough blood. It arises from the build-up of atherosclerotic plaques that narrow the blood vessels and limit the flow of oxygen to the heart. This leads to chest pain (angina) and can progress to a heart attack. It is important to diagnose and treat coronary artery disease in good time in order to prevent serious complications. In this article we describe the methods of diagnosis and treatment and the advantages of treatment in Israel.

Methods of diagnosis

Diagnosis plays a decisive part in establishing the extent of damage to the heart and planning treatment. Modern diagnostic methods include:

  • Electrocardiography (ECG): a simple and quick method that records the electrical activity of the heart. In coronary artery disease an ECG may show abnormalities of rhythm or changes associated with ischaemia.
  • Stress testing: carried out during physical exertion to assess the heart's response to exercise and identify problems with the blood supply.
  • Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI): produces detailed images of the heart and allows its structure and function to be assessed.
  • Coronary angiography: an invasive method in which a contrast medium is introduced into the blood vessels to image the coronary arteries and assess their condition.

Methods of treatment

Treatment aims to improve the blood supply to the heart and prevent the disease progressing. It may include:

  • Drug therapy: medicines such as antiplatelet agents, beta blockers and nitrates are used to control symptoms and reduce the risk of complications.
  • Percutaneous coronary intervention: catheters are used to widen the narrowed arteries and place stents to restore normal blood flow.
  • Surgery: in some cases coronary artery bypass grafting may be needed, in which grafts are placed to bypass the narrowed sections of the arteries.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

Israel is a world leader in cardiology and cardiovascular surgery and offers advanced treatment for coronary artery disease. The advantages include:

  • Qualified specialists: Israeli cardiologists and surgeons are highly qualified and have extensive experience in treating coronary artery disease.
  • Use of advanced technology: medical institutions in Israel are equipped with modern technology, which ensures a high level of professionalism and good treatment results.
  • An integrated approach to treatment: Israel takes a whole-person approach to coronary artery disease, which allows patients to receive comprehensive and individual care.

Conclusion

Coronary artery disease is a serious condition that requires comprehensive treatment and follow-up by experienced specialists. Modern methods of diagnosis and advanced approaches to treatment make Israel an attractive place to deal with it. If you have symptoms of coronary artery disease, consult a doctor for timely diagnosis and effective treatment to protect the health of your heart and improve your quality of life.

fields.title: Pacemakers and coronary angiography
fields.bodyHtml:
Introduction

Pacemakers and coronary angiography are two modern and effective methods of diagnosing and treating heart disease. Pacemakers are used to regulate the heart rhythm, while coronary angiography allows the state of the heart's blood vessels to be assessed and any narrowing or blockage identified. In this article we describe the methods of diagnosis and treatment and the advantages of using pacemakers and coronary angiography in Israel.

Methods of diagnosis

  • Pacemakers: electronic devices fitted under the skin of the chest. They monitor the heart rhythm, correct arrhythmias and prevent the heart stopping.
  • Coronary angiography: an invasive procedure in which a contrast medium is introduced into the blood vessels of the heart so that the coronary arteries can be seen on X-ray images. This establishes whether there is narrowing or blockage, and how severe it is, which could lead to a heart attack.

Methods of treatment

  • Pacemakers: used to treat various types of arrhythmia and heart block. They may be fitted temporarily or permanently, depending on the patient's condition.
  • Coronary angiography: where narrowing or blockage is found in the coronary arteries, further procedures can be carried out to treat them. These may include stenting (placing a stent to widen the vessel) or coronary artery bypass grafting (fitting an arterial or venous graft).

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • Qualified specialists: medical institutions in Israel have experienced and highly qualified cardiologists and surgeons who specialise in pacemakers and coronary angiography.
  • Use of advanced technology: doctors in Israel use advanced medical equipment and technology to diagnose and treat heart disease, which ensures a high level of accuracy and good results.
  • An integrated approach to treatment: Israel takes a whole-person approach to heart disease, which allows patients to receive individual and comprehensive treatment.

Conclusion

Pacemakers and coronary angiography are important innovative methods of diagnosing and treating heart disease. In Israel, highly qualified specialists and advanced technology make these procedures more effective and safer. If you have problems with your heart, consult a qualified cardiologist in Israel for the best treatment and to restore the health of your heart.

fields.title: Cataract
fields.bodyHtml:
A cataract is a clouding of the lens of the eye that leads to deteriorating vision. It is one of the most common eye conditions in people over 60, although it can also occur in younger people following injury or other illness.

Diagnosis of cataract

  1. Visual examination: the doctor examines the eyes using a slit lamp to assess the state of the lens and identify any clouding.
  2. Tonometry: measurement of the pressure inside the eye to rule out glaucoma, which can accompany a cataract.
  3. Visual acuity tests: used to establish the degree of sight loss and how the cataract affects the patient's daily life.
  4. Ultrasound scanning: carried out to obtain an accurate image of the structures of the eye and assess the state of the lens.
  5. Optical coherence tomography (OCT): produces high-quality images of the retina and optic nerve in order to rule out associated conditions.
  6. Keratometry and biometry: measurement of the curvature of the cornea and the length of the eye for accurate selection of the intraocular lens.

Methods of treating cataract

  1. Phacoemulsification:
    • The most widely used surgical treatment for cataract. The surgeon uses ultrasound energy to break up the clouded lens, which is then removed through a small incision. An artificial intraocular lens is then fitted.
    • Advantages: minimal injury to the tissues of the eye, rapid recovery, minimal risk of complications.
  2. Laser cataract surgery:
    • The use of a femtosecond laser to make precise incisions and break up the lens. This method improves the accuracy and safety of the operation.
    • Advantages: high precision, minimal risk of complications, shorter operating time.
  3. Extracapsular cataract extraction (ECCE):
    • A method in which the clouded lens is removed while the capsular bag is left in place for the intraocular lens. Usually used in advanced cataracts.
    • Advantages: allows the removal of large cataracts and stable placement of the lens.
  4. Intracapsular cataract extraction (ICCE):
    • A method in which the whole lens is removed together with the capsular bag. Rarely used, usually in complicated cataracts.
    • Advantages: allows treatment of difficult cases where other methods are unsuitable.

Advantages of cataract treatment in Israel

  1. Highly qualified specialists: Israeli ophthalmologists have great experience and are recognised worldwide for their work in treating cataracts.
  2. Modern equipment: clinics are equipped with the newest diagnostic and surgical devices, which ensures accuracy and effectiveness.
  3. An individual approach: every patient is given a personalised treatment plan that takes account of all aspects of their health.
  4. A short recovery period: thanks to modern technology and techniques, recovery is quick and causes the patient minimal discomfort.
  5. High standards of safety and quality: Israeli clinics adhere strictly to international protocols and standards of medical care.

Cataract treatment in Israel gives patients access to highly qualified medical care, improves their sight and allows them to return to an active life.

fields.title: Ovarian cysts
fields.bodyHtml:
Ovarian cysts: advanced treatment in Israel

Ovarian cysts are fluid-filled sacs in the ovaries and are common in women of reproductive age. Most ovarian cysts are functional and resolve on their own, but some may require medical treatment, particularly if they cause painful symptoms or pose a risk to health. The newest methods of diagnosing and treating ovarian cysts are available in Israel.

Diagnosis of ovarian cysts:

  1. Transvaginal ultrasound:
    The main method of diagnosing ovarian cysts, allowing their size, structure and exact position to be assessed.
  2. Laboratory tests:
    Blood tests for hormones and tumour markers such as CA-125 may be carried out to assess the nature of the cysts and rule out malignancy.
  3. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    Used for more detailed imaging, particularly in unclear cases or where cancer is suspected.
  4. Laparoscopy:
    A minimally invasive procedure sometimes used both to diagnose and to remove cysts.

Methods of treating ovarian cysts:

  1. Observation: many functional cysts resolve on their own, and doctors may recommend periodic follow-up with repeat ultrasound scans to monitor their size and condition.
  2. Hormone therapy: oral contraceptives or other hormonal medicines can help reduce the likelihood of new cysts forming and limit the growth of existing ones.
  3. Surgical treatment:
    • Cystectomy: removal of the cyst with preservation of the ovary.
    • Oophorectomy: removal of the whole ovary may be recommended where a cyst appears suspicious or where other conditions such as endometriosis are present.
    • Laparoscopic surgery: the preferred minimally invasive method of removing cysts, which shortens recovery and reduces pain after the operation.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • Advanced medical equipment and highly qualified specialists: Israeli clinics are equipped with the latest medical technology, and the doctors have extensive international experience.
  • An individual approach: every patient is offered a personalised treatment plan that takes account of her particular medical and personal needs.
  • A multidisciplinary approach: gynaecologists work with radiologists, endocrinologists and oncologists to ensure comprehensive care.

Treatment of ovarian cysts in Israel is aimed at dealing with the problem as effectively and safely as possible while preserving a woman's reproductive health and minimising any adverse consequences.

fields.title: Squint
fields.bodyHtml:
Squint (strabismus) is a condition in which the eyes do not look in the same direction at the same time. It may be constant or intermittent and may show itself as the eye turning inwards (esotropia), outwards (exotropia), upwards (hypertropia) or downwards (hypotropia). Squint can occur in children and adults and causes not only a cosmetic concern but also problems with sight.

Diagnosis of squint

  1. Visual examination: the ophthalmologist carries out an initial examination of the eyes, assessing their position and their ability to fix on a point.
  2. Visual acuity tests: testing the sight of each eye separately to establish whether there is amblyopia (lazy eye) or other visual problems.
  3. Coordination tests: used to assess how well the eyes move together and to measure the angle of the squint.
  4. Refraction tests: measurement of refractive errors (short-sightedness, long-sightedness or astigmatism) using special lenses.
  5. Fundoscopy: examination of the inner structures of the eye to rule out other conditions that may affect sight and the position of the eyes.
  6. Gonioscopy and biomicroscopy: used for detailed examination of the angle of the anterior chamber and the state of the eye muscles.

Methods of treating squint

  1. Correction of vision:
    • Glasses or contact lenses: used to correct refractive errors that may be causing the squint.
    • Prism lenses: help shift the image to correct double vision and improve coordination of eye movement.
  2. Orthoptic exercises:
    • Specific exercises for the eye muscles that help improve the coordination and strength of the muscles responsible for eye movement.
    • Exercises may involve a synoptophore and other devices for training the visual system.
  3. Occlusion therapy:
    • The use of eye patches or special filters to cover the stronger eye temporarily and stimulate the work and development of the weaker one.
    • This method is effective in treating amblyopia, which often accompanies squint.
  4. Botulinum toxin injections:
    • Injection of botulinum toxin into the eye muscles to weaken their action temporarily, which can help correct the position of the eye.
    • The procedure is carried out under local anaesthetic and requires no lengthy recovery.
  5. Surgical treatment:
    • Muscle recession: weakening the action of strong muscles by moving their points of attachment.
    • Muscle resection: strengthening the action of weak muscles by shortening them.
    • Adjustable suture surgery: allows the surgeon to adjust the tension of the muscles during the operation to achieve the best result.

Advantages of treating squint in Israel

  1. Highly qualified specialists: Israeli ophthalmologists have rich experience in treating squint in children and adults and use the most modern methods and technologies.
  2. An individual approach: every patient is given a personalised treatment plan that takes account of all aspects of their health and the state of their eyes.
  3. Modern equipment: clinics are equipped with the newest diagnostic and treatment devices, which ensures accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  4. A comprehensive approach: treatment covers not only surgery but also rehabilitation programmes, orthoptic exercises and psychological support for patients.
  5. A short recovery period: thanks to minimally invasive techniques and advanced technology, recovery after treatment is quick and causes the patient minimal discomfort.
  6. High standards of safety: Israeli clinics adhere strictly to international protocols and standards of medical care, which ensures safety and high quality.

Treatment of squint in Israel gives patients access to highly qualified medical care and improves both their sight and their quality of life.

fields.title: Lagophthalmos
fields.bodyHtml:
Lagophthalmos is a condition in which the eyelids cannot close completely, which leads to dryness and irritation of the eye. It can cause a number of complications, including infection and damage to the cornea. Lagophthalmos often arises from paralysis of the facial nerve, injury or complications after surgery.

Diagnosis of lagophthalmos

  1. Detailed review of the medical history:
    • The doctor talks with the patient, gathering information about symptoms, previous illnesses, treatment and other factors that may affect the condition.
  2. Visual examination:
    • The ophthalmologist examines the patient's eyes and assesses the state of the eyelids, cornea and conjunctiva.
  3. Schirmer's test:
    • Measurement of the amount of tear fluid produced by the eye, to assess the degree of dryness.
  4. Ophthalmoscopy:
    • Assessment of the cornea and the fundus to identify any damage or changes.
  5. Fluorescein test:
    • The use of fluorescein dye to reveal damage to the cornea.
  6. Tonometry:
    • Measurement of the pressure inside the eye to rule out glaucoma and other associated conditions.

Treatment of lagophthalmos

  1. Conservative treatment:
    • Artificial tears: drops to moisten the eyes and prevent dryness.
    • Eye ointments: soothing ointments used at night to protect the cornea.
    • Occlusion therapy: taping or special dressings over the eyelids to prevent tear fluid evaporating.
  2. Physiotherapy:
    • Eyelid massage: helps improve the blood supply and stimulate the eyelid muscles.
    • Warm compresses: help relax the muscles and improve tear production.
  3. Surgical treatment:
    • Tarsorrhaphy: partial or complete joining of the eyelids to narrow the opening of the eye and protect the cornea.
    • Implantation of a gold or platinum weight in the upper eyelid: a small weight is fitted that helps the eyelid close under gravity.
    • Myectomy and myoplasty: surgical procedures that alter the eyelid muscles to improve their function and allow the eye to close.
  4. Treatment of the underlying condition:
    • Where lagophthalmos is caused by facial nerve paralysis, the underlying condition must be treated, which may involve medication or surgery.

Advantages of treating lagophthalmos in Israel

  1. A high level of medical expertise:
    • Israel has leading specialists in ophthalmology with many years of experience and exceptional skills.
  2. Modern equipment:
    • Clinics are equipped with advanced diagnostic and treatment devices, which allows highly accurate investigation and effective treatment.
  3. An individual approach:
    • Every patient is given an individual treatment plan that takes account of the nature of the condition and their general health.
  4. Innovative treatments:
    • The use of the most modern methods and materials, including tarsorrhaphy and eyelid weight implantation.
  5. Comfortable conditions:
    • Patients can count on a high level of comfort and service during treatment and recovery.

Treatment of lagophthalmos in Israel gives patients access to high-quality medical care and considerably improves their quality of life.

fields.title: Treatment of back pain
fields.bodyHtml:
The orthopaedics department of the leading private clinic Assuta provides consultations for patients suffering from back pain. Thanks to the high qualifications of its specialists and its modern equipment, the clinic attracts patients from around the world, helping them deal successfully with a range of conditions and regain the pleasure of movement and their ability to work.

Back pain is often caused by degenerative changes in the intervertebral discs. These discs are the spine's natural shock absorbers: they allow it to move and prevent the nerves being compressed. The disease process is usually accompanied by chronic pain that worsens with physical activity or movement.

Chronic back pain is a symptom of many serious conditions, so it is important to seek qualified medical help at the first sign of trouble. In some cases the most effective treatment may be surgery.

Conservative treatment and physiotherapy can be effective at an early stage, but they usually bring only temporary relief.

Modern medicine has advanced considerably in diagnosing and treating chronic back pain. Developing effective and reliable treatments is a priority for orthopaedic surgeons worldwide. Modern methods are constantly being refined, and traditional approaches are giving way to innovative minimally invasive therapies that speed recovery and are safer for patients.

Intradiscal electrothermal therapy (IDET). The orthopaedics department of the Assuta clinic makes active use of the IDET technique. This is a minimally invasive procedure in which a catheter is introduced into the affected disc and gradually heated to 90°C. The heat causes the structure of the disc to contract and become denser, and destroys the nerve endings that cause the pain.

The operation is carried out under local anaesthetic with light sedation, so that the patient remains conscious and feels no pain.

Preparing for the procedure. Preparation for IDET includes a number of necessary investigations for accurate diagnosis and to study how the condition has developed. CT and MRI of the relevant sections of the spine are used, along with discography with a contrast medium. Biochemistry and clotting tests are also required.

It is important to tell the doctor about any other conditions and allergies, and about any medicines that affect blood clotting. The doctor will give advice on preparing for the operation. Patients are advised not to eat or drink for several hours beforehand.

Recovery. Recovery after IDET is quick and free of discomfort. After the operation the patient stays in a special room for about two hours until the anaesthetic wears off. No long hospital stay is needed, and the patient can go home the same day. Painkillers are needed for the first few weeks. The doctor will give advice on speeding recovery.

The Assuta clinic provides a wide range of medical services to a high standard, as the many positive reports from patients confirm.

fields.title: Meniscus treatment
fields.bodyHtml:
Meniscus treatment in Israel: advanced methods and approaches

Israel holds a leading position worldwide in treating disease and injury of the knee joint, including damage to the meniscus. Thanks to highly qualified specialists, innovative methods of diagnosis and treatment and an individual approach, patients receive effective care and can return to ordinary life quickly.

Diagnosis of meniscal injury

  1. MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)
    The gold standard in diagnosing meniscal injury, allowing the structure of the knee joint to be assessed in detail.
  2. Ultrasound examination
    Used to assess the soft tissues of the knee and can help identify associated injuries.
  3. X-rays
    Needed to rule out fractures and other bone injuries.
  4. Clinical examination
    Includes specific tests to assess the stability of the joint and identify meniscal damage.

Methods of treating the meniscus in Israel

  1. Conservative treatment
    Includes physiotherapy, orthopaedic supports to stabilise the knee and anti-inflammatory medicines to reduce pain and swelling.
  2. Arthroscopic surgery
    A minimally invasive procedure that allows precise inspection and repair of the damaged meniscus through small incisions, which considerably shortens recovery.
  3. Meniscectomy
    Partial or complete removal of the damaged part of the meniscus. Carried out arthroscopically where the meniscus cannot be repaired.
  4. Meniscal repair
    In some cases the meniscus can be repaired surgically, which preserves its function and prevents degenerative change in the joint.
  5. Meniscal transplantation
    In rare cases, where the meniscus is severely damaged, a donor meniscus may be transplanted.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • Advanced medical technology
    Israeli clinics are equipped with the most modern technology, which allows highly precise operations and shortens recovery.
  • Experienced specialists
    Leading orthopaedic and trauma surgeons of international standing with extensive experience in treating meniscal injury.
  • An individual approach
    Treatment in Israel is built on thorough diagnosis and on taking account of every patient's particular circumstances.
  • Comprehensive rehabilitation
    Recovery after surgery includes not only physical exercises but individual rehabilitation programmes aimed at an early return to an active life.

Meniscus treatment in Israel gives patients access to highly effective therapies, relieving pain quickly and restoring the function of the knee joint.

fields.title: Spinal treatment
fields.bodyHtml:
Spinal treatment in Israel: advanced methods and approaches

Israel holds a leading position in the treatment of spinal disease and injury, offering patients access to the newest methods of diagnosis and therapy. Thanks to a comprehensive approach based on the latest research, Israeli clinics achieve outstanding results in restoring the function of the spine and improving patients' quality of life.

Spinal conditions treated in Israel:

  • Back pain associated with herniated discs
    Often caused by a disc bulging and pressing on the nerves.
  • Ankylosing spondylitis
    A chronic inflammatory condition affecting the spine and the sacroiliac joints.
  • Degenerative disc disease
    Degenerative changes in the intervertebral discs that reduce their elasticity and height.
  • Osteoporosis
    A condition in which the bones become fragile and porous, increasing the risk of fracture.
  • Spinal canal stenosis
    Narrowing of the canal that houses the spinal cord, which can cause pain and weakness.
  • Scoliosis
    Sideways curvature of the spine, often accompanied by rotation of the vertebrae.
  • Spinal fracture
    May result from injury, osteoporosis or other conditions.
  • Spinal deformity
    Covers various changes in the shape of the spine, such as scoliosis and kyphosis.
  • Herniated disc
    Protrusion of part of an intervertebral disc beyond its normal position, pressing on the nerve roots.

Methods of diagnosis

  1. MRI and CT
    Produce detailed images of the spine for accurate diagnosis.
  2. X-ray
    Used to assess the state of the bones of the spine.
  3. Electromyography (EMG)
    Assessment of the electrical activity of the muscles to identify nerve damage.
  4. Laboratory tests
    Help identify inflammation and other associated conditions.

Methods of treatment

  1. Conservative treatment
    Physiotherapy, medication and the use of braces.
  2. Minimally invasive operations
    Microdiscectomy and laser decompression.
  3. Surgery
    Spinal fusion and disc replacement.
  4. Comprehensive rehabilitation
    Includes physical exercises, manual therapy and psychological support.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach
    Ensures a comprehensive treatment plan.
  • Advanced technology
    Guarantees accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach
    Takes account of every patient's particular needs.
  • Comprehensive support
    Provides full care at every stage of recovery.

Spinal treatment in Israel gives patients access to the most modern and effective therapies, helping them return to an active life free of pain.

fields.title: Blood cancer, also known as leukaemia
fields.bodyHtml:
Blood cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Blood cancer, also known as haematological malignancy, covers a wide range of conditions including leukaemia, lymphoma and myeloma. Israel holds a leading position in diagnosing and treating blood cancer, offering patients access to innovative treatments and research aimed at improving prognosis and quality of life.

Diagnosis of blood cancer

  1. Full blood count
    Can reveal abnormal levels of white cells, red cells and platelets, which often indicate blood cancer.
  2. Bone marrow biopsy
    A key diagnostic method that allows the state of the bone marrow and the presence of cancer cells to be assessed.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Immunophenotyping
    Used to determine the types of cancer cells on the basis of their molecular and cellular markers.
  4. Molecular and genetic testing,
    including PCR and cytogenetic analysis, helps identify the genetic mutations and chromosomal abnormalities associated with different types of blood cancer.
  5. Imaging,
    such as CT, MRI and PET-CT, may be ordered to identify enlarged lymph nodes or other sites affected by the disease.

Methods of treating blood cancer

  1. Chemotherapy
    The main treatment for blood cancer, aimed at destroying the cancer cells.
  2. Targeted therapy
    Involves medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells.
  3. Immunotherapy
    Stimulates the body's immune system to fight the cancer cells.
  4. Bone marrow (stem cell) transplantation
    A treatment in which the patient's damaged bone marrow is replaced with healthy marrow.
  5. Radiotherapy
    May be used for certain types of blood cancer, in particular to reduce the size of lymph nodes or affected areas.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of blood cancer

  • Highly qualified specialists and the use of advanced medical technology ensure a comprehensive and effective approach to treatment.
  • Individual treatment programmes are developed according to the type of blood cancer, the stage of the disease and the patient's particular circumstances.
  • Access to the newest treatments and clinical trials allows patients to receive innovative therapy, including experimental treatment.

fields.title: Leukaemia
fields.bodyHtml:
Leukaemia: advanced treatment in Israel

Leukaemia is a group of cancers of the blood and bone marrow marked by a raised level of white blood cells. In Israel, patients with leukaemia are offered a comprehensive approach to treatment that includes the latest research and individual treatment strategies.

Diagnosis of leukaemia

  1. Full blood count
    Can detect abnormal levels of white blood cells, anaemia and other changes.
  2. Bone marrow biopsy and aspiration
    The main methods of confirming a diagnosis of leukaemia, allowing the state of the bone marrow to be assessed.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Cytogenetic analysis
    Examination of the chromosomes of the cancer cells to identify genetic abnormalities.
  4. Immunophenotyping
    Testing to determine the type of leukaemia from the characteristics of the cancer cells.
  5. Molecular and genetic testing
    Identification of specific genetic mutations associated with different types of leukaemia.

Treatment of leukaemia

  1. Chemotherapy
    The main treatment, aimed at destroying the cancer cells.
  2. Targeted therapy
    The use of medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells.
  3. Immunotherapy
  4. The use of monoclonal antibodies and other medicines to stimulate the immune system against the cancer cells.
  5. Haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (bone marrow transplant)
    Allows healthy bone marrow to be restored after intensive treatment.
  6. Radiotherapy
    Sometimes used to destroy cancer cells or in preparation for a stem cell transplant.
  7. CAR-T cell therapy
    A newer treatment in which the patient's T cells are modified to fight the cancer cells.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach: the knowledge and experience of specialists from various fields of medicine are combined to develop the best treatment plan.
  • Advanced technology: access to the newest methods of diagnosis and treatment, including molecular and genetic testing and innovative therapies.
  • Individual treatment: treatment programmes developed with the genetic features of the disease and the patient's general condition in mind.
  • A high standard of medical care: modern medical institutions providing high-quality care and support at every stage of treatment.

Treatment of leukaemia in Israel gives patients access to advanced medical resources and innovative therapies, which helps achieve the best results against the disease.

fields.title: Hodgkin lymphoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Hodgkin lymphoma: advanced treatment in Israel

Hodgkin lymphoma is a type of lymphoma marked by the presence of particular cells known as Reed-Sternberg cells. In Israel, patients with Hodgkin lymphoma have access to modern methods of diagnosis and treatment based on the latest research and clinical experience.

Diagnosis of Hodgkin lymphoma

  1. Physical examination and history
    The initial assessment includes examination for enlarged lymph nodes and the gathering of information about symptoms.
  2. Laboratory tests
    Full blood count and measurement of the erythrocyte sedimentation rate.
  3. Lymph node biopsy
    Taking and examining a tissue sample to identify Reed-Sternberg cells.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  4. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    Assessment of how far the disease has spread in the body.
  5. PET-CT
    A combination of positron emission and computed tomography to identify active sites of disease.
  6. Bone marrow biopsy
    Examination for involvement of the bone marrow.

Treatment of Hodgkin lymphoma

  1. Chemotherapy
    The main treatment, often combined with targeted drugs.
  2. Radiotherapy
    Used for localised stages of the disease or after chemotherapy to destroy remaining tumour cells.
  3. Combined therapy
  4. A combination of chemotherapy and radiotherapy to achieve the greatest effect.
  5. Bone marrow transplantation
    Used in cases of relapse or refractory lymphoma.
  6. Immunotherapy
    The use of monoclonal antibodies directed at destroying the cancer cells.
  7. CAR-T cell therapy
    An innovative treatment in which the patient's T cells are modified in the laboratory so that they recognise and destroy cancer cells more effectively, and are then returned to the patient's body.

Why patients choose Israel

  • An individual approach
    Treatment is planned according to the stage of the disease, the patient's general health and their personal preferences.
  • Multidisciplinary teams
    Oncologists, haematologists, radiologists and other specialists work closely together to develop the most effective treatment plan.
  • Access to advanced technology
    The use of the latest advances in medicine and science, including the newest drugs and treatments.
  • A high standard of medical care
    A distinguishing feature of Israeli clinics is their attention to detail and their commitment to patients' comfort.

Treatment of Hodgkin lymphoma in Israel offers a comprehensive approach that combines the high qualifications of its specialists, an individual approach to every patient and the use of the most modern therapies, including CAR-T cell therapy, which gives a good chance of successful treatment and an improved quality of life.

Prices for the treatment and diagnosis of lymphoma

fields.title: Medulloblastoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Medulloblastoma: advanced treatment in Israel

Medulloblastoma is an aggressive brain tumour that occurs most often in children. This cancer affects the back of the skull and can spread to other parts of the central nervous system. In Israel, patients with medulloblastoma are offered many-sided and innovative approaches to treatment, aimed at maximising the chances of recovery and minimising long-term side effects.

Diagnosis of medulloblastoma

  1. Laboratory tests
    Include a full blood count and other tests to assess general health and identify possible markers of inflammation or infection.
  2. MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) of the brain
    The main diagnostic method, producing high-resolution images of the tumour.
  3. Lumbar puncture
    Taking a sample of cerebrospinal fluid to detect cancer cells that may be spreading through the central nervous system.
  4. Biopsy
    Carried out where it is necessary to determine the type of tumour and its genetic characteristics precisely.
  5. Neurophysiological examination
    May be used to assess the functional state of the nervous system.

Treatment of medulloblastoma

  1. Surgery
    The aim of the operation is to remove as much of the tumour as possible. Surgery is often the first step in comprehensive treatment.
  2. Radiotherapy
    Used after surgery to destroy remaining cancer cells. Israel uses advanced radiotherapy techniques that reduce the risk of side effects as far as possible.
  3. Chemotherapy
    Given before and/or after radiotherapy to fight the tumour throughout the body.
  4. Targeted therapy
    Where the tumour has particular genetic mutations, specific medicines directed at those mutations may be used.
  5. Immunotherapy
    A relatively new approach to treating certain forms of medulloblastoma, aimed at stimulating the immune system to fight the tumour.

Why patients choose Israel

  • Highly qualified specialists
    Israeli neurosurgeons, oncologists and radiologists have an international reputation and extensive experience in treating medulloblastoma.
  • An individual approach
    Every treatment plan is drawn up with the patient's age, the stage of the disease, the genetic features of the tumour and the patient's general health in mind.
  • Advanced technology
    Treatment uses the most modern medical technologies, including precision diagnostics and minimally invasive surgery.
  • Comprehensive support
    Psychological, social and rehabilitation support is provided to patients and their families at every stage of treatment.

Treatment of medulloblastoma in Israel offers a comprehensive and individual approach aimed at achieving the best possible outcome while preserving patients' quality of life.

fields.title: Melanoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Melanoma: advanced treatment in Israel

Melanoma is an aggressive form of skin cancer that can spread quickly to other organs. In Israel, patients with melanoma have access to innovative methods of diagnosis and treatment that combine the latest scientific advances with an individual approach to every case.

Diagnosis of melanoma

  1. Dermoscopy
    Visual examination of suspicious moles or marks on the skin using a special magnifying device.
  2. Biopsy
    Taking a tissue sample for histological examination, the gold standard in diagnosing melanoma.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Genetic testing for the BRAF mutation
    Establishing whether a mutation in the BRAF gene is present, which can affect the choice of treatment and the outlook.
  4. PET-CT and MRI
    Used to assess how far the melanoma has spread in the body and to detect metastases.
  5. Genetic testing
    Examination of the biopsy tissue for mutations that may affect the choice of treatment.

Treatment of melanoma

  1. Surgical removal
    The primary and most effective treatment for melanoma at an early stage.
  2. Sentinel lymph node biopsy
    This method is used to determine how far the cancer has spread. The sentinel node is the first lymph node to which cancer cells may spread from the primary tumour. Identifying and examining it helps doctors establish whether the cancer has spread further and whether additional treatment is needed.
  3. Immunotherapy
    The use of medicines that activate the immune system to fight the cancer cells.
  4. Targeted therapy
    The use of medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells, particularly where certain genetic mutations such as BRAF are present.
  5. Chemotherapy
    May be used in advanced melanoma, although it is less effective than immunotherapy and targeted therapy.
  6. Radiotherapy
    Sometimes used to treat metastases in the brain or other parts of the body.
  7. Clinical trials
    Patients may take part in trials of new medicines and treatments.

Why patients choose Israel

  • Highly qualified specialists: Israel has leading world experts in dermato-oncology and melanoma.
  • An individual approach to treatment: treatment programmes are developed according to the nature of the disease and each patient's needs.
  • Access to innovative therapies: patients can receive the most modern medicines and take part in clinical trials.
  • Multidisciplinary teams: these ensure a comprehensive approach to treatment, combining the knowledge and experience of doctors of various specialities.

Treatment of melanoma in Israel gives patients access to advanced medical resources and personalised treatment strategies, which helps achieve the best results and improve the outlook.

Prices for the treatment and diagnosis of melanoma

fields.title: Ocular melanoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Ocular melanoma is a malignant tumour that develops from the pigment cells within the eyeball. Most often it develops in the uveal tract, which includes the iris, the ciliary body and the choroid. The condition can lead to loss of sight and even spread to other organs, which makes it extremely dangerous.

Diagnosis of ocular melanoma

  1. Detailed review of the medical history:
    • The doctor gathers information about symptoms such as changes in vision, dark spots in the field of view, flashes of light and discomfort in the eye, and reviews the family history.
  2. Visual examination and eye tests:
    • Assessment of visual acuity and examination of the eye to identify abnormalities.
  3. Ophthalmoscopy:
    • Examination of the fundus with a special instrument to assess the state of the optic nerve, the vessels and the retina.
  4. Ultrasound examination of the eye:
    • The use of ultrasound to obtain images of the internal structures of the eye and establish the size and position of the tumour.
  5. Fluorescein angiography:
    • Injection of a contrast medium into a vein to assess the blood supply to the retina and identify abnormal changes.
  6. Optical coherence tomography (OCT):
    • Scanning of the structures of the eye to obtain detailed images of the retina and optic nerve.
  7. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT):
    • Used to assess how far the tumour has spread and to detect metastases in other organs.
  8. Biopsy:
    • Taking a tissue sample from the tumour for histological examination to confirm the diagnosis.
      (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)

Treatment of ocular melanoma

  1. Drug therapy:
    • Immunotherapy: the use of medicines that stimulate the immune system to fight the cancer cells.
    • Cytotoxic drugs: used in chemotherapy to shrink the tumour and suppress its growth.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • Brachytherapy: placing radioactive seeds directly in the tumour for local treatment.
    • External beam radiotherapy: radiation directed at the tumour to destroy the cancer cells.
  3. Surgery:
    • Local resection: removal of the tumour and some of the surrounding tissue.
    • Enucleation: complete removal of the eyeball in the case of large tumours or where there is a risk of spread.
  4. Laser therapy:
    • The use of a laser to destroy cancer cells in small, superficial tumours.
  5. Photodynamic therapy:
    • Administration of a light-sensitive agent that is activated by a laser and destroys the cancer cells.

Advantages of treating ocular melanoma in Israel

  1. A high level of professionalism:
    • Israeli doctors have deep knowledge and many years of experience in treating melanoma and other eye conditions.
  2. Modern equipment:
    • Clinics are equipped with advanced diagnostic and treatment devices, which allows highly accurate investigation and effective treatment.
  3. An individual approach:
    • Every patient is given an individual treatment plan that takes account of the nature of the condition and their general health.
  4. Innovative treatments:
    • The use of the most modern methods and medicines, including immunotherapy and photodynamic therapy.
  5. Comprehensive support:
    • Covers not only treatment of the underlying condition but also support for the patient's mental and physical wellbeing during treatment and recovery.

Treatment of ocular melanoma in Israel gives patients access to high-quality medical care and considerably improves both the outlook and their quality of life.

fields.title: Meningioma
fields.bodyHtml:
Meningioma: advanced treatment in Israel

A meningioma is a tumour that develops from the meninges, the membranes covering the brain and spinal cord. Most meningiomas are benign and grow slowly, although some may be aggressive or malignant. In Israel, patients with a meningioma have access to modern methods of diagnosis and treatment and to individually designed treatment programmes.

Diagnosis of meningioma

  1. Laboratory tests
    Include a full blood count and other tests to assess general health and identify possible markers of inflammation or infection.
  2. MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)
    The gold standard in diagnosing meningiomas, allowing detailed study of the size, shape and position of the tumour.
  3. CT (computed tomography)
    May be used to obtain further information about the state of the bones of the skull and spine.
  4. Biopsy
    Carried out where it is necessary to determine the type of tumour and how malignant it is.

Treatment of meningioma

  1. Observation
    Where a benign meningioma grows slowly and causes no symptoms, follow-up with periodic MRI scans may be recommended to monitor the tumour.
  2. Surgery
    The preferred treatment for most meningiomas, allowing the tumour to be removed completely and the patient to be cured. Israel uses both traditional and minimally invasive surgical techniques.
  3. Radiotherapy
    May be used as an alternative to surgery for patients in whom an operation carries a high risk, or to treat tumour remaining after surgery. Advanced methods of radiotherapy are available in Israel, including stereotactic radiosurgery and proton therapy.
  4. Drug therapy
    Currently the subject of active research for malignant meningiomas and those that cannot be treated by surgery or radiotherapy.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach: every case is considered by a team of specialists including neurosurgeons, oncologists and radiologists.
  • Advanced medical equipment: Israeli clinics are equipped with the most modern technology for diagnosing and treating meningiomas.
  • Individual treatment programmes: treatment is planned taking account of every aspect of the patient's health, including age, general condition and preferences.
  • A high standard of medical care: patients receive quality medical care and support at every stage of treatment.

Treatment of meningioma in Israel gives patients access to advanced technology, highly qualified specialists and individual treatment programmes, which offers the best prospects of a successful outcome.

fields.title: Herniated disc
fields.bodyHtml:
Herniated disc: innovative treatment in Israel

A herniated disc is a common condition that can cause severe pain, numbness or weakness because of pressure on the spinal nerves. In Israel, patients are offered advanced methods of diagnosing and treating a herniated disc that bring rapid relief of symptoms and recovery.

Diagnosis of a herniated disc

  1. MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)
    The gold standard in diagnosis, allowing the position and size of the hernia to be established precisely.
  2. CT (computed tomography)
    May be used to obtain detailed images of the bony structures of the spine.
  3. Myelography
    A contrast study that may be used to assess the state of the spinal canal and the nerve roots.
  4. Electromyography (EMG)
    Carried out to assess the electrical activity of the muscles and nerves, which helps establish the extent of nerve damage.

Treatments for a herniated disc in Israel

  1. Conservative treatment
    Includes physiotherapy, pain-relieving medication, the use of braces and nerve blocks. It is aimed at reducing pain and inflammation and at strengthening the supporting muscles.
  2. Endoscopic discectomy — a minimally invasive surgical procedure with very rapid recovery, intended to relieve back pain caused by a herniated disc. This treatment is particularly effective for patients whose pain does not improve with conservative treatment.
  3. Minimally invasive techniques
    Such as percutaneous laser discectomy, radiofrequency ablation and endoscopic removal of the hernia, which offer an alternative to open surgery with a lower risk of complications and a shorter recovery period.
  4. Surgery
    Laminectomy, discectomy or spinal fusion may be recommended where conservative treatment brings no relief and the hernia is causing serious neurological symptoms.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach
    Individual treatment plans are drawn up by a team of specialists including orthopaedic surgeons, neurologists and physiotherapists.
  • Advanced technology
    Israeli clinics are equipped with the most modern devices for carrying out diagnostic and treatment procedures.
  • Experienced specialists
    Doctors with international recognition and extensive experience in treating conditions of the spine.
  • A focus on quality of life
    The main emphasis is not only on relieving pain and restoring function but also on improving patients' overall quality of life.

Treatment of a herniated disc in Israel gives patients access to innovative therapies that achieve a considerable improvement without a long recovery. An individual approach to every case ensures the best choice of treatment, based on the patient's particular needs and expectations.

fields.title: Peritoneal mesothelioma
fields.bodyHtml:
Peritoneal mesothelioma: advanced treatment in Israel

Mesothelioma of the peritoneum, also known as peritoneal mesothelioma, is a rare type of cancer arising in the membrane that lines the abdominal cavity. This type of cancer is often associated with exposure to asbestos. Clinics in Israel offer a comprehensive approach to treating this condition using modern methods of diagnosis and treatment.

Diagnosis of peritoneal mesothelioma:

  1. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    These imaging methods allow the extent of the tumour within the abdominal cavity to be assessed.
  2. PET-CT: Provides a detailed picture of the metabolic activity of the tumour and of any metastases.
  3. Biopsy:
    Taking tissue samples for histological examination — the gold standard for confirming a diagnosis of mesothelioma.
  4. Laboratory tests:
    Blood tests can identify markers associated with mesothelioma, such as mesothelin.

Treatments for peritoneal mesothelioma:

  1. Chemotherapy:
    • Systemic chemotherapy: The use of anti-cancer medicines to destroy the cancer cells.
    • Intraperitoneal chemotherapy: Chemotherapy medicines delivered directly into the abdominal cavity for local treatment.
  2. Surgery:
    • Cytoreductive surgery: Removal of as much tumour tissue as possible.
    • Peritonectomy: Removal of the affected peritoneum to reduce the bulk of the tumour and ease symptoms.
  3. Hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC):
    • After the visible tumours have been removed, the peritoneum is treated with heated chemotherapy medicines to destroy any remaining cancer cells.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: A team of specialists including oncologists, surgeons and radiologists ensures a comprehensive approach to every case.
