  • Advanced medical equipment: The use of modern technology for diagnosis and treatment improves results and shortens recovery time.
  • Individualised treatment: Treatment plans are drawn up taking account of the particular features of the condition and the patient's general health.

Treatment of peritoneal mesothelioma in Israel aims to extend patients' life expectancy and quality of life as far as possible, drawing on the latest advances in medical science and practice.

fields.title: Mydriasis
fields.bodyHtml:
General information about mydriasis

Mydriasis is a condition in which the pupil is dilated. Normally the pupil dilates in darkness or in stressful situations, but mydriasis can be caused by various illnesses, injuries or the effects of medicines. Pathological mydriasis requires diagnosis and treatment, since it may indicate serious disturbances in the body.

Causes of mydriasis

  1. Neurological disorders: damage to the cranial nerves, stroke, raised intracranial pressure.
  2. Eye injuries: bruising, damage to the iris.
  3. Infections: meningitis, encephalitis.
  4. Toxic substances: poisoning by drugs, alcohol or chemicals.
  5. Medicines: antidepressants, antihistamines, eye drops containing atropine.
  6. Other conditions: glaucoma, brain tumours.

Diagnosis of mydriasis

  1. Detailed review of the medical history:
    • The doctor gathers information about the symptoms, any preceding illness, previous conditions and treatment, and possible injuries or exposure to toxic substances.
  2. Visual examination and ophthalmoscopy:
    • The ophthalmologist examines the patient's pupils, noting their reaction to light, their symmetry and any other changes. Ophthalmoscopy allows assessment of the optic nerve, the vessels of the fundus and the retina.
  3. Gonioscopy:
    • Examination of the angle of the anterior chamber of the eye using a special contact lens. This method helps identify causes of impaired drainage in the eye, which may be linked to glaucoma.
  4. Visual field test:
    • A computerised perimeter is used to check the patient's peripheral vision, to identify any restriction and establish the extent of damage to the optic nerve.
  5. Optical coherence tomography (OCT):
    • A scan of the eye that produces high-quality images of the structures of the fundus, including the optic nerve and the retina.
  6. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT):
    • These imaging methods are used to identify possible structural changes in the brain that may be the cause of the mydriasis.
  7. Laboratory tests:
    • Blood and urine tests can help identify toxins or infections that may have caused the mydriasis.

Treatment of mydriasis

  1. Drug therapy:
    • Antibiotics or antiviral medicines: where the mydriasis has an infectious cause (meningitis or encephalitis, for example).
    • Antidotes and detoxification: in cases of poisoning by toxic substances or medicines.
    • Eye drops: depending on the cause of the mydriasis, drops may be prescribed to lower the pressure inside the eye or improve drainage of fluid from it.
  2. Treatment of the underlying condition:
    • Where there is a neurological disorder (stroke or raised intracranial pressure, for example), appropriate treatment is given under the supervision of a neurologist.
  3. Surgery:
    • In rare cases, where the mydriasis is caused by structural changes in the eye or brain, surgical treatment may be required.
  4. Physiotherapy and rehabilitation:
    • Physiotherapy techniques and rehabilitation programmes may be used to restore the function of the eye and improve the patient's general condition.

Advantages of treating mydriasis in Israel

  1. Highly qualified specialists:
    • Israeli doctors have deep knowledge and many years of experience in treating mydriasis and other eye conditions.
  2. Modern equipment:
    • Clinics are equipped with advanced diagnostic and treatment devices, which allows highly accurate investigation and effective treatment.
  3. An individual approach:
    • Every patient is given an individual treatment plan that takes account of the nature of the condition and their general health.
  4. Innovative treatments:
    • The use of the most modern methods and medicines, including laser technology and genetic testing.
  5. Comprehensive support:
    • Covers not only treatment of the underlying condition but also support for the patient's mental and physical wellbeing during treatment and rehabilitation.

Treatment of mydriasis in Israel gives patients access to high-quality medical care and considerably improves both the outlook and their quality of life.

fields.title: Myeloma
fields.bodyHtml:
Myeloma: advanced treatment in Israel

Myeloma, also known as multiple myeloma, is a type of blood cancer affecting the plasma cells in the bone marrow. In Israel, patients with myeloma are offered modern methods of diagnosis and innovative approaches to treatment, aimed at improving both the outlook and quality of life.

Diagnosis of myeloma

  1. Laboratory tests
    These include a full blood count, measurement of protein levels including immunoglobulins and Bence Jones protein in the urine, and biochemical tests to assess kidney function and calcium levels.
  2. Bone marrow biopsy
    A procedure that establishes the presence of cancer cells and assesses how far the bone marrow is affected.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. X-rays of the skeleton
    These help identify areas of bone damage.
  4. MRI and CT
    Highly accurate imaging methods used for a more detailed examination of the affected areas.
  5. PET-CT
    One of the most modern diagnostic methods, allowing the activity of the disease in the body to be assessed.

Treatment of myeloma

  1. Chemotherapy
    The main treatment, aimed at destroying the cancer cells.
  2. Targeted therapy
    The use of medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells.
  3. Immunotherapy
    Includes the use of monoclonal antibodies and other medicines to stimulate the immune system against the cancer cells.
  4. Bone marrow transplant
    A procedure that restores healthy bone marrow after intensive chemotherapy.
  5. Radiotherapy
    Used to relieve pain and treat individual areas of bone damage.
  6. Bisphosphonates
    Medicines that strengthen the bones and prevent the fractures myeloma can cause.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach: treatment involves oncologists, haematologists, radiologists, bone marrow transplant specialists and other doctors.
  • Individualised treatment: the treatment plan is drawn up taking account of the genetic and molecular features of each patient's disease.
  • Innovative treatments: access to the latest developments in medicine, including the newest medicines and therapeutic strategies.
  • A high standard of medical care: modern clinics equipped with advanced technology, and highly qualified medical staff.

Treatment of myeloma in Israel combines highly qualified specialists, the use of advanced technology and an individual approach to every patient, which helps achieve the best results and a considerable improvement in quality of life.

fields.title: Uterine fibroids
fields.bodyHtml:
Uterine fibroids: advanced treatment in Israel

Uterine fibroids are benign tumours of the smooth muscle tissue of the womb, and occur in many women of reproductive age. Advanced methods of diagnosing and treating uterine fibroids are available in Israel, helping to manage symptoms effectively and prevent possible complications.

Diagnosis of uterine fibroids:

  1. Gynaecological examination:
    The doctor may detect enlargement or distortion of the womb on examination.
  2. Ultrasound scan:
    A transvaginal ultrasound is the standard method for imaging fibroids, allowing their size and position to be assessed.
  3. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    Used for a more precise assessment of the size and position of fibroids, particularly when planning surgery.
  4. Hysteroscopy:
    Visual examination of the inner surface of the womb with an optical instrument, which may be needed to assess submucosal fibroids.
  5. Laboratory tests:
    Blood tests may be ordered to assess haemoglobin levels, particularly where there are symptoms of anaemia due to heavy periods.

Treatments for uterine fibroids:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Hormone therapy: Medicines such as gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonists may be used to shrink fibroids and control symptoms.
    • Non-hormonal medicines: Tranexamic acid, for example, to reduce blood loss during periods.
  2. Surgery:
    • Myomectomy: Removal of the fibroids while preserving the womb — the preferred option for women who wish to retain their fertility.
    • Hysterectomy: Removal of the womb, recommended where other treatments are ineffective or where the fibroids have grown very large.
  3. Minimally invasive procedures:
    • Uterine artery embolisation (UAE): A procedure in which the blood supply to the fibroids is blocked by introducing special substances through a catheter, causing the tumours to shrink.
    • MRI-guided ultrasound ablation: The use of high-intensity focused ultrasound to destroy fibroid tissue under MRI control.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Gynaecologists, radiologists and surgeons work together to draw up an individual treatment plan.
  • Advanced medical equipment: The use of the most modern diagnostic and treatment technology.
  • Individual treatment: All procedures and treatment are adapted to the particular needs of each woman, taking account of her age, general health and wish to preserve her fertility.

Treatment of uterine fibroids in Israel aims to relieve symptoms as effectively and safely as possible while preserving the patient's health and quality of life.

fields.title: Kidney stones
fields.bodyHtml:
Introduction

Kidney stone disease, also known as nephrolithiasis or kidney stones, is a common condition of the urinary system characterised by the formation of hard deposits (stones) in the kidneys or urinary tract. These stones can vary in size and may cause painful symptoms, and can lead to complications if they are not detected and treated in good time. This article looks at the methods of diagnosing and treating kidney stone disease, and at the advantages of treating this condition in Israel.

Methods of diagnosis

Diagnosis of kidney stone disease usually begins with a discussion of the patient's medical history and symptoms. Further investigations are then carried out to confirm the presence of stones and establish their type, size and position. The main methods of diagnosing kidney stone disease include:

  • Kidney ultrasound: an ultrasound scan of the kidneys is one of the most accessible and safest methods of diagnosing kidney stone disease. Ultrasound allows stones in the kidneys to be visualised and their characteristics assessed.
  • Computed tomography (CT): a CT scan provides more detailed images of the kidneys and urinary tract, which allows the size and position of the stones to be established more precisely.
  • Urography: an X-ray method in which a contrast medium is introduced to visualise the urinary tract and identify stones.
  • Urine test: a urine test can help identify crystals, which are a precursor to the formation of stones.

Methods of treatment

Treatment of kidney stone disease depends on the type and size of the stones, their number and position, and on whether they are causing symptoms or complications. In some cases stones pass out of the body on their own, but in most cases medical intervention is required. The main treatments for kidney stone disease include:

  • Watchful waiting: in some cases small stones may pass out of the body on their own with plenty of fluids and time. Doctors may recommend regular monitoring and urine tests to follow the situation.
  • Drug treatment: doctors may prescribe medicines that help dissolve stones or reduce the formation of new ones.
  • Extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL): a non-invasive treatment in which sound waves are used to break up the stones so that they can pass out in the urine.
  • Surgical removal of stones: where stones are too large or are causing complications, surgery may be required to remove them.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

Israel is known for its high level of medical expertise and advanced technology. Treatment of kidney stone disease in Israel offers the following advantages:

  • Experienced specialists: doctors at Israeli medical centres have extensive experience in treating kidney stone disease. They trained at leading medical schools and are highly competent in this field.
  • Innovative treatments: Israeli medical centres use advanced methods of treating kidney stone disease, which delivers the best results and minimises the risk of complications.
  • An individual approach: doctors in Israel take account of each patient's particular circumstances and draw up an individual treatment plan to achieve the best results.
  • Comfortable stay: Israel offers a high standard of comfort and service for patients coming for treatment of kidney stone disease.

Conclusion

Kidney stone disease is a serious condition that can lead to painful symptoms and complications. Early detection and treatment play an important part in preventing possible complications and restoring patients' health. Treatment in Israel gives patients access to experienced specialists and advanced treatments, which offers the best chance of overcoming kidney stone disease successfully and restoring quality of life. If you suspect you have kidney stone disease or other problems with your kidneys or urinary tract, we recommend consulting a qualified doctor for an accurate diagnosis and to establish the best treatment plan.

fields.title: Male infertility
fields.bodyHtml:
Introduction

Male infertility is one of the main causes of infertility in couples. It is a medical condition in which a man has difficulty conceiving a child with his partner. Male infertility can have various causes, including reduced sperm quality, obstruction of the urogenital tract, or hormonal disorders. This article looks at the methods of diagnosing and treating male infertility, and at the advantages of treating this condition in Israel.

Methods of diagnosis

Diagnosis of male infertility begins with a medical examination of the patient and the taking of a history. The doctor then orders further tests and investigations to identify the causes of the infertility. The main methods of diagnosing male infertility include:

  • Semen analysis: a test of the semen that assesses the number, movement and shape of the sperm. Semen analysis helps establish the quality of the sperm and the possible causes of infertility.
  • Hormone tests: testing hormone levels can help identify hormonal disorders that may be causing male infertility.
  • Scrotal ultrasound: an ultrasound scan of the scrotum allows its structures to be visualised and any abnormalities identified.
  • Testicular biopsy: in some cases the doctor may recommend a testicular biopsy to examine the tissue and identify the causes of infertility.

Methods of treatment

Treatment of male infertility depends on the causes identified and may involve medicines, surgery or other methods. The main treatments for male infertility include:

  • Drug treatment: doctors may prescribe medicines to raise hormone levels or improve sperm quality.
  • Surgery: an operation may be required to correct abnormalities of the urogenital tract or to restore patency.
  • Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI): a method of assisted fertilisation in which a single sperm is injected directly into the egg.
  • Intracytoplasmic morphologically selected sperm injection (IMSI): a more thorough method of selecting sperm for fertilisation with the aid of a high-magnification microscope.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

Israel is one of the leading countries in the treatment of male infertility, offering patients advanced treatments and a high level of medical expertise. The advantages of treating male infertility in Israel include:

  • Experienced specialists: doctors at Israeli medical centres have many years of experience in diagnosing and treating male infertility. Their knowledge and skills allow them to approach every case effectively and provide high-quality treatment.
  • The use of advanced technology: Israeli medical centres use advanced methods of diagnosing and treating male infertility, which improves the chances of successful treatment and of conceiving a child.
  • An individual approach: doctors in Israel understand that every patient is different, and draw up an individual treatment plan to achieve the best results.
  • High standards of medical care: the medical infrastructure in Israel meets high standards of quality, ensuring a comfortable stay for patients and effective treatment.

Conclusion

Male infertility is a complex condition that can be treated successfully with modern methods and advanced technology. Establishing the causes of male infertility and choosing the best treatment plan are the key steps towards a successful pregnancy. Israel offers patients high-quality medical care, which makes it an attractive place for the treatment of male infertility. If you or your partner are having difficulty conceiving, we recommend consulting qualified specialists in Israel for professional help and support on the way to fulfilling your dream of parenthood.

fields.title: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Non-Hodgkin lymphoma: advanced treatment in Israel

Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is a group of blood cancers affecting the lymphatic system. In Israel, patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma have access to advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment based on the latest scientific research and clinical experience.

Diagnosis of non-Hodgkin lymphoma

  1. Physical examination and history
    Doctors carry out an examination and gather information about the symptoms and the history of the illness.
  2. Laboratory tests
    These include a full blood count and biochemical tests.
  3. Lymph node biopsy
    Obtaining and histologically examining lymph node tissue to confirm the presence of lymphoma.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  4. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    Used to assess how far the tumour has spread in the body.
  5. PET-CT
    A method combining positron emission tomography and computed tomography, allowing the activity of the tumour and the presence of metastases to be assessed.
  6. Bone marrow biopsy and aspiration
    Carried out to identify involvement of the bone marrow.

Treatment of non-Hodgkin lymphoma

  1. Chemotherapy
    The main treatment, aimed at destroying the cancer cells in the body.
  2. Radiotherapy
    Used for localised forms of lymphoma, or to shrink tumours before a stem cell transplant.
  3. Biological and targeted therapy: Includes the use of monoclonal antibodies and other medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells.
  4. Stem cell transplant
    Used in relapsed or refractory non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
  5. Immunotherapy
    Includes the use of medicines that stimulate the immune system to fight the cancer cells.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach: specialists from various fields of medicine work together to create an individualised treatment plan.
  • Advanced treatments: patients have access to the most modern treatments, including the latest developments in targeted and immune therapy.
  • Highly qualified specialists: Israel is home to leading world experts in haemato-oncology.
  • An individual approach to treatment: every aspect of treatment is planned with the patient's personal needs and preferences and their physical and psychological condition in mind.

Treatment of non-Hodgkin lymphoma in Israel gives patients access to innovative therapies and a high standard of medical care, which makes it possible to achieve the best results and improve quality of life.

Prices for the treatment and diagnosis of lymphoma

fields.title: Neuroblastoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Neuroblastoma: advanced treatment in Israel

Neuroblastoma is a type of cancer that most often affects young children. It arises in nerve tissue, particularly in the area of the adrenal glands or around the spinal cord in the chest or abdomen. In Israel, patients with neuroblastoma have access to a comprehensive approach to treatment combining innovative diagnostic methods, advanced treatment strategies and rehabilitation support.

Diagnosis of neuroblastoma

  1. Physical examination and history
    Includes assessment of the symptoms and gathering information about the child's medical history.
  2. Laboratory tests
    Blood and urine tests for markers characteristic of neuroblastoma, including catecholamine levels.
  3. Ultrasound scan
    Helps detect a tumour in the area of the adrenal glands or in the abdominal cavity.
  4. MRI and CT
    Highly accurate imaging methods for establishing the size and position of the tumour and how far it has spread.
  5. PET-CT
    Assessment of the metabolic activity of the tumour and detection of metastases.
  6. Biopsy
    Obtaining and analysing a sample of tumour tissue to confirm the diagnosis.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)

Treatment of neuroblastoma

  1. Surgery
    Aimed at removing as much of the tumour as possible without harming the child's health.
  2. Chemotherapy
    Used to shrink the tumour before surgery and to destroy any remaining cancer cells afterwards.
  3. Radiotherapy
    Used to destroy cancer cells locally, particularly where the tumour cannot be removed completely by surgery.
  4. High-dose chemotherapy followed by a stem cell transplant
    A method used to treat widespread neuroblastoma.
  5. Immunotherapy
    The newest treatment strategy, aimed at activating the child's immune system to fight the tumour.
  6. Targeted therapy
    The use of medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the tumour.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Leading specialists in oncology, surgery, radiology and paediatrics work together to develop the most effective treatment plan.
  • Individualised treatment: Treatment strategies are developed taking account of every aspect of the child's health and the particular features of the illness.
  • Access to the newest technology and medicines: The use of the most modern methods of diagnosis and treatment, including clinical trials of new medicines.
  • Support and rehabilitation: Comprehensive support for the child and family at every stage of treatment, including rehabilitation programmes.

Treatment of neuroblastoma in Israel combines highly qualified specialists, advanced treatments and a deep understanding of the need to support young patients and their families, offering strong prospects of recovery and a return to full life.

fields.title: Neuroendocrine cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Neuroendocrine cancer (NEC) is a rare and complex cancer arising from the cells of the neuroendocrine system, which have both nerve and endocrine functions. These tumours can arise in any organ, but occur most often in the gastrointestinal tract, the pancreas and the lungs. Israel has developed advanced methods of diagnosing and treating this condition, which makes it possible to achieve good results and improve patients' quality of life.

Diagnosis of neuroendocrine cancer

  1. Laboratory tests:
    • Blood and urine tests to identify specific markers such as chromogranin A and 5-HIAA, which help establish the presence and activity of the tumour.
  2. Somatostatin receptor PET-CT:
    • Positron emission tomography (PET) combined with computed tomography (CT), using radiopharmaceuticals that bind to somatostatin receptors. This allows tumours and metastases to be imaged precisely, giving a high level of diagnostic accuracy.
  3. Biopsy:
    • A biopsy of the tumour followed by histological and immunohistochemical analysis to confirm the diagnosis and establish the type of neuroendocrine tumour. The biopsy helps determine the exact nature of the tumour and choose the best treatment.

Treatments for neuroendocrine cancer:

  1. Surgery:
    • Tumour resection: removal of the tumour together with some healthy tissue. Used in localised forms of the disease.
    • Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) and cryoablation: minimally invasive methods used to destroy the tumour with high or low temperatures.
  2. Drug treatment:
    • Biotherapy: the use of somatostatin analogues (octreotide, lanreotide), which suppress hormone secretion and slow the growth of the tumour.
    • Targeted therapy: the use of medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the tumour cells (sunitinib, everolimus).
    • Chemotherapy: prescribed in aggressive forms of NEC or where the cancer has spread.
  3. Radiotherapy:
    • Local radiotherapy: used to shrink the tumour and relieve symptoms.
    • Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT): an innovative treatment in which radionuclides bind to the tumour cells through somatostatin receptors and destroy them from within.
  4. Radioembolisation:
    • Introduction of radioactive microspheres into the blood vessels supplying the tumour, which reduces its size and activity.

Advantages of treating neuroendocrine cancer in Israel:

  1. Highly qualified specialists: internationally recognised oncologists with extensive experience in treating rare and complex cancers.
  2. Modern equipment: the use of the newest technology and devices for accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  3. An individual approach: personalised treatment regimens developed with each patient's particular circumstances in mind.
  4. Innovative treatments: the use of advanced therapies such as PRRT and targeted therapy.
  5. High standards of quality: compliance with international protocols and standards for cancer treatment.
  6. Comprehensive support: a multidisciplinary approach involving oncologists, surgeons, radiologists, endocrinologists and other specialists to provide patients with all-round care.

Treatment of neuroendocrine cancer in Israel achieves good results and improves both the outlook and quality of life for patients, thanks to modern methods of diagnosis and therapy and the professionalism of Israeli doctors.

fields.title: Diabetes insipidus
fields.bodyHtml:
Diabetes insipidus: approaches to treatment in Israel

Diabetes insipidus is a rare condition in which the balance of fluid in the body is disturbed. It is caused by a lack of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) or by that hormone not working effectively, which leads to excessive loss of water in the urine. In Israel, patients with diabetes insipidus are offered a comprehensive approach to the diagnosis and treatment of this condition.

Diagnosis of diabetes insipidus:

  1. History and physical examination
    The doctor gathers information about symptoms such as excessive thirst and frequent urination, and carries out a general medical examination.
  2. Urine test
    Helps establish the concentration of the urine, which is usually low in patients with diabetes insipidus.
  3. Blood tests for electrolytes and kidney function
    Allow assessment of sodium and other electrolyte levels and of how the kidneys are working.
  4. Water deprivation test
    The patient is asked to go without fluids for a set period while doctors monitor changes in the volume of urine passed and in electrolyte concentrations.
  5. MRI of the brain
    May be ordered to rule out other causes, such as tumours, that can produce symptoms resembling diabetes insipidus.

Treatment of diabetes insipidus in Israel:

  1. Replacement therapy
    Administration of a synthetic analogue of ADH, such as desmopressin, to control the symptoms of the condition.
  2. Lifestyle adjustments
    Advice on maintaining hydration and on changes to the diet to manage symptoms.
  3. Treatment of the underlying condition
    Where the diabetes insipidus is caused by another condition, such as a pituitary tumour, treating it may require surgery or other therapy.
  4. Monitoring and support
    Regular monitoring of electrolyte levels and kidney function, together with support from medical staff to ensure the condition is managed properly.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An individual approach
    Treatment is chosen according to the features of each case and any accompanying conditions.
  • Access to the newest medicines
    The use of the most modern medicines, including desmopressin in various forms (tablets, nasal spray, injections), for effective control of symptoms.
  • A multidisciplinary team of specialists
    Close cooperation between endocrinologists, neurologists, surgeons and other specialists for a comprehensive approach to treatment.
  • Educational programmes for patients
    Information and support for patients and their families to help them understand the condition and how to control it.

Treatment of diabetes insipidus in Israel aims to minimise symptoms, prevent complications and improve patients' quality of life, with a comprehensive and joined-up approach to managing the condition.

fields.title: Ulcerative colitis
fields.bodyHtml:
Ulcerative colitis: advanced treatment in Israel

Ulcerative colitis is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease characterised by periods of flare-up and remission. Israel uses modern methods of diagnosing and treating this condition, aimed at reducing symptoms and achieving lasting remission.

Diagnosis of ulcerative colitis:

  1. Colonoscopy with biopsy:
    The main diagnostic method, allowing the inner surface of the large bowel to be examined and tissue samples to be taken for histological examination.
  2. Barium enema:
    An X-ray examination of the bowel using a contrast medium to assess changes in the structure of the bowel.
  3. Laboratory tests:
    • Blood tests: full blood count, markers of inflammation (C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate).
    • Stool tests: for occult blood and calprotectin (a marker of inflammation in the bowel).

Treatments for ulcerative colitis:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Aminosalicylates (mesalazine): used to reduce inflammation and maintain remission.
    • Corticosteroids: used to control acute flare-ups.
    • Immunosuppressants (azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine): to reduce the immune response and maintain remission.
    • Biological medicines (infliximab, adalimumab): targeted therapies for moderate and severe ulcerative colitis.
  2. Surgery:
    • Carried out where drug treatment is ineffective or serious complications develop (massive bleeding or perforation of the bowel, for example).
    • Proctocolectomy with ileoanal anastomosis: removal of the affected section of bowel followed by restoration of function.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An individual approach: a personal treatment plan based on thorough investigation and on the particular features of each patient's illness.
  • Multidisciplinary teams: gastroenterologists, surgeons, dietitians and psychologists working together for a comprehensive approach to treatment.
  • Access to advanced treatments: the use of advanced treatments, including biological medicines and targeted therapy, which considerably improve both the outlook and patients' quality of life.
  • Personalised support: support for patients at every stage of treatment, from diagnosis through to recovery and rehabilitation.
  • Thorough support during remission: planning of diet and medication and regular medical check-ups to maintain health and prevent relapse.

Treatment of ulcerative colitis in Israel aims to achieve lasting remission and a considerable improvement in patients' quality of life, giving them access to the most effective and modern treatments.

fields.title: Neuralgia
fields.bodyHtml:
Neuralgia: advanced treatment in Israel

Neuralgia is a condition characterised by sharp, piercing, shooting pain along the affected nerve. Israel uses modern approaches to the diagnosis and treatment of neuralgia that relieve pain and improve patients' quality of life.

Diagnosis of neuralgia:

  1. Medical examination and history
    The doctor assesses the symptoms and the history of the illness and carries out a physical examination.
  2. Neurological examination
    Testing of sensation, muscle strength and reflexes to identify the affected nerve.
  3. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    Used to image the nerves and surrounding tissues and look for the cause of the neuralgia.
  4. Electromyography (EMG) and nerve conduction studies
    Tests that help assess nerve function and identify damage.

Treatments for neuralgia in Israel:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Anti-inflammatory medicines.
    • Anti-epileptic medicines, such as gabapentin or pregabalin, to control neuropathic pain.
    • Antidepressants to reduce the pain.
  2. Physiotherapy:
    • The use of heat or cold to relieve pain.
    • Specific exercises to improve mobility and reduce tension in the affected nerves.
  3. Injection therapy:
    • Nerve blocks using steroids and anaesthetics around the affected nerve for temporary pain relief.
  4. Surgery:
    • Where conservative treatment is ineffective, minimally invasive surgery may be recommended to remove the cause of pressure on the nerve.
  5. Minimally invasive procedures:
    • Microsurgery.
    • Neurostimulation.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • Highly qualified specialists: Israeli doctors have extensive experience in diagnosing and treating various forms of neuralgia.
  • Modern equipment: Israeli medical institutions are equipped with advanced technology, which allows accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach: Every patient is given a personalised treatment plan that takes account of their particular needs and the features of their condition.
  • An integrated approach: Combining different treatments provides a comprehensive approach to managing pain and restoring function.

Treatment of neuralgia in Israel aims to minimise pain and restore patients' normal activity, using a multidisciplinary approach and the latest medical innovations.

fields.title: Orthopaedic oncology
fields.bodyHtml:
Orthopaedic oncology is the field of medicine concerned with diagnosing and treating tumours of the bones and soft tissues. In Israel, patients are offered innovative treatments for cancers of the musculoskeletal system based on the latest scientific research and clinical experience.

Diagnosis in orthopaedic oncology

  1. MRI and CT
    Highly accurate imaging methods that produce detailed pictures of bone and soft tissue, helping establish the size and extent of the tumour.
  2. X-ray
    A traditional but important method of assessing the state of the bones.
  3. Biopsy
    The key method for obtaining an accurate diagnosis, involving the taking of a sample of tumour tissue for histological examination.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  4. PET-CT
    A modern diagnostic method combining positron emission tomography and computed tomography to assess the metabolic activity of tumours and search for metastases in the body.
  5. Laboratory tests
    These include a full blood count, biochemical tests and measurement of specific tumour markers.

Treatment in orthopaedic oncology

  1. Surgery
    The aim of the operation is to remove the tumour while preserving function as far as possible and minimising the loss of healthy tissue. Reconstructive techniques and joint replacement may be used.
  2. Radiotherapy
    Used to destroy remaining cancer cells and reduce the risk of recurrence. It may be given either before or after surgery.
  3. Chemotherapy
    Used to treat certain types of tumour, particularly where metastases are present.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    The newest treatments, aimed at destroying cancer cells with minimal harm to healthy tissue.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach: leading specialists from various fields of medicine work together to develop an individual treatment plan.
  • Advanced technology and treatments: patients have access to the most modern methods of diagnosis and treatment, which improves the chances of successful treatment and of preserving function.
  • Highly qualified specialists: Israel is home to internationally recognised experts in orthopaedic oncology, which guarantees a high standard of medical care.
  • An individual approach to every patient: treatment is planned with every feature of the case in mind, aiming to preserve the patient's quality of life as far as possible.

Orthopaedic oncology in Israel combines highly qualified doctors, innovative treatments and an individualised approach to every patient, delivering the best results in the fight against cancers of the musculoskeletal system.

fields.title: Osteoporosis
fields.bodyHtml:
Osteoporosis: modern treatment in Israel

Osteoporosis is a chronic condition characterised by reduced bone density, which makes the bones more fragile and increases the risk of fractures. The condition often develops unnoticed, without obvious symptoms, and is only discovered after the first fracture.

Diagnosis of osteoporosis

Modern methods of diagnosing osteoporosis in Israel include:

  1. Bone density scan (DXA): The main method of measuring bone density, which allows the degree of osteoporosis to be established precisely.
  2. X-ray: Used to identify fractures and deformities of the bones.
  3. Laboratory tests: Blood tests to measure levels of calcium, phosphorus and vitamin D, and markers of bone metabolism.
  4. CT and MRI: Used for a more detailed study of bone structure and to identify possible complications.

Treatments for osteoporosis

Treatment of osteoporosis in Israel aims to slow the progression of the condition, improve the state of the bone tissue and prevent fractures. The main treatments include:

  1. Drug therapy:
    • Bisphosphonates: Medicines that slow the breakdown of bone tissue.
    • Calcitonin: A hormone that helps regulate calcium levels in the body.
    • Vitamin D and calcium: To strengthen the bones and improve their density.
    • Hormone therapy: Particularly effective for women after the menopause.
    • Antibody treatment (denosumab): A medicine that blocks the breakdown of bone tissue.
  2. Physical therapy and rehabilitation:
    • Exercises to strengthen the bones and muscles.
    • Physical activity programmes to improve balance and coordination, which helps prevent falls.
  3. Dietary therapy:
    • Advice on a diet rich in calcium and vitamin D.
    • Consultations with dietitians to draw up individual eating plans.
  4. Minimally invasive surgical methods:
    • Kyphoplasty and vertebroplasty: Procedures to restore the spine after compression fractures.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  1. A high standard of medicine: Israeli clinics are equipped with modern technology and use advanced methods of diagnosing and treating osteoporosis.
  2. Qualified specialists: Treatment is carried out by experienced doctors specialising in conditions of the skeletal system.
  3. An individual approach: Every patient is given a personalised treatment plan that takes account of their individual circumstances and needs.
  4. A comprehensive approach: Treatment includes not only medicines but also physiotherapy, dietary therapy, rehabilitation and psychological support.
  5. International standards: Israeli medical institutions meet high international standards of quality and safety in treatment.

Treatment of osteoporosis in Israel combines advanced medical technology with highly qualified staff, which ensures that therapeutic and surgical interventions are both effective and safe.

fields.title: Osteosarcoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Effective treatment of osteosarcoma in Israel

Osteosarcoma is an aggressive form of bone cancer that requires a comprehensive and innovative approach to treatment. Advanced methods of diagnosis and therapy are available in Israel, delivering a high level of effectiveness and patient-centred care.

Diagnosis of osteosarcoma:

  1. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the bones:
    These allow the position and nature of the tumour to be established precisely.
  2. Biopsy:
    Taking a tissue sample for laboratory analysis to confirm the diagnosis and establish the genetic characteristics of the tumour.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Laboratory tests:
    Basic blood tests indicating cancer activity.
  4. PET-CT:
    Provides a detailed picture of the metabolic activity of the tumour and of any metastases.

Treatments for osteosarcoma:

  1. Surgery:
    • Radical resection of the tumour: Removal of the tumour together with surrounding healthy tissue to prevent recurrence.
    • Limb-sparing surgery: The possibility of preserving the function of the limb, provided the tumour can be removed completely.
  2. Chemotherapy:
    • Chemotherapy before surgery: Used to shrink the tumour and destroy any metastases.
    • Chemotherapy after surgery: Given to destroy any remaining cancer cells and prevent recurrence.
  3. Radiotherapy:
    • Radiotherapy before surgery: Used to shrink the tumour in preparation for surgical removal.
    • Radiotherapy after surgery: Given to destroy any remaining cancer cells and prevent recurrence.
  4. New treatments:
    • Immunotherapy: The use of the patient's own immune system to fight the cancer cells.
    • Targeted therapy: The use of medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells.
    • Stereotactic radiosurgery: Highly precise irradiation of tumours with minimal effect on healthy tissue.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An integrated approach to treatment: A team of specialists in oncology, surgery and radiotherapy works together to develop individualised treatment plans.
  • The use of advanced technology: Israeli medical centres are equipped with modern devices that allow accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • Multidisciplinary case conferences: Regular meetings of specialists to discuss complex cases and take well-founded treatment decisions.

Treatment of osteosarcoma in Israel is based on advanced methods and scientific progress, which makes it possible to achieve high survival rates and give patients the best possible quality of life.

fields.title: Obesity
fields.bodyHtml:
Obesity: a comprehensive approach to treatment in Israel

Obesity is a serious condition that can lead to many accompanying illnesses, such as type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, cardiovascular disease and many others. Israel uses a comprehensive approach to treating obesity that includes not only changes to lifestyle and drug treatment but also advanced surgical techniques.

Diagnosis of obesity:

  1. Body mass index (BMI) measurement
    Helps establish the degree of obesity.
  2. Anthropometric measurements
    Assessment of waist circumference to establish the risk of developing accompanying conditions.
  3. Laboratory tests
    Blood tests for the lipid profile, glucose and insulin levels and other metabolic markers.
  4. Assessment of accompanying conditions
    Diagnosis of illnesses associated with obesity.

Treatment of obesity in Israel:

  1. Individualised diet and exercise programmes
    A diet and exercise plan adapted to each patient's needs.
  2. Drug treatment
    The use of medicines to correct metabolic disturbances and control appetite.
  3. Gastric banding
    A minimally invasive procedure in which a silicone band is placed around the upper part of the stomach, limiting the amount of food that can be eaten at one time.
  4. Gastric bypass
    Surgery in which part of the stomach and small intestine is bypassed, which reduces the absorption of food and promotes weight loss.
  5. Laparoscopic techniques using the da Vinci surgical robot
    The newest surgical techniques for treating obesity, which allow operations to be carried out with great precision and minimal intervention, considerably shortening the recovery period.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A personalised approach
    Every patient is given an individual treatment plan that takes account of their particular medical and personal needs.
  • A multidisciplinary team of specialists
    Doctors, dietitians, psychologists and surgeons work together to offer the most effective treatment.
  • Access to advanced medical technology
    Including laparoscopic operations with the da Vinci surgical robot, which makes procedures less traumatic, allows rapid recovery and delivers excellent long-term results.
  • A comprehensive approach to treatment
    Not only weight loss but also improvement in general health, control of accompanying conditions and a better quality of life for patients.

Treatment of obesity in Israel aims to achieve a lasting result, including considerable weight loss, normalisation of metabolic markers and an improvement in patients' general wellbeing.

fields.title: Inguinal hernia
fields.bodyHtml:
Inguinal hernia: advanced treatment in Israel

An inguinal hernia is the protrusion of part of the internal organs through a weakened area in the groin. It is one of the most common types of hernia and requires surgery to prevent complications such as strangulation. Modern and effective treatments for inguinal hernia are available in Israel.

Diagnosis of an inguinal hernia:

  1. Clinical examination
    The doctor carries out a physical examination, during which the hernia may be detected when the patient coughs or strains.
  2. Ultrasound scan
    Helps confirm the presence of a hernia and assess its size and contents.
  3. Herniography
    A contrast X-ray examination, rarely used but possible for diagnosing complex cases.

Treatments for an inguinal hernia:

  1. Surgery:
    • Open hernia repair: The traditional method, involving an incision in the groin, returning the contents of the hernia and strengthening the hernia opening using the patient's own tissue or a synthetic mesh.
    • Laparoscopic hernia repair: A minimally invasive operation carried out through small punctures using special instruments and a video camera. It reduces pain after the operation and shortens the recovery period.
  2. Non-surgical measures:
    • Wearing a truss or hernia belt: A temporary measure that may be used before an operation or where surgery is not possible.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • Highly qualified surgeons: Israeli surgeons have extensive experience in both traditional and laparoscopic operations.
  • The use of modern materials and technology: The use of high-quality synthetic meshes and minimally invasive techniques, which reduce the risk of recurrence and speed up recovery.
  • An individual approach to choosing the treatment: Surgery is planned taking account of the patient's individual circumstances, lifestyle and any accompanying conditions.
  • Comprehensive aftercare: Includes advice on rehabilitation, diet and physical activity to prevent the hernia recurring.

Treatment of an inguinal hernia in Israel aims at rapid recovery and at minimising the risk of future complications. Patients receive comprehensive medical support, from accurate diagnosis through to rehabilitation after the operation, which allows them to return to an active life confident of a successful outcome.

fields.title: Pancreatitis
fields.bodyHtml:
Pancreatitis: advanced treatment in Israel

Pancreatitis is inflammation of the pancreas, which may take an acute or a chronic form and requires active medical intervention. Israel uses modern diagnostic and treatment approaches aimed at removing the causes of the condition, easing symptoms and preventing complications.

Diagnosis of pancreatitis:

  1. Laboratory tests:
    • Blood tests: Measurement of amylase and lipase levels, which may be raised in pancreatitis.
    • Full blood count (CBC) to assess the inflammatory process.
  2. Imaging:
    • Ultrasound scan: The initial investigation, to assess the structure of the pancreas.
    • Computed tomography (CT): A detailed image to assess the extent of the inflammation and identify possible complications.
    • Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP): Used to image the bile and pancreatic ducts.

Treatments for pancreatitis:

  1. Conservative treatment:
    • Hydration: Intravenous fluids to maintain the balance of water and electrolytes.
    • Observation in hospital: To monitor the patient's condition and prevent complications.
    • Diet: A low-fat diet or temporary fasting to reduce the load on the pancreas.
    • Painkillers: To relieve pain.
  2. Endoscopic treatment:
    • Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP): May be used to clear obstructions in the pancreatic ducts, such as stones or strictures.
  3. Surgery:
    • Used in chronic pancreatitis to remove damaged areas of the pancreas, or for complications of acute pancreatitis such as abscesses or pseudocysts.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: A team of specialists including gastroenterologists, surgeons and intensive care doctors works together to provide a comprehensive approach to treatment.
  • Advanced medical equipment: World-leading technology and techniques that allow pancreatitis to be diagnosed accurately and treated effectively at any stage.
  • Individualised therapy: Treatment plans drawn up with each patient's individual circumstances, condition and needs in mind.
  • A high standard of patient care: All-round support for patients during and after treatment, including advice on diet and lifestyle to prevent further episodes.

Treatment of pancreatitis in Israel aims at a rapid improvement in patients' condition and at minimising the risk of long-term complications, which aids recovery and helps maintain quality of life.

fields.title: Squamous cell carcinoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Squamous cell carcinoma: advanced treatment in Israel

Squamous cell carcinoma is a type of cancer that develops from the flat cells of the epithelium and occurs frequently in the skin, the lungs, the head and neck, and the body and neck of the womb. Israel uses modern approaches to treating this condition, including advanced methods of diagnosis, surgery, radiotherapy and chemotherapy.

Diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma:

  1. Biopsy: The main diagnostic method, providing tumour tissue for histological examination.
  2. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI): Used to assess how far the cancer has spread and whether there are metastases.
  3. PET-CT: An effective method for establishing the activity of the cancer and its metabolic activity at an early stage.
  4. Laboratory tests: Blood tests to establish general health and organ function, and specific cancer markers.

Treatments for squamous cell carcinoma:

Treatment of squamous cell carcinoma of the body and neck of the womb:
  • Surgery: Radical hysterectomy with removal of the lymph nodes.
  • Radiotherapy and chemotherapy: Used in combination to destroy cancer cells and prevent recurrence.
Treatment of squamous cell carcinoma of the skin:
  • Local surgical removal: Excision of the tumour together with healthy tissue around it.
  • Mohs micrographic surgery: Precise removal of the cancer layer by layer, preserving as much healthy tissue as possible.
  • Cryotherapy and photodynamic therapy: For superficial forms of the cancer.
Treatment of squamous cell carcinoma of the lung:
  • Surgery: Lobectomy or pneumonectomy to remove part or all of the lung.
  • Chemotherapy and radiotherapy: For the treatment of local and metastatic cancer.
Treatment of squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx:
  • Laryngectomy: Partial or complete removal of the larynx, depending on the stage of the disease.
  • Radiotherapy and chemotherapy: Often used as an alternative to surgery in order to preserve the voice.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Oncologists, surgeons, radiologists and other specialists work together to develop individual treatment plans.
  • Innovative treatments: Access to the latest medical developments and technology, which allows the most effective and safest treatments to be used.
  • Highly qualified doctors: Israeli specialists are internationally recognised and have rich experience in treating various forms of cancer, including squamous cell carcinoma.

Treatment of squamous cell carcinoma in Israel aims to give patients the longest and best possible life, using a comprehensive and individualised approach.

fields.title: Heart defects
fields.bodyHtml:
Heart defects: advanced treatment in Israel

Advanced diagnosis of heart defects:

  1. Clinical examination and history: It is important to establish the type and severity of the symptoms and whether there are any accompanying conditions.
  2. Echocardiography: An ultrasound examination that allows the structure of the heart to be imaged and the function of the valves assessed.
  3. Electrocardiogram (ECG): A recording of the electrical activity of the heart, which may indicate abnormalities associated with heart defects.
  4. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the heart: Gives a detailed picture of the structure of the heart and helps establish the anatomical features of the defect.
  5. Cardiac catheterisation and angiography: Allow assessment of the pressure in the chambers of the heart and the state of the coronary vessels.
  6. Laboratory tests:
    • Blood tests: full blood count, biochemistry, markers of inflammation.
    • Specific tests to identify infectious agents where infective endocarditis is suspected.

Treatments for heart defects:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Aimed at controlling symptoms, improving the working of the heart and preventing complications.
  2. Surgery:
    • Valve repair or valve replacement with artificial or biological prostheses.
    • Correction of defects of the ventricular and atrial septum.
  3. Interventional cardiology:
    • Minimally invasive methods, including balloon valvuloplasty and closure of defects of the ventricular and atrial septum through a catheter.
  4. Rehabilitation:
    • A comprehensive recovery programme after surgery or intensive care, aimed at improving quality of life and returning the patient to normal activity.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, rehabilitation specialists and others combine their efforts to create the most effective treatment plan.
  • An individual treatment plan: Every feature of the patient's condition is taken into account in order to achieve the best results.
  • Access to the newest technology: The use of the latest medical advances in diagnosing and treating heart defects.
  • A high quality of medical care: A distinguishing feature of Israeli medicine, offering strong prospects of successful treatment and recovery.

Treatment of heart defects in Israel aims at an active improvement in the patient's condition and their return to a full life, minimising risks and possible complications.

fields.title: Prostatitis
fields.bodyHtml:
Prostatitis: modern treatment in Israel

Prostatitis is inflammation of the prostate gland, which can cause various symptoms including pain, problems passing urine and sexual difficulties. Israel uses comprehensive and innovative approaches to the diagnosis and treatment of prostatitis, aimed at removing the causes of the condition and easing symptoms.

Diagnosis of prostatitis:

  1. History and physical examination
    Includes a detailed account of the patient's symptoms and a rectal examination of the prostate gland.
  2. Urine tests
    Help identify the presence of infection.
  3. Prostatic fluid
    Analysis for inflammatory cells and bacteria.
  4. Ultrasound scan
    Used to assess the size and structure of the prostate gland and to identify any stones or cysts.
  5. PSA test (prostate-specific antigen)
    Helps rule out prostate cancer.

Treatments for prostatitis in Israel:

  1. Antibiotic treatment
    Used in bacterial prostatitis; the choice of medicine is based on sensitivity testing.
  2. Anti-inflammatory medicines
    Prescribed to reduce pain and inflammation.
  3. Alpha blockers
    Used to improve the flow of urine where there are symptoms of difficulty passing urine.
  4. Physiotherapy
    Includes magnetic therapy, laser therapy, heat treatment and prostate massage, aimed at improving circulation in the pelvic area and relieving spasm.
  5. Minimally invasive procedures
    Used to relieve congestion in the prostate gland.
  6. Lifestyle changes
    Advice on diet, increasing physical activity and managing stress.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An individual approach to every patient
    A treatment plan drawn up with the particular course of the illness in mind.
  • Highly qualified specialists
    Israel's leading urologists have extensive experience in treating prostatitis and other conditions of the prostate gland.
  • Innovative treatments
    The use of advanced technology and techniques to achieve the best results.
  • A comprehensive approach
    A combination of medicines, physiotherapy and lifestyle advice to address both the causes and the symptoms of the condition.

Treatment of prostatitis in Israel aims to relieve symptoms quickly, remove the causes of the inflammation and prevent recurrence, allowing patients to return to normal life. Modern techniques and an individual approach to treatment make the therapy highly effective and minimise the risk of possible complications, which makes Israel one of the leading destinations for urological care at international level.

fields.title: Umbilical hernia
fields.bodyHtml:
Umbilical hernia: advanced treatment in Israel

An umbilical hernia is the protrusion of part of the internal organs through a weakened area around the navel. Israel uses both traditional and innovative methods to treat umbilical hernias, delivering high effectiveness and a minimal risk of complications.

Diagnosis of an umbilical hernia:

  1. Clinical examination
    The main diagnostic method, involving inspection and palpation of the area around the navel, particularly when the abdominal muscles are tensed.
  2. Ultrasound scan
    Allows assessment of the size of the hernia opening and the contents of the hernia sac.
  3. Computed tomography (CT)
    Used for detailed imaging of the abdominal cavity and to establish the contents of the hernia in complex or unusual cases.

Treatments for an umbilical hernia:

  1. Conservative treatment:
    • Used rarely, and mainly as a temporary measure or in preparation for surgery. It involves wearing a truss or support belt to reduce pressure on the hernia.
  2. Surgery:
    • Open hernia repair: Used rarely (the second option is usually chosen); it involves an incision over the hernia, returning the contents of the hernia to the abdominal cavity and closing the hernia opening with sutures.
    • Laparoscopic surgery (hernioplasty): A minimally invasive procedure through small incisions, using a camera and special instruments to reduce the hernia and place a mesh implant that strengthens the abdominal wall.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An individual approach: The choice of treatment is based on the patient's individual circumstances, the size of the hernia and any accompanying conditions.
  • Highly qualified specialists: Operations are carried out by experienced surgeons specialising in minimally invasive techniques.
  • Modern equipment: The use of advanced technology and materials, such as biocompatible meshes, which reduce the risk of the hernia recurring and aid rapid recovery.
  • A comprehensive approach to recovery: All-round support during rehabilitation, including advice on physical activity and diet to prevent hernias recurring.

Modern treatment considerably improves quality of life after the operation, with little pain, rapid recovery and a low risk of recurrence. Patients receive all-round support at every stage of treatment, from preparation for surgery through to rehabilitation afterwards, which is the key to a successful outcome.

fields.title: Umbilical and other abdominal hernias
fields.bodyHtml:
Introduction

Abdominal hernias — umbilical, inguinal and others — are conditions in which internal organs protrude through weak areas or openings in the abdominal wall. These hernias can cause pain and discomfort and may require medical intervention. In this article we look at the methods of diagnosing and treating abdominal hernias, and at the advantages of seeking help in Israel.

Methods of diagnosis

Diagnosis of abdominal hernias begins with a thorough medical examination and the use of modern methods to establish the nature and extent of the hernia:

  • Clinical examination: the doctor carries out a physical examination, identifying any protruding area and checking for pulsation.
  • Ultrasound scan of the abdomen: an ultrasound examination allows the area of the abdominal hernia to be imaged and its size and nature established.
  • Computed tomography (CT): a method that gives a more detailed picture of the hernia and the tissues around it.

Methods of treatment

Treatment of abdominal hernias depends on the type of hernia and how far it has developed:

  • Surgery: where an abdominal hernia is significant, an operation may be required to restore normal anatomy and strengthen the weak area.
  • The use of a hernia truss: a temporary solution to hold the hernia and reduce discomfort.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

Israel provides high-quality medical care using advanced methods and technology. The advantages of treating abdominal hernias in Israel include:

  • Expert specialists: medical institutions in Israel work with experienced surgeons and gastroenterologists specialising in the treatment of abdominal hernias.
  • Modern methods: doctors in Israel use advanced methods of diagnosis and surgical treatment, which helps achieve the best results.
  • An individual approach: treatment in Israel is adapted to the individual needs of the patient, ensuring the best solution.

Conclusion

Abdominal hernias are conditions that require competent diagnosis and proper treatment. Modern diagnostic methods, surgical approaches and experienced specialists allow patients to overcome the discomfort and restore their health. Seeking help in Israel gives access to quality medical care and advanced treatments, which helps restore comfort and improve quality of life.

fields.title: Cancer of the duodenum
fields.bodyHtml:
Cancer of the duodenum: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the duodenum is a rare condition affecting the first section of the small intestine. Israeli clinics offer innovative approaches to diagnosing and treating this type of cancer, giving patients access to advanced medical technology and the international experience of their specialists.

Diagnosis of cancer of the duodenum

  1. Endoscopy with biopsy (gastroscopy)
    An endoscopic examination allows the inner surface of the duodenum to be seen and tissue samples to be taken for histological analysis
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed).
  2. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    These imaging methods are used to assess the stage of the disease and identify metastases.
  3. Laboratory tests
    These include a full blood count, biochemical tests and tumour marker tests that help in diagnosing the cancer.
  4. PET-CT
    A method that allows the metabolic activity of the tumour to be assessed and metastases in other organs to be identified.

Treatment of cancer of the duodenum

  1. Surgery
    Radical removal of the tumour is the main treatment. Depending on the position and size of the tumour, part of the duodenum and neighbouring organs may need to be removed.
  2. Chemotherapy
    Used to destroy cancer cells, particularly where metastases are present, or to shrink the tumour before surgery.
  3. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    The newest treatments, aimed at destroying cancer cells with minimal effect on healthy tissue.
  4. Radiotherapy
    Sometimes used in combination with chemotherapy to control the disease and reduce symptoms.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Israel's leading clinics bring in specialists from various fields to develop a comprehensive treatment plan.
  • Innovative treatments: Patients have access to the latest advances in oncology, including targeted therapy and immunotherapy.
  • Highly qualified specialists: The experience and knowledge of Israeli doctors make treatment highly effective and provide support at every stage.
  • An individual approach: Treatment is planned with the particular features of each case in mind, which makes it possible to achieve the best results.

Choosing Israel for the treatment of cancer of the duodenum gives patients a chance of successful treatment thanks to access to advanced medical technology and the deep professionalism of its doctors.

fields.title: Cancer of the eye socket
fields.bodyHtml:
Cancer of the eye socket (an orbital tumour) is a rare and dangerous condition that requires accurate diagnosis and highly effective treatment. It can affect various structures of the eye socket, including the muscles, nerves and blood vessels, which leads to serious impairment of vision and of the functioning of the eye.

Diagnosis of cancer of the eye socket

  1. Detailed review of the medical history: The doctor talks to the patient about their medical history, including their symptoms, any preceding illness, previous conditions and treatment.
  2. Visual examination: The doctor examines the patient's eyes, noting any changes in the structure of the eye socket and the surrounding tissues.
  3. Ophthalmoscopy: Using special instruments, the doctor assesses the state of the optic nerve, the vessels of the fundus and the retina.
  4. Computed tomography (CT): Produces detailed images of the structure of the eye socket, reveals the presence of a tumour and allows its size and position to be assessed.
  5. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI): Used for a more precise assessment of the structure of the tumour and its relationship to the surrounding tissues.
  6. Biopsy: Taking a sample of tumour tissue for histological examination, which helps establish the type of tumour and how malignant it is.
  7. Ultrasound examination of the eye: Allows assessment of the structure of the eyeball and the optic nerve and identification of possible changes in the eye socket.
  8. Doppler ultrasound of the vessels of the eye: Used to assess the blood supply in the vessels of the eye and identify possible abnormalities associated with cancer of the eye socket.

Treatment of cancer of the eye socket

Cancer of the eye socket is treated in Israel using the most modern and innovative methods. The main treatments include:

  1. Surgery: The main treatment, aimed at removing the tumour. Depending on the size and position of the tumour, various types of operation are possible, including minimally invasive techniques.
  2. Radiotherapy: Used to destroy cancer cells, to shrink the tumour before an operation, or to prevent recurrence after surgery. Modern equipment is used to deliver precise and safe radiotherapy.
  3. Chemotherapy: The use of medicines to destroy cancer cells. It may be used on its own or in combination with surgery and radiotherapy.
  4. Immunotherapy: A modern treatment aimed at activating the patient's immune system to fight the cancer cells, using medicines that strengthen the immune response to the tumour.
  5. Targeted therapy: The use of medicines that act on specific molecules involved in the growth and development of cancer cells. This method minimises damage to healthy tissue.

Advantages of treating cancer of the eye socket in Israel

  1. A high level of medical expertise: Israel is home to leading specialists in oncology and ophthalmology with many years of experience and unique skills.
  2. Modern equipment: Clinics are equipped with advanced diagnostic and treatment devices, which allows highly accurate investigation and effective treatment.
  3. An individual approach: Every patient is given an individual treatment plan that takes account of the nature of the condition and their general health.
  4. Innovative treatments: The use of the most modern methods and medicines, including immunotherapy and targeted therapy.
  5. Comfortable conditions: Patients can expect a high standard of comfort and service during treatment and rehabilitation.

Treatment of cancer of the eye socket in Israel gives patients access to high-quality medical care and considerably improves the outlook.

fields.title: Breast cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Breast cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Breast cancer is one of the most common cancers in women worldwide. Israel has developed and successfully applies advanced approaches to diagnosing and treating this disease, combining innovative medical technology with highly qualified specialists, including the use of tumour marking for precise guidance during treatment.

Diagnosis of breast cancer

  1. Mammography
    The main method of early detection of breast cancer, allowing tumours to be identified at an early stage.
  2. Ultrasound scan
    Used for further examination of areas of the breast that have raised suspicion on mammography.
  3. Breast MRI
    A highly informative method, particularly recommended for women at high risk of developing breast cancer.
  4. Biopsy
    Taking a tissue sample for histological analysis is the definitive way of confirming the diagnosis.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  5. PET-CT
    A method combining PET and CT to assess accurately how far the cancer has spread, determine the stage of the disease and judge the effectiveness of treatment.
  6. MRI-guided tumour marking
    This method allows the position of the tumour in the breast to be established precisely, which makes planning treatment and surgery easier.

Treatment of breast cancer

  1. Surgery
    Includes lumpectomy (removal of the tumour while preserving the breast) and mastectomy (removal of the whole breast). The choice depends on the stage of the disease and the patient's wishes.
  2. Radiotherapy
    Given after surgery to destroy any remaining cancer cells.
  3. Chemotherapy
    Used both before and after surgery to reduce the risk of recurrence and destroy cancer cells in the body.
  4. Hormone therapy
    Prescribed for patients with hormone-dependent breast cancer, to block the effect of oestrogen on the cancer cells.
  5. Targeted therapy
    Involves the use of medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells.
  6. Immunotherapy
    The newest treatment, stimulating the body's immune system to fight the cancer cells.

Why patients choose Israel

Israel attracts patients from all over the world for a number of reasons:

  • Multidisciplinary teams of specialists, including oncologists, surgeons, radiologists and geneticists.
  • An individual approach to the treatment of every patient, taking account of every aspect of her health.
  • Access to innovative treatments and the latest clinical research.
  • A high standard of medical care and attention to patients' comfort.

Innovative approaches and highly qualified specialists make Israel one of the world leaders in the treatment of breast cancer, offering patients not only treatment but hope of a full recovery.

fields.title: Lip cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Lip cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Lip cancer is a malignant growth affecting the outer layers of the skin or the mucous membrane of the lips. In Israel, patients are offered an advanced and comprehensive approach to treating this disease, delivering high effectiveness and a minimal risk of recurrence.

Diagnosis of lip cancer

  1. Visual examination and palpation
    The first diagnostic method, allowing abnormalities on the lips to be detected.
  2. Biopsy
    Taking a tissue sample from the suspicious area for histological examination.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Laboratory tests and tumour markers
    Blood tests are carried out to establish general indicators of health and specific biomarkers associated with cancer.
  4. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    These help assess how deeply the tumour has penetrated and whether there are metastases.
  5. Ultrasound scan
    Used to assess the state of the regional lymph nodes of the neck and the surrounding tissues.
  6. PET-CT for a comprehensive assessment
    This method makes it possible to assess not only the position and size of the tumour but also the metabolic activity of the tissue, which is critically important for staging the cancer and planning treatment.

Treatment of lip cancer

  1. Surgery
    The main treatment, aimed at removing the tumour together with enough surrounding healthy tissue to minimise the risk of recurrence.
  2. Radiotherapy
    May be given either before or after surgery to destroy any remaining cancer cells.
  3. Chemotherapy
    Used less often, mainly to treat advanced forms of lip cancer or metastases.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    The newest approaches to treatment, directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells and at activating the immune system to fight the tumour.

Why patients choose Israel

  • Highly qualified specialists
    Doctors in Israel have international experience and constantly develop their skills through scientific research.
  • An individual approach
    Every patient is given a personalised treatment programme that takes account of every feature of their condition and their preferences.
  • Advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment
    The use of the most modern technology and treatments makes the therapy as effective as possible.
  • Multidisciplinary teams
    Specialists of various kinds take part in treatment, which ensures a comprehensive approach to fighting the disease.

Israeli clinics offer patients with lip cancer access to advanced medical technology and highly qualified care, which makes it possible to achieve the best treatment results and considerably improve quality of life after therapy.

fields.title: Bone cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Bone cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Bone cancer is a serious condition that may take the form of primary bone tumours or of metastases from other parts of the body. Israel uses innovative methods of diagnosing and treating bone cancer, aimed at improving both the outlook and patients' quality of life.

Diagnosis of bone cancer:

  1. X-rays:
    The first method for identifying changes in the structure of the bones.
  2. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    Assesses how far the bones and soft tissues are affected.
  3. Computed tomography (CT):
    Used for a more detailed study of bone structure and to identify small lesions.
  4. Bone scan:
    A radioactive substance is given to identify cancer cells in the bones.
  5. PET-CT:
    An integrated approach combining PET and CT to assess the metabolic activity of the tumour and search for metastases.
  6. Biopsy:
    Definitive confirmation of the presence of cancer cells in the bone.

Treatments for bone cancer:

  1. Surgery:
    • Resection of the tumour: Removal of the tumour together with some of the surrounding healthy tissue.
    • Limb-sparing surgery: A technique that allows the limb to be preserved when the tumour is removed.
    • Amputation: Used where the tumour is too large or too awkwardly placed for the limb to be preserved.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • Used to destroy cancer cells and reduce the risk of recurrence, particularly after surgery or where an operation is not possible.
  3. Chemotherapy:
    • Used to treat bone cancer, particularly in aggressive and metastatic forms of the disease.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy:
    • The use of modern medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the tumour.
    • Immunotherapy to activate the patient's own immune system to fight the cancer.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Specialists from different fields of medicine work together to create the most effective treatment plan.
  • Advanced medical equipment: The use of the latest advances in medical technology and treatment techniques.
  • An individual approach: Treatment plans are adapted to the particular patient, taking account of the stage of the disease, general health and other important factors.

Treatment of bone cancer in Israel aims for maximum effectiveness, the preservation of function and quality of life, and the minimisation of side effects and the risk of recurrence.

fields.title: Lung cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Lung cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Lung cancer is one of the most serious cancers and requires a comprehensive and individualised approach to treatment. Israeli clinics offer advanced methods of diagnosing and treating lung cancer, combining highly qualified specialists, modern technology and an individual approach to every patient.

Diagnosis of lung cancer

  1. Computed tomography (CT)
    of the chest allows a tumour to be identified at an early stage.
  2. PET-CT
    allows tumours and metastases to be detected and their activity and extent assessed. It helps show how the tumour is responding to treatment.
  3. Bronchoscopy with biopsy
    makes it possible to obtain tissue samples for histological analysis.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  4. Laboratory tests
    include blood tests and cancer markers that help in diagnosis.
  5. Consultation with a specialist
    is needed to establish the best treatment strategy.

Treatment of lung cancer

  1. Surgery
    involves removing the tumour together with part of the lung. Israel uses both traditional operations and minimally invasive methods, including video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS).
  2. Chemotherapy
    is used to destroy cancer cells, both before and after surgery, and as the main treatment in advanced stages.
  3. Targeted therapy
    is directed at particular mutations in the cancer cells, which makes treatment more effective and produces fewer side effects.
  4. Immunotherapy activates the patient's own immune system to fight the cancer cells.
  5. Radiotherapy
    is used on its own and in combination with other treatments to destroy cancer cells and shrink the tumour.

Why patients choose Israel

Israel attracts patients from all over the world thanks to its advanced approach to treating lung cancer. Highly qualified specialists, the use of the latest medical technology and an individual approach to every patient offer strong prospects of successful treatment. Patients also value the comprehensive approach to treatment, with support at every stage — from diagnosis through to rehabilitation afterwards — and the opportunity to receive the newest therapies, take part in clinical trials and access innovative treatments that may not be available in other countries.
