fields.title: Uterine cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Uterine cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the womb accounts for a significant share of cancers in women. The latest medical advances are available in Israel, aimed at effective treatment and at improving patients' quality of life.

Diagnosis of uterine cancer

  1. Transvaginal ultrasound
    Gives more accurate images of the internal structure of the womb.
  2. Hysteroscopy:
    A miniature camera is introduced into the cavity of the womb through the vagina and cervix, allowing the doctor to examine the inner surface of the womb and take tissue samples for a biopsy.
  3. Biopsy:
    Examination of tissue samples, which confirms the presence of cancer cells.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  4. PET-CT
    Assesses how far the cancer has spread and whether there are metastases.
  5. Laboratory tests
    Full blood count, biochemistry and blood tests for the relevant tumour markers.
  6. Consultation with a specialist
    To develop an individual treatment strategy (treatment may begin with a consultation with an oncologist or a surgeon).

Treatments for uterine cancer

  1. Surgery
    Israel makes wide use of both traditional operations and minimally invasive surgical techniques. One example is surgery using the da Vinci robot, which allows the operation to be carried out with great precision and minimal risk to the patient. Hysterectomy (removal of the womb) is recommended depending on the stage and extent of the disease.
  2. Hormone therapy with progestin
    Used to slow the growth of the tumour, particularly in certain types of uterine cancer. This method can be effective as an addition to other treatments.
  3. Radiotherapy
    Includes external beam radiotherapy and brachytherapy (internal irradiation). These methods are aimed at destroying cancer cells and preventing the disease from recurring.
  4. Chemotherapy and radiotherapy
    A combination of these methods is often used to treat advanced stages of uterine cancer. Chemotherapy fights the cancer cells throughout the body, while radiotherapy is directed at destroying cells in a particular area.

Every treatment plan in Israel is drawn up carefully, taking account of many factors including the type of cancer, its stage, the patient's general health and her personal preferences. Particular attention is given not only to fighting the disease but also to preserving the patient's quality of life and to support and rehabilitation after treatment.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of uterine cancer

Israeli clinics are known for their advanced methods of treating uterine cancer, and attract patients from all over the world thanks to a number of key advantages:

  • Highly qualified specialists
    Israeli oncologists and gynaecologists have international experience and use the most modern approaches to treatment.
  • Advanced equipment
    The use of the newest technology, including the da Vinci robotic system, allows minimally invasive operations that speed up patients' recovery.
  • An individual approach
    Treatment is planned with each patient's particular circumstances in mind, which makes the therapy as effective as possible.
  • A multidisciplinary approach
    Specialists from various fields take part in treatment, which helps address the problem comprehensively.
  • Innovative treatments: Patients have access to the newest treatment protocols, including targeted therapy and immunotherapy.
  • Comprehensive support
    Care for patients at every stage of treatment, including help with arranging their stay and with rehabilitation.

These factors make Israel the preferred choice for those seeking effective, high-quality treatment for uterine cancer.

fields.title: Bladder cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Bladder cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Bladder cancer is one of the more common cancers. In Israel, patients are offered a comprehensive approach to treating this disease, combining innovative methods of diagnosis and treatment.

Diagnosis of bladder cancer:

  1. Laboratory tests:
    Full blood count, biochemistry, tumour markers and urine tests
  2. Cystoscopy:
    Visual examination of the inner surface of the bladder using a cystoscope.
  3. Ultrasound scan:
    Imaging of the bladder and detection of growths.
  4. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    Detailed assessment of the tumour, its size and extent.
  5. CT urography:
    CT with a contrast medium that concentrates in the urinary system, for highly accurate diagnosis.
  6. Biopsy or review of pathology material:
    Obtaining and analysing tissue samples to confirm the diagnosis.

Treatments for bladder cancer in Israel:

  • Transurethral resection (TUR) followed by intravesical chemotherapy:
    • The cost of the operation includes routine pre-operative preparation (ECG, chest X-ray, consultation with an anaesthetist), the surgical procedure and up to 2 days in hospital, consumables and equipment, express biopsy and pathology examination.
  • Radical resection of the bladder with simultaneous reconstruction:
    • Includes all the items of pre-operative preparation, the surgical procedure and up to 9 days in hospital. After discharge the patient must remain in Israel for 10 days for follow-up.
  • Ureteral reimplantation:
    • The cost of the operation includes routine pre-operative preparation, the surgical procedure and up to 5 days in hospital, together with the necessary consumables and express biopsy. After discharge it is recommended that the patient remain in Israel for follow-up for 10 days.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Oncologists, urologists, radiologists and surgeons combine their efforts to develop the best treatment strategy.
  • Advanced technology: The use of the most modern methods of diagnosis and treatment, delivering high accuracy and a minimal risk of complications.
  • An individualised treatment plan: Treatments are chosen with the stage of the disease, the patient's general health and their preferences in mind.
  • Comprehensive support: Including help with rehabilitation and psychological support at every stage of treatment.

Treatment of bladder cancer in Israel gives patients access to high-quality medical care and innovative treatments, which makes it possible to achieve the best results.

fields.title: Brain cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Brain cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Brain cancer covers various types of brain tumour, including primary tumours that begin in the brain and metastatic tumours that spread from other parts of the body. Israel is known for its innovative approaches to treating this complex disease, which improve both the outlook and patients' quality of life.

Diagnosis of brain cancer:

  1. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    The standard imaging method for establishing the size, shape and position of a tumour in the brain and how it relates to the structures around it.
  2. Computed tomography (CT):
    Used for a rapid assessment of the brain, particularly after injury or when MRI is not available.
  3. Positron emission tomography (PET):
    Helps check for and assess the spread of the disease.
  4. Biopsy:
    Carried out to obtain an accurate diagnosis of the type of brain cancer, its stage and how aggressive it is likely to be.

Treatments for brain cancer:

  1. Surgery:
    • Craniotomy: An open operation to remove the tumour, in which the surgeons aim to remove as little healthy tissue as possible.
    • Stereotactic biopsy: A minimally invasive method of taking a sample of the tumour using computer guidance.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • External beam radiotherapy: Uses high-energy beams to destroy the cancer cells.
    • Stereotactic radiosurgery: A technique that allows precise targeting of a tumour in the brain without the need for open surgery.
  3. Chemotherapy:
    • Used to destroy cancer cells and prevent them growing and spreading.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy:
    • Targeted medicines: Directed at particular abnormalities in the cancer cells.
    • Immunotherapy: Stimulates the body's own immune system to fight the cancer.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: A team of specialists including neurosurgeons, oncologists, radiologists and others ensures a comprehensive approach to every case.
  • Advanced medical equipment: The use of the latest advances in medical technology and treatment techniques.
  • An individual approach: Treatment plans are adapted to the particular patient, taking account of the stage of the disease, general health and other important factors.

Treatment of brain cancer in Israel aims for maximum effectiveness, the preservation of function and quality of life, and the minimisation of side effects and the risk of recurrence.

fields.title: Adrenal cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Adrenal cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Adrenal cancer is a rare cancer affecting the adrenal glands — small glands situated above the kidneys. In Israel, patients are offered a comprehensive approach to treating this disease, combining innovative methods of diagnosis and treatment in order to achieve the best results.

Diagnosis of adrenal cancer

  1. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    allow a detailed assessment of the adrenal glands and detection of a tumour.
  2. Biochemical tests of blood and urine
    identify the excess hormone production characteristic of some types of adrenal cancer.
  3. Biopsy
    followed by histological analysis of the tissue sample helps establish the type of tumour precisely
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed).
  4. PET-CT
    is used to identify metastases and assess how far the disease has spread.

Treatments for adrenal cancer

  1. Surgery
    remains the main treatment, involving removal of the tumour together with the adrenal gland.
  2. Radiotherapy
    may be used to reduce symptoms or control metastases.
  3. Chemotherapy
    is used to treat metastatic adrenal cancer, particularly in aggressive forms of the disease.
  4. Biological treatment
    includes medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells.
  5. Radiosurgery in Israel: the CyberKnife
    is an advanced technology that destroys tumour cells precisely and effectively with minimal effect on the surrounding healthy tissue.
  6. The newest developments
    in the treatment of adrenal cancer are innovative methods and medicines at the clinical trial stage, which gives patients access to the most modern therapies.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of adrenal cancer

  • A multidisciplinary approach ensures all-round assessment and treatment, including consultations with oncologists, surgeons, endocrinologists and other specialists.
  • Advanced technology and treatments, including the CyberKnife and biological therapy, make treatment highly effective.
  • Individualised treatment programmes are developed with the particular features of the disease and each patient's needs in mind.
  • Access to the newest developments and participation in clinical trials open up innovative treatments to patients.

Israeli clinics offer a wide range of treatment options for adrenal cancer, from traditional methods through to the latest innovations in oncology, which makes it possible to achieve the best possible results even in the most difficult cases.

fields.title: Liver cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Liver cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Liver cancer is a serious cancer that may arise as a primary disease of the liver or as the spread of another cancer. Israeli clinics offer innovative approaches to treating liver cancer. The combination of highly qualified specialists and the latest medical technology helps achieve the best results.

Diagnosis of liver cancer

  1. Ultrasound scan
    of the liver allows tumours or abnormalities in the structure of the liver to be detected.
  2. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    provide detailed images of the liver, helping establish the size and position of the tumour and whether there are metastases.
  3. Liver biopsy
    a procedure in which a sample of liver tissue is taken for histological examination. It allows the type of cancer to be diagnosed precisely
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed).
  4. Laboratory tests, including blood tests for tumour markers (AFP) and liver function tests, help assess how the liver is working and whether cancer cells are present.
  5. PET-CT is used for a more precise assessment of the stage of the cancer and to identify metastases in other organs.

Treatments for liver cancer

  1. Surgery,
    including liver resection, is the preferred treatment for localised forms of liver cancer.
  2. Liver transplant
    is considered as an option for patients with severe liver damage or where other treatments are ineffective.
  3. Local ablative treatment,
    including radiofrequency ablation (RFA) and microwave ablation. Used to destroy cancer cells in the liver.
  4. Transarterial chemoembolisation (TACE) and radioembolisation
    are treatments in which medicines or radioactive particles are delivered directly to the tumour through the blood vessels.
  5. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    offer new approaches to treating liver cancer, directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells and at activating the body's immune system.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of liver cancer

  • Advanced medical technology and highly qualified specialists
    ensure accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach to every patient
    makes it possible to design treatment that best matches their needs and state of health.
  • Innovative treatments,
    including the latest advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy, give patients access to the most modern and effective methods.
  • Comprehensive support for patients at every stage of treatment, from diagnosis through to rehabilitation and follow-up.

Israeli clinics offer a comprehensive, multidisciplinary approach to the treatment of liver cancer, aiming to extend life as far as possible and improve patients' quality of life.

fields.title: Oesophageal cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Cancer of the oesophagus is a malignant growth developing in the tissue of the oesophagus. Effective treatment of this disease requires accurate diagnosis and the use of modern therapies. Israel is known for its advanced medical technology and its highly qualified specialists in oncology.

Diagnosis of oesophageal cancer

  1. Laboratory tests
    Laboratory tests include blood tests for tumour markers and other specific indicators.
  2. Endoscopy
    Endoscopy is the main method of diagnosing oesophageal cancer, allowing the inner surface of the oesophagus to be examined and a biopsy taken from any suspicious areas of tissue.
  3. PET-CT
    Positron emission tomography (PET) combined with computed tomography (CT) helps identify metastases and assess how far the disease has spread. This method allows the position of the tumour to be established precisely and secondary sites of cancer to be identified.
  4. Biopsy
    A biopsy involves taking a sample of tissue from the tumour for examination under the microscope. It is the key method confirming a diagnosis of cancer and establishing the type of tumour, which is important in choosing the right treatment.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)

Treatments for oesophageal cancer

  1. Surgery
    An operation to remove the tumour is the main treatment for oesophageal cancer. Israel makes wide use of minimally invasive techniques such as laparoscopic and robotic surgery, which minimise damage to tissue and speed up recovery.
  2. Chemotherapy
    Chemotherapy is used to destroy cancer cells and prevent them growing. Israel uses modern medicines and combinations that make treatment more effective and reduce side effects.
  3. Radiotherapy
    Radiotherapy is used to shrink the tumour before an operation or to destroy any remaining cancer cells afterwards. Modern methods of irradiation allow precise targeting of the tumour, minimising the effect on healthy tissue.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    Targeted therapy is directed at specific molecules involved in the growth and division of cancer cells. Immunotherapy stimulates the patient's immune system to fight the cancer. These methods are highly effective, particularly in treating aggressive forms of oesophageal cancer.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  1. Highly qualified specialists: Israeli doctors have many years of experience and international recognition in the field of oncology.
  2. Modern technology: The use of the newest diagnostic and treatment methods makes therapy accurate and effective.
  3. An individual approach: Every patient is given a personalised treatment plan that takes account of the features of their illness and their general health.
  4. International recognition: Israeli medical centres are known for their successes in treating cancer and attract patients from all over the world.

Treatment of oesophageal cancer in Israel is an opportunity to receive advanced medical care and improve the chances of a successful recovery, thanks to modern methods and high standards of medical practice.

fields.title: Kidney cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Kidney cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Kidney cancer is a serious condition that requires prompt diagnosis and effective treatment. Israel is one of the world leaders in oncology, offering advanced treatments for kidney cancer that help maximise the chances of a full recovery and improve patients' quality of life.

Diagnosis of kidney cancer

  1. Ultrasound scan
    is a quick, non-invasive method that can reveal tumours in the kidneys.
  2. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    help establish the size, shape and extent of the tumour and whether there are metastases.
  3. Kidney biopsy
    a procedure in which a sample of tissue is taken from the tumour for histological analysis. This allows the type of cancer to be established precisely
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed).
  4. Laboratory tests of blood and urine
    can reveal changes indicating the presence of kidney cancer.
  5. PET-CT
    may be used for a more precise assessment of how far the kidney cancer has spread and for planning treatment.

Treatments for kidney cancer

  1. Surgery:
    • Radical nephrectomy — removal of the kidney together with the tumour.
    • Partial nephrectomy — removal of the tumour alone, preserving as much healthy kidney tissue as possible.
    • Robot-assisted surgery using the da Vinci system — an advanced technology delivering great surgical precision, less pain after the operation and a shorter recovery period.
  2. Ablation and cryoablation
    minimally invasive methods used to destroy the tumour by freezing or heating the tissue.
  3. Targeted therapy
    is aimed at blocking particular molecular pathways that help cancer cells grow and spread.
  4. Immunotherapy
    stimulates the body's immune system to fight the cancer cells.
  5. Radiotherapy
    may be used to ease symptoms and reduce pain, particularly in metastatic kidney cancer.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of kidney cancer

  • An individual approach to the treatment of every patient, taking account of every feature of their illness.
  • Highly qualified specialists and the use of advanced medical equipment ensure accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • Multidisciplinary teams of doctors develop comprehensive treatment plans, combining various therapies to achieve the best results.
  • Value for money makes Israel an attractive destination for cancer patients from all over the world.

Israeli clinics offer a wide range of treatments for kidney cancer, focusing on meeting patients' needs as fully as possible and on preserving and improving their quality of life.

fields.title: Pancreatic cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Pancreatic cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Pancreatic cancer is one of the most difficult cancers to treat, partly because it is often diagnosed late and progresses quickly. Israeli clinics offer advanced approaches to the diagnosis and treatment of this disease, using the latest advances in medical science to extend patients' lives and improve their quality of life.

Diagnosis of pancreatic cancer

  1. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    provide detailed images of the pancreas, helping identify a tumour and assess how far it has spread.
  2. Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)
    produces high-quality images of the pancreas and surrounding tissues and also allows a biopsy to be taken.
  3. Laboratory tests
    Full blood count, biochemistry and blood tests for the tumour markers CA 19-9 and CEA, which may indicate the presence of pancreatic cancer.
  4. Biopsy
    followed by histological analysis of the tissue sample is the definitive method of diagnosing pancreatic cancer
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed).
  5. PET-CT
    is used to assess metastases and the effectiveness of treatment.

Treatments for pancreatic cancer

  1. Surgery,
    including the Whipple procedure, is the main treatment for resectable forms of pancreatic cancer.
  2. Chemotherapy
    is used both before the operation, to shrink the tumour, and afterwards, to destroy any remaining cancer cells.
  3. Radiotherapy
    may be used in combination with chemotherapy for local control of the disease.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    offer new possibilities in the treatment of pancreatic cancer, particularly for patients with certain genetic mutations.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of pancreatic cancer

  • A multidisciplinary approach ensures a comprehensive assessment of the patient's condition and the development of an individualised treatment plan.
  • Highly qualified specialists and modern equipment guarantee accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach to every patient makes it possible to take every aspect of the illness and the patient's preferences into account when choosing treatments.
  • Research programmes and clinical trials give access to the newest treatments, which may not be available in other countries.

Israeli clinics offer a wide range of treatments for pancreatic cancer, from surgery through to the newest protocols in chemotherapy, targeted therapy and immunotherapy, aiming to extend each patient's life as far as possible and improve its quality.

fields.title: Oral cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Oral cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Oral cancer covers tumours that develop in the lips, tongue, floor of the mouth, gums, cheeks or palate. Israeli clinics offer a comprehensive approach to treating this disease, using modern technology and innovative methods to deliver the best possible results.

Diagnosis of oral cancer:

  1. Examination and biopsy:
    The doctor carries out a visual examination of the mouth and takes a biopsy of any suspicious areas for histological analysis.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  2. Endoscopy of the mouth and throat:
    Allows doctors to see the internal structures of the mouth and throat in order to assess the spread of the cancer.
  3. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT):
    Used to establish how deeply the tumour has penetrated and whether there are metastases.
  4. PET-CT:
    Helps assess the activity of the tumour and detect distant metastases.
  5. Laboratory tests:
    Blood tests can reveal general indicators of health and of the functioning of organs that may be affected by the cancer.

Treatments for oral cancer:

  1. Surgery:
    • Excision of the tumour: Removal of the tumour together with some healthy tissue to prevent recurrence.
    • Neck dissection: Removal of the lymph nodes of the neck where the cancer has spread.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • External beam radiotherapy: Used to destroy any cancer cells remaining after surgery, or as the main treatment.
    • Brachytherapy: Internal irradiation, in which radioactive sources are placed directly in the tissue affected by the cancer.
  3. Chemotherapy:
    • Used in combination with radiotherapy or as an addition to surgery, to control metastases.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy:
    • Targeted medicines: Medicines directed at specific biological pathways involved in the growth and development of cancer cells.
    • Immunotherapy: The use of medicines to stimulate the body's immune system to attack the cancer cells.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Oncologists, surgeons, radiotherapists and other specialists work together to create an individual treatment plan.
  • Advanced medical equipment: The use of the latest technology in diagnosing and treating cancer.
  • An individual approach to every patient: Treatment plans are developed with each patient's personal needs and clinical data in mind.

Treatment of oral cancer in Israel aims to minimise the risk of recurrence, improve functional outcomes and give every patient the best possible quality of life.

fields.title: Penile cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Penile cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Penile cancer is a rare condition that requires a comprehensive approach to treatment, including surgery, radiotherapy and chemotherapy. Israeli clinics offer innovative treatments aimed at preserving function and minimising the psychological consequences for the patient.

Diagnosis of penile cancer:

  1. Visual examination and palpation:
    The first method for identifying visible abnormalities on the skin of the penis.
  2. Biopsy:
    Taking a tissue sample for examination under the microscope to confirm the presence of cancer cells.
  3. Ultrasound of the penis:
    Used to assess how deeply the tumour has penetrated and whether it has spread to nearby structures.
  4. MRI and CT:
    Needed to establish the stage of the cancer and plan treatment.
  5. PET-CT:
    Carried out to identify metastases in the lymph nodes and other organs.

Treatments for penile cancer:

  1. Surgery:
    • Partial or total penectomy: Removal of part or all of the penis, depending on the stage and extent of the cancer.
    • Lymphadenectomy: Removal of the lymph nodes in the groin where metastases are suspected.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • Used to destroy cancer cells, particularly where surgery is not possible, or to reduce the risk of recurrence after an operation.
  3. Chemotherapy:
    • Used in advanced cancer or to shrink the tumour before surgery.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy:
    • The use of the newest medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells.
    • Activation of the immune system to fight the cancer cells.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Urologists, oncologists and radiotherapists coordinate their efforts to develop an individual treatment plan.
  • The use of modern technology: Access to advanced medical equipment and treatments.
  • Preserving quality of life: Particular attention is given to functional and cosmetic results after treatment, and to supporting patients at every stage of therapy.

Treatment of penile cancer in Israel aims for the greatest possible effectiveness while preserving function and minimising psychological distress for patients.

fields.title: Spinal cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Spinal cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the spine requires highly accurate diagnosis and carefully chosen comprehensive treatment. Israeli medical centres give patients access to the latest advances in medical science and practice, together with a high standard of medical care.

Diagnosis of spinal cancer

  1. Doctors carry out a medical examination and take a history in order to understand the patient's symptoms and the course of the illness, and then set out a plan of action.
  2. Laboratory tests, including a full blood count and other specialised tests that help identify the cancer.
  3. This is followed by imaging using high-resolution 3 Tesla MRI.
  4. PET-CT provides detailed images of the tumour and allows its metabolic activity to be assessed.
  5. Biopsy — needed for definitive confirmation of the diagnosis and to establish the type of tumour. (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)

Treatments for spinal cancer

  1. Minimally invasive, low-trauma surgery, which allows the tumour to be removed with minimal risk and few complications.
  2. Next, radiotherapy and stereotactic radiosurgery are used to deliver high doses of radiation precisely to the tumour.
  3. Chemotherapy is used to destroy cancer cells, particularly where the cancer has spread.
  4. Hormone therapy and endoscopic techniques also add to the range of treatments, offering gentler approaches.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of spinal cancer

  • First, advanced medical equipment and highly qualified specialists deliver effective diagnosis and treatment.
  • Second, an individual approach to treatment guarantees a personalised treatment plan for every patient, which is extremely important in this condition.
  • Finally, comprehensive rehabilitation helps patients recover after treatment and return to a full life.

Choosing Israel for the treatment of spinal cancer gives access to advanced medical technology and highly qualified specialists — and, most importantly, attentive support at every stage of treatment and rehabilitation.

fields.title: Prostate cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Prostate cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Prostate cancer is one of the most significant cancers in men, particularly in the over-50 age group. Israel offers advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment, combining the latest scientific advances with an individual approach to every patient. All of this helps achieve the best possible quality of life after treatment.

Diagnosis of prostate cancer

  1. Digital rectal examination (DRE)
    allows the prostate to be assessed for hardening or other abnormalities.
  2. Laboratory tests:
    — PSA blood test (prostate-specific antigen): The main marker for screening and monitoring prostate cancer. A raised PSA level may indicate the presence of cancer, although it can also rise in other conditions of the prostate.
    — Full blood count: Includes checking haemoglobin, white cells and other important indicators that may reveal inflammation or other abnormal changes in the body.
    — Blood biochemistry: Assessment of the functioning of the kidneys, liver and other organs is important in deciding whether certain treatments, including chemotherapy, are possible.
  3. Prostate biopsy
    under ultrasound guidance — an accurate method of confirming a diagnosis of prostate cancer
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed).
  4. Prostate MRI: A highly accurate imaging method that helps establish the exact position of the tumour.
  5. PSMA PET
    (positron emission tomography with prostate-specific membrane antigen) is an innovative imaging method that considerably improves diagnostic accuracy, allowing even microscopic metastases to be detected.

Treatments for prostate cancer

  1. Active surveillance
    is recommended in low-risk prostate cancer with no signs of spread.
  2. Surgery
    carried out using robotic systems — the da Vinci robot — for minimally invasive removal of the prostate.
  3. Radiotherapy and brachytherapy
    are used to destroy cancer cells with minimal damage to the surrounding tissue.
  4. HIFU (high-intensity focused ultrasound)
    a method using high-intensity focused ultrasound to destroy cancer cells locally.
  5. Tookad therapy
    an innovative approach using a combination of a photosensitising agent and laser irradiation to destroy cancer cells.
  6. NanoKnife
    an advanced technology for targeted treatment of the tumour.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of prostate cancer

Israeli clinics are known for their achievements in oncology. Patients are offered a comprehensive approach, from accurate diagnosis using PSMA PET through to individualised treatment programmes that may include both traditional and innovative methods. The high qualifications of Israeli specialists, modern equipment and attention to patients' quality of life after treatment make Israel a preferred destination for the treatment of prostate cancer at international level.

fields.title: Rectal cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Rectal cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the rectum is one of the more common cancers. It requires a comprehensive approach to diagnosis and treatment. Israeli medical centres use innovative methods of treatment and diagnosis, offering patients effective treatment programmes aimed at a full recovery or at extending life and quality of life as far as possible.

Diagnosis of rectal cancer

  1. Colonoscopy
    is the main diagnostic method, allowing a tumour to be detected and a biopsy taken for histological analysis.
  2. Laboratory tests: full blood count, biochemistry, and tests for tumour markers including carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and Ca19.9, which help assess the activity of the disease and monitor the response to treatment.
  3. Sigmoidoscopy
    makes it possible to see the inner surface of the lower part of the rectum and detect abnormalities.
  4. PET
    is used to assess the stage of the disease, detect metastases and judge the effectiveness of treatment. It gives full information about how far the cancer has spread.
  5. Biopsy
    is the key step in confirming the presence of cancer cells and establishing the type of tumour
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed).

Treatments for rectal cancer

  1. Surgery
    remains the main treatment, aimed at removing the tumour and the affected sections of bowel.
  2. Chemotherapy
    is used to destroy cancer cells, particularly after an operation, to reduce the risk of recurrence.
  3. Radiotherapy
    is often used before surgery to shrink the tumour and afterwards to destroy any remaining cancer cells.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    are newer approaches to treatment, directed at particular molecular targets and at activating the patient's immune system to fight the cancer.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of rectal cancer

  • Advanced technology and highly qualified specialists deliver accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach to every patient makes it possible to design treatment that best matches their needs and the features of their illness.
  • Value for money makes treatment in Israel accessible to many patients looking for quality medical care at a competitive price.

Israeli clinics offer the most effective and safe treatments for rectal cancer, combining the latest medical developments with care for every patient and aiming for the greatest possible improvement in their health and quality of life.

fields.title: Cervical cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Cervical cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cervical cancer is one of the most serious cancers in women. Israeli medical centres offer an advanced approach to treating this disease, with the emphasis on innovative methods of diagnosis and treatment that help not only fight the disease effectively but also preserve patients' fertility, which is particularly important for young women.

Diagnosis of cervical cancer

  1. Medical examination and history
    are the first step in diagnosis, allowing specialists to assess general health and identify possible symptoms.
  2. Colposcopy makes it possible to examine the cervix in detail under high magnification in order to identify abnormalities.
  3. Laboratory tests
    include blood tests for tumour markers, which may indicate the presence of cancer cells in the body.
  4. PET-CT is used to assess how far the disease has spread, detect metastases and help plan treatment.
  5. Biopsy provides cervical tissue for detailed examination under the microscope, which is the definitive confirmation of the diagnosis
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed).

Treatments for cervical cancer

  1. Surgery
    may range from conisation of the cervix to hysterectomy. It all depends on the stage of the disease and the patient's plans for having children.
  2. Radiotherapy
    is used on its own or in combination with surgery, and is aimed at destroying the cancer cells.
  3. Chemotherapy
    is used in advanced cancer to destroy cancer cells throughout the body.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    offer new possibilities in the treatment of cervical cancer, directed at particular biological targets in the cancer cells.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of cervical cancer

  • Advanced equipment and highly qualified specialists
    deliver accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach to every patient
    makes it possible to develop the best treatment plan, taking account of every aspect of the illness and her personal preferences.
  • Value for money
    makes Israel an attractive choice for many patients looking for quality medical care at an affordable price.
  • Particular attention to preserving fertility
    reflects the aim of preserving patients' quality of life after treatment as fully as possible.

Israeli clinics offer a comprehensive approach to the treatment of cervical cancer, combining the newest medical developments with deep care for the wellbeing of every patient.

fields.title: Thyroid cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Thyroid cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Thyroid cancer is one of the most treatable cancers, provided it is diagnosed in good time and treated properly. Israeli clinics offer a wide range of innovative approaches to treating this disease, with high success rates.

Diagnosis of thyroid cancer

  1. Ultrasound scan
    The main diagnostic method, allowing the structure of the thyroid gland to be assessed and nodules or other abnormalities detected.
  2. Fine-needle aspiration biopsy
    A method in which material is taken from suspicious nodules under ultrasound guidance for cytological examination.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Laboratory tests
    These include tests for thyroid hormones and antibodies, and measurement of thyroglobulin levels after treatment.
  4. Radioisotope scan of the thyroid gland
    Allows the functional activity of nodules to be assessed.
  5. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    Used to assess the extent of the disease where metastases are suspected.

Treatment of thyroid cancer

  1. Surgery
    Includes thyroidectomy (complete or partial removal of the thyroid gland), which is the main treatment.
  2. Radioactive iodine therapy
    Given after surgery to destroy any remaining cancer cells and thyroid tissue, and also to treat metastases.
  3. Hormone therapy
    Prescribed to suppress the production of TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone), which prevents any remaining cancer cells from growing.
  4. Targeted therapy
    Used to treat metastatic thyroid cancer, particularly where certain molecular mutations are present.
  5. External beam radiotherapy
    Used rarely, mainly to control locally advanced disease or where there are metastases in the bones.

Why patients choose Israel

  • Experienced specialists
    Israel is home to leading experts in oncology and endocrinology with many years of experience in successfully treating thyroid cancer.
  • Advanced technology
    Israeli clinics are equipped with modern diagnostic and treatment devices, which allows accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach
    Every patient is given a personal treatment programme that takes account of every feature of their condition and illness.
  • Multidisciplinary teams
    Specialists of various kinds take part in treatment, which ensures a comprehensive approach and makes the treatment process as efficient as possible.

Innovative treatments, the high professionalism of medical specialists and an individual approach to every patient make Israel one of the leaders in the treatment of thyroid cancer at international level.

fields.title: Lacrimal gland cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Cancer of the lacrimal gland is a rare but aggressive malignant growth that develops in the tear gland. These tumours may be primary, arising directly in the lacrimal gland, or secondary, spreading from other parts of the body. Lacrimal gland cancer can lead to various complications, including loss of sight and the spread of the cancer.

Diagnosis of lacrimal gland cancer

  1. Detailed review of the medical history:
    • The doctor gathers information about symptoms such as swelling or pain in the area of the lacrimal gland, changes in tear production, visual disturbance, and past medical history.
  2. Visual examination and palpation:
    • The doctor examines and feels the area of the lacrimal gland to identify abnormalities and signs of a tumour.
  3. Ophthalmoscopy:
    • Examination of the fundus and the structures of the eye to identify changes and abnormalities.
  4. Ultrasound examination of the eye:
    • Used to obtain images of the structures of the eye and establish the size and position of the tumour.
  5. Computed tomography (CT):
    • Produces detailed images of the eye socket and reveals the spread of the tumour into neighbouring structures.
  6. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    • Used for a detailed study of the soft tissues and to identify metastases.
  7. Biopsy:
    • Taking a sample of tissue from the tumour for histological examination and confirmation of the diagnosis.
      (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  8. Doppler ultrasound:
    • Assessment of the blood supply to the lacrimal gland and identification of possible vascular abnormalities.

Treatment of lacrimal gland cancer

  1. Drug therapy:
    • Chemotherapy: The use of cytostatic medicines to destroy cancer cells and shrink the tumour.
    • Immunotherapy: The use of medicines that stimulate the immune system to fight the cancer cells.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • Brachytherapy: Placing radioactive seeds directly in the tumour for local treatment.
    • External beam radiotherapy: Radiation directed at the tumour to destroy the cancer cells.
  3. Surgery:
    • Local resection: Removal of the tumour and some of the surrounding tissue.
    • Orbital exenteration: Complete removal of the contents of the eye socket, including the lacrimal gland, in the case of large tumours or where there is a risk of spread.
  4. Laser therapy:
    • The use of a laser to destroy cancer cells in small, superficial tumours.
  5. Photodynamic therapy (PDT):
    • Administration of a light-sensitive agent that is activated by a laser and destroys the cancer cells.

Advantages of treating lacrimal gland cancer in Israel

  1. A high level of professionalism:
    • Israeli doctors have deep knowledge and many years of experience in treating lacrimal gland cancer and other cancers.
  2. Modern equipment:
    • Clinics are equipped with advanced diagnostic and treatment devices, which allows highly accurate investigation and effective treatment.
  3. An individual approach:
    • Every patient is given an individual treatment plan that takes account of the nature of the condition and their general health.
  4. Innovative treatments:
    • The use of the most modern methods and medicines, including immunotherapy and photodynamic therapy.
  5. Comprehensive support:
    • Covers not only treatment of the underlying condition but also support for the patient's mental and physical wellbeing during treatment and rehabilitation.

Treatment of lacrimal gland cancer in Israel gives patients access to high-quality medical care and considerably improves both the outlook and their quality of life.

fields.title: Salivary gland cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Salivary gland cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the salivary glands is a rare condition affecting one of the salivary glands. Israel treats it using innovative approaches that combine the latest advances in medical science with an individual approach to every patient.

Diagnosis of salivary gland cancer

  1. Examination and palpation
    The doctor examines and feels the area of the salivary glands for growths and hardening.
  2. Biopsy
    Taking a tissue sample to confirm the diagnosis by histological examination.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Blood tests and tumour markers
    Blood tests for tumour markers help assess general health and identify possible metastases.
  4. Ultrasound scan
    Used to assess the structure and size of the salivary glands.
  5. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI): These methods allow the extent of the tumour to be assessed.
  6. PET-CT
    An integrated investigation combining PET and CT for a detailed examination, including assessment of the activity of the tumour and the search for metastases.

Treatment of salivary gland cancer

  1. Surgery
    The main treatment, aimed at removing the tumour together with part or all of the salivary gland.
  2. Radiotherapy
    May be used as an additional treatment after surgery to destroy any remaining cancer cells, or to treat tumours that cannot be removed.
  3. Chemotherapy
    Used in advanced cancer or where there are metastases.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    The newest treatments, aimed at destroying cancer cells with the greatest precision and minimal effect on healthy tissue.

Why patients choose Israel

  • Multidisciplinary teams
    Leading specialists in oncology, surgery, radiology and other fields work together to develop the best treatment plan.
  • A personalised approach
    All treatments are chosen with the particular features of the illness and the patient's wellbeing in mind.

    Patients have access to the most modern technology and treatment techniques, which considerably improves the chances of successful treatment.
  • A high standard of medical care
    Israeli clinics are known for the quality of their service, attention to detail and care for patients' comfort.

Treatment of salivary gland cancer in Israel gives patients access to advanced medical technology and highly qualified care, with an individualised and comprehensive approach to every case.

fields.title: Thymus cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Thymus cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the thymus, also known as thymoma, is a rare tumour arising from the epithelial cells of the thymus — an organ that plays an important part in the immune system. Israel treats this disease using the most modern medical technology and methods, which provide a comprehensive approach and highly effective therapy.

Diagnosis of thymus cancer:

  1. Computed tomography (CT) of the chest:
    The main method of imaging the thymus, allowing the size and structure of the tumour to be assessed along with any spread into the surrounding tissues.
  2. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    Used for more detailed imaging of the soft tissues and structures.
  3. PET-CT:
    Helps identify distant metastases.
  4. Biopsy:
    Carried out to obtain tumour tissue, which is necessary for accurate histological diagnosis.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  5. Laboratory tests:
    These include blood tests that can reveal abnormalities relating to the functioning of the immune system.

Treatments for thymus cancer:

  1. Surgery:
    • Thymectomy: Removal of the thymus and surrounding tissue. It may be radical or partial, depending on the stage of the cancer.
    • Extended surgical resection: Removal of the tumour together with part of the surrounding affected tissues or structures.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • Given after surgery to destroy any remaining cancer cells, or as the primary treatment for inoperable thymomas.
  3. Chemotherapy:
    • Used in advanced cancer or where surgery is not possible. It is effective in shrinking tumours before an operation or radiotherapy.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy:
    • Targeted medicines: Directed at the molecular and genetic abnormalities of the tumour.
    • Immunotherapy: Medicines that stimulate the immune system to attack the cancer cells, particularly relevant where immunological syndromes are present.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Oncologists, thoracic surgeons, radiologists and immunologists combine their efforts to deliver the best result.
  • Advanced medical equipment and treatments: The newest developments are brought into clinical practice.
  • Individualised treatment plans: Approaches adapted as closely as possible to the features of the illness and the patient.

Treatment of thymus cancer in Israel aims to give patients the longest and best possible life, minimise side effects and provide comprehensive support at every stage of the fight against the disease.

fields.title: Colon cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Colon cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the large bowel is one of the most common cancers worldwide. Israeli clinics offer a comprehensive approach to treating this disease, using the latest advances in medical science and technology to provide the most effective and gentlest treatment possible.

Diagnosis of colon cancer

  1. Colonoscopy
    the main diagnostic method, allowing the inner surface of the large bowel to be examined and a biopsy taken from any suspicious areas.
  2. Biopsy
    During the colonoscopy a tissue sample is taken, which allows the presence of cancer cells and the type of cancer to be established precisely under the microscope. This is the key method for definitive confirmation of a diagnosis of colon cancer.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Laboratory tests
    a full blood count and tests for tumour markers such as carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and Ca19.9 help assess the presence and activity of cancer cells.
  4. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    are used where necessary to establish the stage of the disease and identify metastases.
  5. PET-CT
    an integrated investigation combining positron emission tomography and computed tomography, for a more precise assessment of the extent of the tumour.

Treatments for colon cancer

  1. Surgery
    removal of the affected part of the bowel is the standard treatment in the early stages of the cancer.
  2. Chemotherapy
    is used to destroy any remaining cancer cells, particularly in advanced cancer or after an operation to reduce the risk of recurrence.
  3. Radiotherapy
    may be used to shrink the tumour before an operation or to destroy any remaining cancer cells afterwards.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    are directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells and at the immune system respectively, offering new possibilities in treating this disease.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of colon cancer

  • An individual approach to every patient makes it possible to design the best treatment programme, taking account of the features of the illness and general health.
  • Advanced medical technology and highly qualified specialists deliver accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • Value for money makes treatment in Israel accessible to many patients, offering high-quality medical care at a competitive price.
  • Particular attention to patients' quality of life after treatment, including recovery and rehabilitation.

Israeli clinics offer the most effective and safe treatments available.

fields.title: Small bowel cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Small bowel cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the small bowel involves the formation of malignant tumours in the small intestine. In Israel, patients are offered advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment aimed at fighting the disease effectively and considerably improving quality of life.

Diagnosis of small bowel cancer

  1. Medical examination and history
    are the first stage, in which doctors assess the patient's symptoms and the history of the illness.
  2. Endoscopy
    including capsule endoscopy and enteroscopy, allows the inner surface of the small bowel to be seen and tumours identified.
  3. Colonoscopy
    is used for a detailed examination of the large bowel, with a biopsy taken afterwards.
  4. Biopsy
    makes it possible to obtain tissue samples for histological analysis.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  5. Laboratory tests: blood tests may reveal raised levels of certain tumour markers — carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and CA 19-9 — which may indicate the presence of small bowel cancer. These results help assess the activity of the disease and monitor the response to treatment.
  6. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    are used to assess the stage of the disease and search for metastases.
  7. PET-CT
    may be ordered for a more precise assessment of how far the cancer has spread and for planning treatment.

Treatments for small bowel cancer

  1. Surgery
    the primary and most common treatment. Removal of the tumour together with part of the bowel. It may involve resection of the affected section of bowel.
  2. Chemotherapy
    is used to destroy cancer cells, particularly in advanced cancer or to prevent recurrence.
  3. Radiotherapy
    is used less often than in other types of cancer, but can be effective in shrinking tumours or destroying any cancer cells remaining after surgery.
  4. Targeted therapy
    is directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells, which helps block the growth and spread of the tumour.
  5. Immunotherapy
    uses the mechanisms of the body's immune system to fight the cancer, stimulating or restoring the body's natural ability to fight cancer cells.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of small bowel cancer

  • Advanced medical technology and highly qualified specialists in Israel deliver accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach to every patient makes it possible to design treatment that best matches the needs and features of each case.
  • Value for money makes Israel an attractive choice for many patients looking for affordable, quality medical care.

Israeli clinics offer a comprehensive approach to the treatment of small bowel cancer, combining the newest medical developments with deep care for the wellbeing of every patient and aiming to extend their lives and improve their quality as far as possible.

fields.title: Urethral cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Urethral cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the urethra is a rare cancer affecting the urinary passage. In Israel, patients are offered innovative methods of diagnosing and treating this type of cancer, which makes it possible to achieve the best results even in difficult cases.

Diagnosis of urethral cancer

  1. Urethroscopy
    Visual examination of the urethra with a special instrument to identify abnormalities or tumours.
  2. Biopsy
    Obtaining a sample of tumour tissue for histological analysis, which is the key to confirming a diagnosis of urethral cancer.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Urine cytology
    Examination of the cells in the urine for cancer cells.
  4. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    Help assess how far the tumour has spread within the body.
  5. Ultrasound scan
    Used to assess the state of the bladder, kidneys and surrounding tissues.
  6. Laboratory tests
    Including a full blood count, biochemistry and measurement of tumour markers.
  7. PET-CT
    Combines positron emission tomography and computed tomography for an accurate assessment of how far the cancer has spread. It also establishes the stage of the disease and the effectiveness of treatment.

Treatment of urethral cancer

  1. Surgery
    The main treatment. It may involve partial or complete removal of the urethra, depending on the stage of the disease and the position of the tumour.
  2. Radiotherapy
    Used on its own or in combination with surgery, particularly for tumours that cannot be removed.
  3. Chemotherapy
    May be used to treat metastatic urethral cancer or as an addition to other treatments to reduce the risk of recurrence.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    Innovative approaches directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells or at activating the immune system to fight the tumour.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach
    Urologists, oncologists, radiologists and other specialists take part in treatment, ensuring a comprehensive approach to every case.
  • Advanced treatments
    Patients have access to the most modern methods of diagnosis and treatment, including minimally invasive surgical techniques and the latest advances in drug therapy.
  • Highly qualified specialists
    Israeli doctors have international experience and regularly exchange knowledge and practice with colleagues from other countries.
  • An individualised approach to treatment
    Every patient is given a personal treatment programme that takes account of every feature of their condition and their preferences.

Israeli clinics offer patients with urethral cancer access to advanced medical technology and highly qualified care, which makes it possible to achieve the best treatment results and improve patients' quality of life.

fields.title: Vaginal cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Vaginal cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the vagina is a rare type of cancer that can be diagnosed and treated effectively with modern approaches. Advanced technology and techniques are available in Israel that allow comprehensive treatment of this disease, taking account of the individual circumstances of every patient.

Diagnosis of vaginal cancer:

  1. Gynaecological examination:
    The doctor carries out a visual examination of the vagina and cervix, using special instruments to take a tissue sample for histological analysis.
  2. Biopsy
    Taking a tissue sample for histological examination, which is the gold standard in diagnosis.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Colposcopy:
    Detailed examination of the lining of the vagina and cervix using a special microscope to identify atypical cells.
  4. Transvaginal ultrasound:
    Used to establish the size, shape and structure of the tumour.
  5. MRI and CT:
    Assessment of the extent of the tumour in the pelvis and identification of metastases.
  6. PET-CT:
    The search for active cancer cells in the body and checking for metastases.

Treatments for vaginal cancer:

  1. Surgery:
    • Wide local excision: Removal of the tumour together with some healthy tissue.
    • Vaginectomy: Partial or complete removal of the vagina, depending on the stage and extent of the cancer.
    • Lymphadenectomy: Removal of the regional lymph nodes where metastases are present.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • Used as the main treatment or in combination with surgery to destroy cancer cells and prevent recurrence.
  3. Chemotherapy:
    • Used to treat advanced cancer or where an operation is not possible. It may be combined with radiotherapy to make it more effective.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy:
    • The use of the newest medicines directed at specific biological targets in the cancer cells, and activation of the immune system to fight the cancer.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Oncologists, gynaecologists, radiotherapists and surgeons work together to develop the best treatment plan.
  • Advanced medical equipment: The use of the latest advances in medical devices and technology for diagnosis and treatment.
  • Individual treatment: Treatment plans are developed taking account of the stage of the disease, the patient's general health and her personal preferences.

Treatment of vaginal cancer in Israel aims to extend patients' lives and improve their quality as far as possible, delivering high survival rates and minimal side effects.

fields.title: Testicular cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Testicular cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Although testicular cancer is a relatively rare condition, it is a serious threat, particularly to young men. Israeli medical centres offer a comprehensive approach to treating this disease, including advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment aimed at achieving a cure and preserving fertility.

Diagnosis of testicular cancer

  1. Medical examination and palpation provide important initial information about the state of the testicles.
  2. Ultrasound scan of the testicles helps identify structural changes and tumours.
  3. Blood tests and tumour markers
    Including: full blood count, biochemistry
    AFP (alpha-fetoprotein)
    hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin)
    LDH (lactate dehydrogenase), which help establish the presence and activity of cancer cells.
  4. PET-CT of the abdomen, chest and pelvis is used to detect metastases and assess the overall spread of the cancer.
  5. Biopsy confirms the diagnosis by establishing the type of cancer cells (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed).

Treatments for testicular cancer

  1. Surgery
    Including orchiectomy (removal of the affected testicle), which is often the first step in treating testicular cancer.
  2. Robotic operations using the da Vinci system
    Allow operations to be carried out with great precision and minimal complications.
  3. Chemotherapy
    Used to destroy cancer cells, particularly in advanced cancer or after surgery to minimise the risk of recurrence.
  4. Radiotherapy
    May be prescribed to destroy any remaining cancer cells, particularly in certain types of testicular cancer.
  5. Surveillance
    Is an option in the early stages of testicular cancer, where there is no sign of spread beyond the testicle.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of testicular cancer

  • Advanced equipment and highly qualified specialists in Israel guarantee accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach to every case makes it possible to design treatment that best matches each patient's needs and circumstances.
  • Particular attention to preserving fertility reflects Israeli clinics' aim not only to cure the disease but also to ensure patients' quality of life after treatment.
  • The combination of high-quality medical care and the cost of treatment attracts patients from all over the world. Israel offers affordable yet high-technology and effective treatment.

fields.title: Ovarian cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Ovarian cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Ovarian cancer is one of the leading cancers of the female reproductive system. Thanks to innovative medical technology and the deep professionalism of its doctors, Israel offers advanced methods of diagnosing and treating this serious disease.

Diagnosis of ovarian cancer

  1. Medical examination and history
    help doctors form an initial picture of the patient's state of health.
  2. Laboratory tests
    including blood tests for the tumour markers CA-125 and CEA, which help detect ovarian cancer early.
  3. Transvaginal ultrasound
    provides detailed images of the ovaries and allows abnormalities to be detected at an early stage.
  4. PET-CT
    is used to assess the stage of the disease, the size of the tumour and the presence of metastases.
    Important — PET-CT is not carried out sooner than 2 weeks after a course of chemotherapy, 5 weeks after a course of radiotherapy, or 4 weeks after an operation.
  5. Biopsy
    the decisive stage of diagnosis, confirming the presence of cancer cells and establishing the type of tumour
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)

Treatments for ovarian cancer

  1. Minimally invasive and laparoscopic surgery
    removal of as much of the tumour and affected tissue as possible.
  2. Robotic surgery for ovarian cancer
    allows operations to be carried out with great precision and minimal complications.
  3. Radiotherapy and gentler chemotherapy are used to destroy any remaining cancer cells and minimise the risk of recurrence.
  4. Targeted therapy and hormone therapy are aimed at destroying cancer cells at the molecular level, reducing side effects and making treatment more effective.

Newer treatment protocols for ovarian cancer
— A combination of niraparib (Zejula) and pembrolizumab (Keytruda) has opened up new possibilities for patients with recurrent ovarian cancer. This regimen is used for tumours resistant to platinum-based chemotherapy.
— A protocol combining binimetinib (Mektovi) and buparlisib (BKM120) is intended for tumours with RAS or BRAF genetic mutations. This approach is being studied in clinical trials and is one strand of personalised therapy in Israel.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of ovarian cancer

  • Advanced equipment and highly qualified specialists guarantee accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach to treatment makes it possible to develop the best treatment strategy, taking account of the features of each case.
  • Comprehensive rehabilitation after treatment aids rapid recovery and a return to normal life.

Israeli clinics offer the most effective and safe treatments for ovarian cancer, with the emphasis on patients' quality of life and on extending their lives as far as possible.

fields.title: Tongue cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Tongue cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the tongue is one of the types of oral cancer and requires a comprehensive approach to treatment. Israeli clinics offer innovative methods of diagnosis and treatment, giving patients access to advanced technology and highly qualified specialists.

Diagnosis of tongue cancer

  1. Examination and palpation
    The doctor examines the mouth and feels the tongue for hardening or unusual growths.
  2. Biopsy
    Taking a tissue sample for histological examination confirms the presence of cancer cells.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Laboratory tests
    These include a full blood count and biochemical tests, and measurement of tumour markers, which helps assess general health.
  4. Ultrasound scan of the neck
    Helps detect metastases in the lymph nodes.
  5. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    Used to assess how far the tumour has spread.
  6. PET-CT
    Allows the activity of the tumour to be assessed and distant metastases to be identified.

Treatment of tongue cancer

  1. Surgery
    Removal of the tumour of the tongue, sometimes with some healthy tissue, to minimise the risk of recurrence. In some cases reconstruction of the tongue may be required.
  2. Radiotherapy
    Used on its own or in combination with surgery, particularly for small tumours or to destroy any remaining cancer cells.
  3. Chemotherapy
    Used in advanced tongue cancer, often together with radiotherapy.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    The newest treatments, directed at particular biological targets in the cancer cells and at activating the immune system to fight the tumour.

Why patients choose Israel

  • Multidisciplinary teams of specialists, ensuring a comprehensive approach to every case.
  • Individual treatment plans, developed with the features of the illness and the patient in mind.
  • Access to innovative treatments, including the latest advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy.
  • A high standard of medical care and attention to patients.

Israeli clinics offer advanced treatments for tongue cancer, with the emphasis on an individual approach and the use of the newest medical technology to achieve the best results.

fields.title: Gallbladder cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Gallbladder cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Although cancer of the gallbladder is a rare condition, it requires a careful approach to diagnosis and treatment. Israeli medical centres offer a comprehensive and individualised approach using the most modern and effective methods.

Diagnosis of gallbladder cancer

  1. Ultrasound scan
    The first diagnostic method for identifying abnormalities in the gallbladder.
  2. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    Detailed imaging methods that allow the stage of the disease to be assessed.
  3. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP)
    Used to examine the bile ducts and take a biopsy.
  4. Biopsy
    Examination of samples of tumour tissue for histological analysis.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  5. Laboratory tests
    These include a full blood count, biochemical tests and tumour marker tests, which may indicate the presence of cancer.
  6. PET (positron emission tomography)
    Provides information about the metabolic activity of the tissue and the presence of metastases.
  7. Consultation with a specialist
    Needed for a comprehensive analysis of the results and for planning further treatment.

Treatment of gallbladder cancer

  1. Surgery
    Most often involves complete removal of the gallbladder (cholecystectomy), and in some cases resection of part of the liver and the regional lymph nodes.
  2. Chemotherapy
    Used to destroy any remaining cancer cells, or as the main treatment where the cancer cannot be removed.
  3. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    The newest approaches, aimed at destroying cancer cells with minimal effect on healthy tissue.
  4. Palliative treatment
    Aimed at easing symptoms and improving patients' quality of life in the later stages of the disease.

Why patients choose Israel

Israeli clinics give patients access to first-class medical care, including advanced methods of diagnosing and treating gallbladder cancer. Experienced specialists, individualised treatment programmes and the use of the latest scientific developments and clinical research make Israel one of the best choices for the treatment of this disease.

fields.title: Stomach cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Stomach cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Stomach cancer is a serious condition that requires prompt, accurate diagnosis and a comprehensive approach to treatment. Israeli clinics offer some of the most advanced methods of diagnosing and treating stomach cancer, combining innovative medical technology with highly qualified specialists.

Diagnosis of stomach cancer

  1. Endoscopy (gastroscopy)
    The main diagnostic method, allowing the doctor to examine the inner surface of the stomach and take tissue samples (a biopsy) for histological examination.
  2. Biopsy
    Examination of tissue samples for an accurate diagnosis.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Laboratory tests
    These include blood tests, checks for tumour markers and other specific tests that may indicate stomach cancer.
  4. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    Provide detailed images that can reveal the presence of a tumour, its size and extent.
  5. PET-CT
    A highly informative method for assessing the metabolic activity of the tumour and identifying metastases.

Treatment of stomach cancer

  1. Surgery
    The main treatment, involving partial or total gastrectomy (removal of the stomach), often with removal of some of the lymph nodes.
  2. Chemotherapy
    Used both before and after the operation to destroy cancer cells, and as the main treatment for patients with metastatic cancer.
  3. Radiotherapy
    Used in combination with chemotherapy to shrink the tumour before an operation or to destroy any remaining cancer cells afterwards.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    The newest treatments, directed at specific molecular targets in the tumour and at stimulating the immune system to fight the cancer.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach
    Israel's leading clinics use a team approach to treatment, providing a comprehensive assessment and an individual treatment strategy for every patient.
  • Innovative treatments
    Patients have access to the latest advances in oncology, including targeted therapy and immunotherapy, all of which considerably improves the chances of successful treatment.
  • Highly qualified specialists
    Oncologists, surgeons, radiologists and other specialists in Israel have international experience and regularly exchange knowledge with colleagues from other countries.
  • Quality and comfort of treatment
    Israeli medical centres provide a high standard of medical care and comfort. Considerable attention is given not only to patients' physical but also to their psychological condition, with support at every stage of treatment.
  • Access to clinical trials
    Patients have the opportunity to take part in international clinical trials of the newest medicines and therapies, which gives access to innovative treatments not yet available in other countries.
  • Individualised treatment programmes
    Every patient is given a personalised treatment plan that takes account of the features of their illness, their general health and their personal preferences and goals. This makes treatment as effective as possible while minimising the risk of side effects.

Choosing Israel for the treatment of stomach cancer gives patients access to world-class medical care, combining advanced technology, highly qualified medical specialists and a whole-person approach to the health of every patient.

fields.title: Sarcoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Treatment and diagnosis of sarcoma in Israel

Sarcoma is a rare and complex disease that requires a comprehensive approach to diagnosis and treatment. Thanks to their experience, advanced technology and individual approach to every patient, Israeli medical centres offer some of the most effective ways of fighting this disease.

Diagnosis of sarcoma

  1. The start of the process
    physical examination and medical history. Doctors begin with a detailed full medical history and a physical examination. After that, on the basis of the initial findings, the doctor decides what further investigations are needed.
  2. Laboratory tests
    The key laboratory tests are a full blood count and blood biochemistry. A full blood count can reveal changes characteristic of cancer. Blood biochemistry helps assess the working of various organs and systems, including the liver and kidneys, which is important for a complete picture of the patient's health.
  3. PET-CT (positron emission tomography)
    This method is used to assess the metabolic activity of the tumour and identify metastases at an early stage. It allows the position of the tumour to be established precisely and the effectiveness of treatment to be assessed.
  4. Biopsy
    This procedure involves taking tumour tissue for histological analysis, which is the key method for establishing the type of sarcoma. A biopsy is needed for definitive confirmation of the diagnosis and for choosing a treatment strategy. Histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed.

After analysing all the results, the professor will establish the diagnosis and prescribe the appropriate treatment. It is worth noting that the diagnostic process itself takes up to 3 working days.

Treatments for sarcoma

  1. Surgery
    The main aim is complete removal of the tumour while preserving healthy tissue. Depending on the position and size of the sarcoma, reconstructive surgery may be required.
  2. Radiotherapy
    Given before or after the operation to destroy any remaining cancer cells or to shrink the tumour before surgery.
  3. Chemotherapy
    This method is used to destroy cancer cells throughout the body. It may be given before or after an operation, or as the main treatment for certain types of sarcoma.
  4. Targeted therapy
    It is directed at particular genetic or molecular targets found in the cancer cells.
  5. Immunotherapy
    This treatment stimulates the body's immune system to fight the cancer and is particularly effective in certain types of sarcoma.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of sarcoma

  • Advanced medical technology. Israeli clinics are equipped with the most modern devices.
  • Experienced specialists. Israel is home to leading experts in oncology who have extensive experience in treating sarcoma.
  • An individual approach. Every patient is given a personalised treatment plan.
  • Reasonable prices. Prices for treatment in Israel are competitive, and the quality of medical care fully matches the cost. This makes treatment accessible to a wide range of patients from all over the world.
  • High patient satisfaction. Thanks to the quality of the service and the attention to detail, patients feel both confident and comfortable at every stage of treatment, and — importantly — there is no language barrier.

In choosing Israel, patients receive not only treatment to the highest world standards but also care and support at every stage of their journey to recovery.
