fields.title: Multiple sclerosis
fields.bodyHtml:
Multiple sclerosis: innovative treatment in Israel

Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic disease of the central nervous system characterised by damage to the myelin sheath of the nerve fibres. This can lead to a wide range of symptoms, including fatigue, poor coordination, problems with vision and many others. Israel is one of the leading centres for the treatment of MS, giving patients access to innovative methods of diagnosis and therapy.

Diagnosis of multiple sclerosis in Israel:

  1. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    The main method of diagnosing MS, allowing areas of demyelination in the brain and spinal cord to be detected.
  2. Laboratory tests
    For the detection of oligoclonal IgG.
  3. Examination of the cerebrospinal fluid (lumbar puncture)
    Helps detect changes characteristic of MS, including the presence of oligoclonal bands.
  4. Neurological examination: Assessment of the functions of the central nervous system and identification of disturbances in nerve conduction.

Treatments for multiple sclerosis:

  1. Disease-modifying therapy
    Medicines that slow the progression of the disease and reduce the frequency of relapses. Both traditional and the newest medicines are available in Israel.
  2. Treatment of relapses
    A course of high-dose corticosteroids, usually given intravenously, to reduce inflammation and speed recovery.
  3. Symptomatic treatment
    Prescribed to ease particular symptoms such as fatigue, spasticity, bladder problems and others.
  4. Rehabilitation
    Includes physiotherapy, therapeutic exercise, occupational therapy and speech therapy to maintain physical activity and improve quality of life.
  5. Psychological support
    Psychotherapy and support groups for patients and their families.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A personalised approach: Treatments are chosen individually according to the form of MS, the stage of the disease and the patient's general condition.
  • Innovative treatments: The opportunity to take part in clinical trials of new medicines and therapies.
  • A multidisciplinary team: Leading specialists in neurology, rehabilitation and psychotherapy work together to achieve the best results.

Treatment of multiple sclerosis in Israel aims to slow the progression of the disease as far as possible, reduce symptoms and improve patients' quality of life.

fields.title: Retinoblastoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Retinoblastoma is a malignant tumour of the retina of the eye. It is a rare condition, but it is the most common cancer inside the eye in children. If left untreated, retinoblastoma can lead to loss of sight and to the spread of cancer cells to other parts of the body.

Diagnosis of retinoblastoma

  1. Detailed review of the medical history:
    • The doctor gathers information about symptoms such as a white reflex in the pupil, squint, and pain or redness of the eyes, and also considers the family history of the condition.
  2. Visual examination and ophthalmoscopy:
    • The ophthalmologist examines the fundus with an ophthalmoscope to identify a tumour in the retina.
  3. Ultrasound examination of the eye:
    • An ultrasound of the eye helps image the internal structures of the eye and establish the size and position of the tumour.
  4. Computed tomography (CT):
    • A CT scan helps obtain detailed images of the eye and identify any spread of the tumour beyond it.
  5. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    • MRI is used for a more precise study of the soft tissues of the eye and to identify metastases.
  6. Fluorescein angiography:
    • This method allows the blood supply to the retina to be assessed and abnormalities associated with the tumour to be identified.
  7. Genetic testing:
    • Carried out to establish whether mutations are present in the RB1 gene, which are associated with the hereditary form of retinoblastoma.

Treatment of retinoblastoma

  1. Drug therapy:
    • Chemotherapy: Used to shrink the tumour and prevent it spreading. Chemotherapy may be systemic (intravenous) or local (intravitreal).
    • Immunotherapy: Medicines are used that stimulate the immune system to fight the cancer cells.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • Brachytherapy: Placing radioactive seeds directly in the tumour for local treatment.
    • External beam radiotherapy: Radiation directed at the tumour to destroy the cancer cells.
  3. Surgery:
    • Enucleation: Removal of the eye in the case of large tumours or where there is a risk of spread.
    • Local resection: Removal of the tumour and some of the surrounding tissue.
  4. Laser therapy:
    • The use of a laser to destroy cancer cells in small, superficial tumours.

Advantages of treating retinoblastoma in Israel

  1. A high level of professionalism:
    • Israeli doctors have deep knowledge and many years of experience in treating retinoblastoma and other cancers.
  2. Modern equipment:
    • Clinics are equipped with advanced diagnostic and treatment devices, which allows highly accurate investigation and effective treatment.
  3. An individual approach:
    • Every patient is given an individual treatment plan that takes account of the nature of the condition and their general health.
  4. Innovative treatments:
    • The use of the most modern methods and medicines, including immunotherapy and photodynamic therapy.
  5. Comprehensive support:
    • Covers not only treatment of the underlying condition but also support for the patient's mental and physical wellbeing during treatment and rehabilitation.

Treatment of retinoblastoma in Israel gives patients access to high-quality medical care and considerably improves both the outlook and their quality of life.

fields.title: Rheumatoid arthritis
fields.bodyHtml:
Rheumatoid arthritis: innovative treatment in Israel

Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory disease affecting primarily the small joints of the hands and feet. A distinguishing feature of RA is that it affects the joints symmetrically, which can lead to their deformity and destruction. In Israel, patients with rheumatoid arthritis are offered advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment aimed at reducing symptoms as far as possible and preventing the disease from progressing.

Diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis

  1. Laboratory tests
    These include measurement of rheumatoid factor (RF) and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibodies (anti-CCP), and a full blood count to identify inflammation.
  2. MRI and ultrasound of the joints
    Used to assess the extent of damage to the joints and the presence of inflammation and erosions.
  3. X-rays
    Allow the characteristic changes in the joints associated with RA to be identified, including erosions and osteoporosis around the joints.

Treatments for rheumatoid arthritis in Israel

  1. Drug treatment
    • Disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs): methotrexate, leflunomide and others, used to slow the progression of the disease.
    • Biological medicines: TNF-alpha inhibitors, interleukin inhibitors and other biological agents aimed at controlling the inflammatory process.
    • Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors: The newest class of medicines for treating RA. They act on the inflammatory signalling pathways inside the cells.
  2. Physiotherapy and rehabilitation
    These include a set of exercises aimed at maintaining mobility in the joints, strengthening the muscles and improving general wellbeing.
  3. Surgery
    Used where conservative treatment brings no relief. Surgical options include synovectomy (removal of the inflamed lining of the joint), osteotomy and joint replacement.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach
    Provides a comprehensive view of the problem and the development of an individual treatment plan covering both medicines and physiotherapy.
  • Access to innovative medicines
    Patients are able to receive the most modern medicines, including the latest generation of biological treatments.
  • Highly qualified specialists
    Israel is home to some of the world's leading rheumatologists, with extensive experience in treating rheumatoid arthritis.
  • Individualised rehabilitation
    Rehabilitation programmes are adapted to the needs of each patient, which aids faster recovery and a better quality of life.

Treatment of rheumatoid arthritis in Israel offers patients not only relief from symptoms and a slowing of the disease, but also the chance to lead an active life with a good quality of life.

fields.title: Type 1 diabetes
fields.bodyHtml:
Type 1 diabetes: advanced approaches to treatment in Israel

Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune condition in which the immune system attacks the insulin-producing cells in the pancreas. Israel offers a comprehensive approach to the diagnosis and treatment of this condition, using modern technology and methods.

Diagnosis of type 1 diabetes in Israel:

  1. Blood glucose measurement
    The main method of establishing a raised level of sugar in the blood.
  2. Glycated haemoglobin test (HbA1c)
    Shows the average level of glucose in the blood.
  3. Autoantibody tests
    Help confirm the autoimmune nature of the condition.
  4. C-peptide measurement
    Helps assess the body's own production of insulin.
  5. Use of a continuous glucose monitor (CGM)
    Allows glucose levels to be tracked continuously, giving more precise control of the condition.
  6. Consultation with a nutritionist
    Development of an individual eating plan adapted to the needs of a patient with type 1 diabetes, which is an important part of the comprehensive approach to treatment.

Treatment of type 1 diabetes in Israel:

  1. Insulin therapy
    The basis of treatment for type 1 diabetes; it involves finding an individual insulin regimen.
  2. Educational programmes
    Teaching patients how to monitor their own blood glucose, eat properly and manage insulin doses.
  3. The use of technology
    Insulin pumps and CGM systems to optimise control of blood glucose levels.
  4. Support and advice
    Psychological support for patients and their families, and access to specialist support groups.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A personalised approach: Every patient is given an individual treatment and monitoring programme that takes account of their particular needs and way of life.
  • Innovative technology and treatments: Patients have access to the latest advances in the treatment of diabetes, which gives better control of the condition and improves quality of life.
  • A multidisciplinary team of specialists: Doctors, nutritionists, dietitians and psychologists work together to provide a comprehensive approach to treatment and support for patients.

Treatment of type 1 diabetes in Israel aims to achieve and maintain a stable level of glucose in the blood, prevent complications and ensure a good quality of life for patients.

fields.title: Type 2 diabetes
fields.bodyHtml:
Type 2 diabetes: innovative treatment in Israel

Type 2 diabetes is a chronic condition involving a disturbance of glucose metabolism, in which the body's cells lose their sensitivity to insulin. It is the most common type of diabetes and is often linked to excess weight, lifestyle and genetic factors. Israel offers a comprehensive approach to the treatment and control of type 2 diabetes, including advanced methods of diagnosis, individualised treatment and an extensive rehabilitation programme.

Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes:

  1. Blood glucose measurement
    Measurement of blood sugar when fasting and after eating.
  2. Glycated haemoglobin test (HbA1c)
    Allows the average glucose level to be assessed.
  3. Glucose tolerance test (OGTT)
    Helps assess how the body absorbs glucose.
  4. Measurement of C-peptide and insulin
    To assess the production of insulin by the pancreas.
  5. Autoantibody tests
    To rule out the autoimmune causes characteristic of type 1 diabetes.

Treatment of type 2 diabetes in Israel:

  1. Drug therapy
    Includes medicines that improve the sensitivity of cells to insulin, stimulate the production of insulin and lower the level of glucose in the blood.
  2. Lifestyle changes
    Adjusting the diet, increasing physical activity, controlling weight, giving up smoking and limiting alcohol.
  3. Educational programmes
    Teaching patients the basics of managing diabetes, eating properly and monitoring their own blood glucose.
  4. Insulin therapy
    May be prescribed in the later stages of the condition, where medicines and lifestyle changes do not give adequate control of glucose.
  5. Monitoring and control of complications
    Regular monitoring of the cardiovascular system, kidneys, eyes and feet for the prompt detection and treatment of complications.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An individualised approach
    Every patient is offered a personal treatment programme that takes account of every aspect of their health and the particular course of their condition.
  • A multidisciplinary team
    Specialists from various fields of medicine work together to provide a comprehensive approach to the treatment and rehabilitation of patients.
  • Access to innovation
    Patients can gain access to the latest medical developments and technology in the treatment of diabetes.
  • Support and education
    Wide opportunities to learn how to manage diabetes, including programmes covering diet, exercise and psychological support.

Treatment of type 2 diabetes in Israel aims to achieve and maintain the target level of glucose in the blood, prevent the development of complications and improve patients' quality of life.

fields.title: Angina
fields.bodyHtml:
Angina: advanced diagnosis and treatment in Israel

Diagnosis of angina:

  1. Clinical examination and history: Analysis of the symptoms and identification of risk factors.
  2. Electrocardiogram (ECG): Assessment of the electrical activity of the heart.
  3. Echocardiography: Imaging of the structure and function of the heart.
  4. Thallium isotope scan of the heart: Assessment of the blood supply to the heart muscle and identification of areas with reduced blood flow.
  5. Cardiac exercise testing: Examination of the working of the heart under exertion on an exercise bike or treadmill.
  6. Laboratory tests: Blood tests, including the lipid profile and markers of inflammation.

Treatments for angina:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Nitrates, beta blockers and calcium channel blockers to control symptoms and improve the blood supply to the heart.
    • Antithrombotic medicines to prevent the formation of clots.
  2. Balloon angioplasty:
    • A minimally invasive procedure in which a balloon is introduced through a catheter to widen the narrowed section of the artery and restore normal blood flow.
  3. Stenting:
    • Placing a stent in the narrowed section of the vessel after balloon angioplasty to keep it open.
  4. Coronary artery bypass grafting:
    • An operation to create a bypass around the narrowed sections of the coronary arteries in order to improve the blood supply to the heart muscle.
  5. A comprehensive rehabilitation programme:
    • Includes physical exercise, dietary advice and teaching on managing stress.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Cardiologists, cardiac surgeons and rehabilitation specialists work together to provide all-round care.
  • Innovative treatments: Access to the most advanced techniques and technology in cardiology.
  • An individual treatment plan: The treatment strategy is chosen according to the particular features of each patient's condition.
  • A high quality of medical care: The use of the newest diagnostic and treatment equipment to achieve the best results.

In Israel, patients with angina receive comprehensive treatment aimed at minimising the risk of cardiovascular events and improving their quality of life.

fields.title: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
fields.bodyHtml:
ADHD (attention deficit hyperactivity disorder): approaches to treatment in Israel

ADHD is a common neurodevelopmental condition characterised by difficulties with attention, impulsiveness and, in some cases, hyperactivity. Israeli medical centres use a comprehensive approach to treating ADHD, combining medication, psychotherapy and educational and support programmes.

Diagnosis of ADHD

  1. Psychological testing: Assessment of cognitive function, attention, concentration and patterns of behaviour.
  2. Medical examination: Ruling out physical conditions that can produce symptoms resembling ADHD.
  3. Questionnaires and rating scales: Used to gather information from parents, teachers and the child about their behaviour in different settings.
  4. Neurological examination: Assessment of neurological status to identify possible abnormalities.

Treatments for ADHD in Israel

  1. Medication:
    • Stimulants (methylphenidate, for example): Improve attention and reduce impulsiveness and hyperactivity.
    • Non-stimulants (atomoxetine, for example): May be used where stimulants are unsuitable or cause side effects.
  2. Psychotherapy:
    • Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT): Helps develop skills of self-control, managing attention and planning.
    • Behavioural therapy: Aimed at improving behaviour at home and at school.
  3. Family counselling and training: Support for parents in bringing up and communicating with a child who has ADHD.
  4. Educational programmes and support sessions: Adapting the learning process to the child's needs and working on improving study skills.
  5. Diet and lifestyle changes: In some cases adjusting the diet and introducing regular exercise can improve the symptoms of ADHD.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Comprehensive assessment and treatment of the child by a team of specialists including psychologists, psychiatrists, neurologists and educators.
  • An individualised treatment plan: The development of a personal treatment and support strategy for each child and family.
  • Access to the newest treatments: The use of advanced medicines and therapeutic techniques.
  • Support and education for the family: Involving parents in the treatment process and giving them the tools to understand and support their child better.

Treatment of ADHD in Israel aims not only to improve the symptoms of the condition but also to integrate the child fully into social and school life, helping them realise their potential to the full.

fields.title: Synovial sarcoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Synovial sarcoma: advanced treatment in Israel

Synovial sarcoma is a rare type of malignant tumour that most often develops near the joints, particularly in the area of the knees, arms and legs. In Israel, patients have access to advanced treatments including surgery, radiotherapy and chemotherapy, as well as the newest approaches in targeted and immune therapy.

Diagnosis of synovial sarcoma:

  1. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    Used to assess the size, position and extent of the tumour and how it relates to the surrounding tissues.
  2. Computed tomography (CT):
    Helps establish whether there are metastases, particularly in the lungs.
  3. Biopsy:
    The key method for obtaining an accurate diagnosis. It may be carried out as an open biopsy or with a fine needle under CT or ultrasound guidance.
  4. PET-CT:
    Effective in assessing the metabolic activity of the tumour and detecting distant metastases.
  5. Laboratory tests:
    These include blood tests to assess general health and the functioning of the organs.

Treatments for synovial sarcoma:

  1. Surgery:
    • Wide local resection: Removal of the tumour together with a margin of healthy tissue around it to minimise the risk of recurrence.
    • Lymphadenectomy: Where metastases in the lymph nodes are suspected.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • May be given before or after the operation to destroy any remaining cancer cells or to shrink the tumour before surgery.
  3. Chemotherapy:
    • Used as neoadjuvant (before surgery) or adjuvant (after surgery) therapy to destroy cancer cells and reduce the risk of the cancer spreading.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy:
    • Targeted medicines: Directed at specific molecular targets involved in the growth and survival of cancer cells.
    • Immunotherapy: Medicines that activate the immune system to fight the cancer.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Oncologists, surgeons, radiologists and other specialists work together to develop an individual treatment plan.
  • Advanced medical equipment and treatments: The use of the newest technology and treatment protocols.
  • Individual treatment: Every treatment plan is adapted to the needs and circumstances of the patient, including their psychological state.

Treatment of synovial sarcoma in Israel aims to achieve the best possible results, minimise side effects and improve patients' quality of life.

fields.title: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM)
fields.bodyHtml:
A continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system is a modern device designed to measure the level of glucose in the blood continuously and in real time. CGM is used primarily in the management of diabetes and allows patients to control their sugar levels more precisely, preventing sharp rises and falls.

How does a CGM system work?

A CGM system has several main components:

  1. The sensor — a small detector placed under the skin, which measures the level of glucose in the interstitial fluid every few minutes.
  2. The transmitter — attaches to the sensor and sends the data to a reader (a smartphone, an insulin pump or a special monitor).
  3. The receiver or app — the device that displays the data, allowing the patient to follow their sugar levels.

The system measures glucose every 1–5 minutes and transmits the data in real time, giving the user a graph of their sugar levels and warnings when readings are too high or too low.

Advantages of using CGM

  1. Continuous monitoring: allows changes in sugar levels to be tracked around the clock, including during sleep and physical activity.
  2. Warnings: the system alerts the user to low or high blood sugar before it occurs.
  3. Better treatment: using the CGM data, the doctor can adjust the insulin dose or choose more suitable therapy.
  4. Tracking trends: the device shows how various factors (food, exercise, stress) affect sugar levels.
  5. Convenience: removes the need for frequent sugar measurements with a glucose meter and finger pricks.

When CGM is used

  • Type 1 diabetes (particularly in children and adolescents).
  • Type 2 diabetes with frequent episodes of low blood sugar.
  • Frequent episodes of low or high blood sugar.
  • Poorly controlled diabetes (unstable sugar levels).
  • Use of an insulin pump.
  • Pregnancy in women with diabetes.

How is CGM fitted?

  1. Fitting the sensor: the sensor is attached to the skin on the abdomen, upper arm or thigh. Fitting is painless and takes only a few minutes.
  2. Connecting the transmitter: the transmitter is connected to the sensor and begins sending data.
  3. Syncing with a device: the glucose data is sent to the receiver or smartphone by Bluetooth or another wireless connection.

Common CGM systems

There are several leading manufacturers of CGM systems on the market:

  • Dexcom G6: an accurate and convenient system that works without finger pricks.
  • FreeStyle Libre: a compact device that is simple to fit and scans the sugar level.
  • Medtronic Guardian Connect: integrates with Medtronic insulin pumps.

Frequently asked questions

  1. Is CGM suitable for everyone with diabetes?
    CGM is suitable for most patients, but whether the device is needed is decided by the doctor, based on the type of diabetes, how often low blood sugar occurs and other factors.
  2. How does CGM differ from a glucose meter?
    A glucose meter shows the sugar level only at the moment of measurement, whereas CGM tracks it 24/7, showing trends and warning of risks.
  3. Is fitting the sensor painful?
    No, fitting the sensor is practically painless and takes only a few minutes.
  4. Can CGM be worn during sport?
    Yes, most CGM devices are water- and dust-resistant, so they can be used during physical activity.
  5. How much does a CGM system cost?
    The cost depends on the model, the country and the healthcare system. Some systems may be partly covered by insurance.

Conclusion

Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) is an innovative technology that makes managing diabetes more convenient and more effective. Thanks to constant monitoring of sugar levels, patients can avoid sharp swings, improve their quality of life and reduce the risk of complications. If you would like to start using CGM, consult an endocrinologist to find the right device for you.

fields.title: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)
fields.bodyHtml:
Systemic lupus erythematosus: modern treatment in Israel

Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the body's own tissues and organs. This can lead to inflammation and damage in various systems of the body, including the skin, joints, kidneys, heart and lungs. SLE can produce a wide variety of symptoms, which makes it difficult to diagnose and treat. Israeli clinics offer advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment aimed at improving patients' quality of life and preventing complications.

Diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus in Israel

Diagnosis of SLE in Israel involves a comprehensive approach based on modern technology and the deep knowledge of its specialists. The main methods of diagnosis include:

  • Clinical examination and history: a detailed study of the patient's symptoms and medical history.
  • Laboratory tests: blood and urine tests to identify the characteristic signs of inflammation and autoimmune reactions.
  • Immunological tests: detection of specific antibodies such as antinuclear antibodies (ANA), anti-dsDNA and other markers indicating SLE.
  • Biopsy: examination of tissue samples to assess the extent of damage to the organs.
  • Imaging: ultrasound, computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to assess the state of the internal organs.

Treatments for systemic lupus erythematosus in Israel

Treatment of SLE in Israel aims to reduce inflammation, control symptoms and prevent damage to the organs. The main treatments include:

  • Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs):
    • Naproxen and ibuprofen: reduce inflammation and address symptoms in the joints; often used as short-term therapy.
  • Steroid ointments: help with the skin rashes caused by lupus.
  • Antimalarial medicines:
    • Hydroxychloroquine: used on its own or in combination with topical steroids for skin rashes; it helps with fatigue and joint pain, lowers cholesterol levels and helps control kidney disease.
  • Steroid tablets:
    • Prednisolone: used as short-term therapy for complications such as pleurisy or pericarditis, and as long-term therapy for other problems including inflammation of the kidneys or serious disorders of the blood-forming system.
  • Disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs):
    • Azathioprine, ciclosporin, cyclophosphamide, methotrexate, mycophenolate: used to suppress the overactive immune system and control raised blood pressure; they help prevent kidney problems and are often used together with steroid tablets so that the steroid dose can be reduced.
  • Biological therapies:
    • Rituximab and belimumab: block or reduce the activity of B cells — the white blood cells that produce the harmful autoantibodies — and are used in lupus where conventional DMARDs do not help.
  • Steroid injections: used for urgent treatment during a lupus flare-up, and can be injected into the scalp where there is hair loss.

Advantages of treating systemic lupus erythematosus in Israel

  1. Highly qualified specialists: doctors with many years of experience in treating SLE and other autoimmune conditions.
  2. Modern technology and equipment: the use of advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment.
  3. A comprehensive approach: individually designed treatment programmes that take account of every feature of the patient's case.
  4. Innovative methods: access to the latest advances in biological therapy and immunotherapy.
  5. Comfortable conditions: a high standard of service and support for patients at every stage of treatment.

Treatment of SLE in Israel aims to achieve lasting remission, improve patients' quality of life and minimise the risk of complications. Thanks to advanced methods and the high professionalism of its doctors, patients can expect the best results in the fight against this complex disease.

fields.title: Scoliosis and kyphosis
fields.bodyHtml:
Scoliosis and kyphosis: advanced treatment in Israel

Scoliosis (sideways curvature of the spine) and kyphosis (excessive forward curvature of the spine) are common conditions of the spine that can cause pain, poor posture and, in severe cases, serious functional problems. Israeli medical centres offer a comprehensive and innovative approach to treating these conditions, including conservative methods, minimally invasive procedures and surgery.

Diagnosis of scoliosis and kyphosis

  1. Clinical examination
    The doctor assesses the degree of curvature of the spine, any visible deformity, restricted movement and other symptoms.
  2. X-rays
    Allow the degree of curvature of the spine to be measured precisely and reveal possible changes in the structure of the vertebrae.
  3. MRI and CT
    Used for detailed imaging of the soft tissues, the intervertebral discs and the nerve structures around the spine.
  4. Laboratory tests
    May be ordered to rule out other conditions contributing to the development of scoliosis or kyphosis.

Treatments in Israel

  1. Conservative treatment:
    • Physiotherapy: Individually designed exercise programmes to strengthen the supporting muscles and correct the curvature.
    • Wearing a brace: Used to stabilise and correct curvature in children and adolescents during growth.
    • Drug treatment: Prescribed to reduce pain and inflammation.
  2. Minimally invasive procedures:
    • Vertebroplasty and kyphoplasty: Procedures to restore the height of the vertebrae and relieve pain in compression fractures.
  3. Surgery:
    • Spinal fusion: Surgical fixation of the vertebrae to stabilise the spine and correct the curvature.
    • Laminectomy: Removal of part of a vertebra to relieve pressure on the nerve roots.
    • Fitting of metal implants: Used to hold the spine in the correct position.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • An individualised approach: Every patient is given a personal treatment programme that takes account of the features of their condition and their general health.
  • Advanced technology: The use of the newest methods of diagnosis and treatment, including minimally invasive techniques and innovative surgical methods.
  • A multidisciplinary team: Doctors of various specialities work together to achieve the best treatment results.
  • Comprehensive rehabilitation: Recovery programmes after treatment are aimed at returning the patient to normal life quickly.

Treatment of scoliosis and kyphosis in Israel gives patients access to the most modern and effective treatments, with strong prospects of an improvement in their condition and quality of life.

fields.title: Stenting
fields.bodyHtml:
Introduction

Stenting is an advanced, minimally invasive procedure used to restore normal blood flow in narrowed or blocked vessels. It is widely used to treat various vascular conditions, including coronary artery disease (CAD), peripheral artery disease (PAD) and vascular stenoses. In this article we describe the methods of diagnosis and treatment and the advantages of stenting in Israel.

Methods of diagnosis

Vascular conditions are usually diagnosed using modern methods that establish the degree of narrowing or blockage of the vessels. These include:

  • Angiography: a procedure in which a contrast medium is introduced into the blood vessels and X-rays are then taken to image the state of the vessels and detect narrowed sections or blockages.
  • Ultrasound scan: ultrasound is used to create images of the vessels and establish their structure and function.
  • Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI): MRI provides detailed images of the vessels and helps establish the degree of narrowing or blockage.

Methods of treatment

Stenting is an invasive procedure carried out in an operating theatre or a specialist medical centre. It is performed under local anaesthetic and does not usually require a general anaesthetic. The treatments include:

  • Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI): a procedure in which a flexible tubular stent is introduced into the narrowed section of a coronary artery through a catheter, to restore normal blood flow and prevent further narrowing.
  • Percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA): in PTA a special balloon is inflated inside the narrowed vessel, widening it and restoring normal blood flow.
  • Peripheral artery stenting: stents are also used to treat narrowing or blockage in the peripheral arteries, such as those of the legs, in order to restore the blood supply to the limbs.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

Israel is one of the leading countries in cardiology and vascular surgery, which makes it an attractive place to have stenting. The advantages of stenting in Israel include:

  • Qualified specialists: Israeli cardiologists and surgeons are highly qualified and have extensive experience in carrying out stenting.
  • Modern technology and equipment: medical institutions in Israel are equipped with advanced devices and technology, which ensures a high level of precision and successful results.
  • An integrated approach to treatment: Israel uses a whole-person approach to the treatment of vascular conditions, which allows patients to be given comprehensive, individual care.

Conclusion

Stenting is an effective and safe treatment for various vascular conditions. The procedure is carried out using advanced technology by experienced specialists in Israel. If you have vascular problems, consult a qualified cardiologist in Israel for the best treatment and the restoration of your health.

fields.title: Tarlatamab
fields.bodyHtml:
An innovative medicine for small cell lung cancer.
In brief: Tarlatamab is a first-in-class bispecific T-cell engager directed at the DLL3 protein, which is expressed on small cell lung cancer (SCLC) cells. It activates the patient's own T lymphocytes and directs them to destroy the tumour cells.

Key features of the medicine

  • Mechanism of action: it binds CD3 on T cells and DLL3 on tumour cells, creating a cytolytic synapse and inducing cell lysis.
  • Indicated in relapsed or progressing extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) after platinum-based chemotherapy.
  • Clinical data: in the phase 2 DeLLphi-301 study, 99 patients showed an objective response rate (ORR) of about 40% and a median duration of response of about 9.7 months.
  • Approved by the US FDA in May 2024.

What to bear in mind during treatment

  • Monitoring is required for cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and neurological toxicity (including immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, ICANS).
  • The medicine is given intravenously with a step-up dosing schedule — for example 1 mg on day 1, 10 mg on days 8 and 15, then every 2 weeks (the dose may be adjusted).
  • For the first infusions, patients need to stay in hospital or a well-equipped cancer centre for the infusion and observation, because of the risk of complications.

What the process looks like for the patient

  1. Preliminary assessment — send in the medical documentation (case history, histology, previous treatment, DLL3 expression, test results).
  2. Consultation with an oncologist and an immunologist, and discussion of suitability and arrangements.
  3. Arrival, first infusions (admission to hospital for observation).
  4. Monitoring for side effects.
  5. Discharge, and a plan for further monitoring and support after treatment.

Cost and estimates

  • This is a high-technology cancer therapy, and the cost is set by an individual estimate (depending on the dose, the length of treatment, accompanying procedures and hospital stay).
  • The estimate covers: the cost of the medicine, the infusion procedures, monitoring (laboratory tests and investigations), hospital admission for the initial doses, and consultations with specialists.
  • Not usually included: accommodation for anyone accompanying the patient, flights, visa costs, and additional supportive treatments if they are not part of the main programme.


Frequently asked questions

Q: Can I have treatment with tarlatamab in Israel?

A: Yes, but only with confirmed small cell lung cancer. The decision is taken by the doctor after reviewing the documentation.

Q: How is the treatment given?

A: The medicine is given intravenously, under observation in hospital because of possible side effects.

Q: When can an effect be seen?

A: In some patients an improvement is seen 2–3 months after treatment begins.

fields.title: Thrombosis
fields.bodyHtml:
Thrombosis: advanced treatment and prevention in Israel

Thrombosis is a condition in which blood clots form in the blood vessels, which can block the flow of blood and lead to serious complications including heart attack and stroke. Israeli medical institutions use modern approaches to the treatment and prevention of thrombosis, based on the latest advances in medical science.

Diagnosis of thrombosis:

  1. Clinical examination and history: The doctor assesses the symptoms and the risk factors for developing thrombosis.
  2. Doppler ultrasound: Allows the blood flow to be assessed and clots in the veins to be detected.
  3. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT): Used to diagnose clots in the deep veins and arteries.
  4. Coagulation screen: A laboratory test of blood clotting.

Treatments for thrombosis:

  1. Drug therapy:
    • Anticoagulants: Medicines that prevent new clots forming and existing ones growing.
    • Thrombolytics: Used to dissolve clots that have already formed.
    • Anti-inflammatory medicines: To reduce inflammation and pain around the clot.
  2. Surgery:
    • Thrombectomy: Removal of the clot from the vessel.
    • Fitting a vena cava filter in the inferior vena cava to prevent clots travelling from the legs to the lungs.
  3. Compression therapy: Wearing compression stockings to improve the flow of blood in the veins and prevent clots forming.
  4. Physiotherapy: Specific exercises to improve blood flow and prevent thrombosis.

Prevention of thrombosis:

  • An active lifestyle: Regular exercise to stimulate the circulation.
  • Diet: A diet rich in omega-3 fatty acids and low in saturated fats, to keep the blood vessels healthy.
  • Avoiding long periods of inactivity: Regular breaks to move about during long journeys or sedentary work.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Specialists from various fields of medicine work together to create an individual treatment plan for every patient.
  • Access to innovative treatments: The use of the latest medical developments and medicines.
  • Modern diagnostic technology: Ensuring accurate diagnosis and monitoring of patients' condition.
  • A comprehensive approach to prevention: The development of individual recommendations on lifestyle changes to reduce the risk of thrombosis.

Treatment and prevention of thrombosis in Israel is carried out through integrated programmes aimed at minimising the risk of complications and improving patients' general health.

fields.title: Vacuum disc removal
fields.bodyHtml:
Vacuum disc removal, also known as percutaneous disc aspiration, is a minimally invasive procedure for treating a herniated disc. It can be used to reduce pain and restore the function of the spine in patients suffering from back pain caused by a herniated intervertebral disc, where conservative treatment has brought no relief.

How vacuum disc removal is carried out:

  1. Preparation
    The patient may be offered a local anaesthetic to reduce discomfort during the procedure.
  2. The procedure
    A special needle instrument is introduced through the skin under fluoroscopy (real-time X-ray guidance) to reach the affected disc. A vacuum aspirator is then passed through the needle to remove part of the affected disc material, which reduces the pressure on the nerve roots.
  3. Completing the procedure: Once part of the disc has been removed, the instruments are withdrawn and a sterile dressing is applied to the puncture site. The procedure usually takes about 30–60 minutes.

Advantages:

  • A minimally invasive approach
    No large surgical incision is needed, which reduces the risk of infection and speeds up recovery.
  • Rapid recovery
    Patients can often go home the same day and resume their usual activities within a few days of the procedure.
  • Less pain
    Compared with traditional surgery, vacuum disc removal causes less pain afterwards.

The choice of treatment for a herniated disc should be based on thorough investigation and consultation with a specialist. Vacuum disc removal can be an effective solution for patients looking for a minimally invasive alternative to traditional surgery.

fields.title: Bunion (hallux valgus)
fields.bodyHtml:
Treatment of hallux valgus in Israel: advanced methods and approaches

Israel offers a comprehensive approach to the treatment of hallux valgus, combining highly qualified specialists, innovative methods of diagnosis and treatment, and individualised rehabilitation programmes. This condition, commonly known as a bunion, causes not only discomfort and pain but can also lead to problems with walking and with the overall function of the foot.

Diagnosis of hallux valgus

  1. Clinical examination
    Allows assessment of the degree of deformity, the pain and any restriction of movement.
  2. X-rays
    Needed to measure the angle of deviation of the toe and the degree of arthritis in the joint.
  3. MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) and CT (computed tomography)
    Used in complex cases to assess the state of the bones, joints and soft tissues of the foot.
  4. Ultrasound scan
    Used to image the soft tissues, including the tendons and ligaments.
  5. Laboratory tests
    Although laboratory tests are not used directly to diagnose hallux valgus, they may be ordered to rule out inflammatory and rheumatic conditions that can contribute to the symptoms or complicate treatment.

Treatments for hallux valgus in Israel

  1. Conservative treatment
    • Orthopaedic aids, including supportive insoles and night splints to correct the position of the toe.
    • Physiotherapy to strengthen the muscles of the foot and improve its function.
    • Anti-inflammatory and pain-relieving medicines to reduce pain and swelling.
  2. Surgery
    • Osteotomy: Correction of the bones of the foot to restore the correct position of the big toe.
    • Arthrodesis: Fixing the joint in the correct position to relieve pain and restore function.
    • Exostectomy: Removal of the bony growth on the joint.
    • Soft tissue reconstruction: Correction of the ligaments and tendons to hold the big toe in the correct position.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach
    Assessment and treatment by specialists from various fields — orthopaedic surgeons, rehabilitation specialists and physiotherapists.
  • Advanced technology
    Israeli clinics use the newest surgical techniques, which are minimally invasive and deliver rapid recovery and excellent long-term results.
  • Individualised treatment
    The treatment plan is developed with each patient's individual circumstances, needs and expectations in mind.
  • Comprehensive rehabilitation
    Extensive recovery programmes after surgery help achieve the best functional result and a return to normal life.

Treatment of hallux valgus in Israel offers patients not only relief from pain and discomfort but also restoration of the appearance of the foot and an improvement in its function and in quality of life.

fields.title: Varicocele
fields.bodyHtml:
Varicocele: modern treatment in Israel

Varicocele, an enlargement of the veins in the scrotum, can affect male fertility. Israel uses advanced techniques to diagnose and treat this condition, providing a comprehensive approach to resolving the problem and improving reproductive health.

Diagnosis of varicocele:

  1. Physical examination and history
    Allows the enlarged veins to be identified when standing or straining.
  2. Scrotal ultrasound with Doppler
    Assesses the blood flow and the presence of reverse flow in the veins of the scrotum.
  3. Semen analysis
    The key test for assessing the effect of the varicocele on fertility. It shows the number, movement and shape of the sperm and other important features of the seminal fluid.
  4. Thermography
    May be used to identify the changes in temperature associated with a varicocele.

Treatments for varicocele:

  1. Microsurgical varicocelectomy
    Considered the gold standard of treatment, minimising risks and delivering excellent long-term results.
  2. Laparoscopic surgery
    A minimally invasive method with small incisions and rapid recovery.
  3. Embolisation of the scrotal veins
    A minimally invasive procedure in which a substance is introduced through a catheter to block the enlarged vein.
  4. Sclerotherapy
    A method in which a special sclerosing solution is injected into the vein, causing it to seal shut and be taken out of the circulation, thereby removing the cause of the varicocele. The procedure may be carried out under ultrasound or X-ray guidance.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An individual approach to every patient: In Israel considerable attention is given to the particular features of the condition and its effect on each man's fertility.
  • Highly qualified specialists: Israeli doctors have extensive experience in treating varicocele and use the most modern techniques.
  • The use of the latest technology: The use of the newest equipment and treatments makes the therapy highly effective and minimises the risk of complications.
  • A comprehensive approach to fertility: As well as treating the varicocele itself, doctors give particular attention to restoring and improving the patient's reproductive function.

Treatment of varicocele in Israel aims not only to resolve the physical problem but also to improve the overall quality of life of men affected by this condition, including the restoration of their fertility.

fields.title: Varicose veins of the legs
fields.bodyHtml:
Varicose veins of the legs: advanced treatment in Israel

Varicose veins of the legs are a condition involving impaired circulation and changes in the structure of the vein walls, which leads to their enlargement, the formation of "knots" and poorer blood flow. Modern methods of diagnosing and treating varicose veins are available in Israel, which deal effectively with the problem and help avoid complications.

Diagnosis of varicose veins of the legs

  1. Duplex scanning (ultrasound with Doppler)
    The main diagnostic method, allowing the structure and function of the veins to be assessed.
  2. Venography
    An X-ray examination with a contrast medium to assess the state of the deep veins.
  3. Examination by a vein specialist
    Includes visual examination and palpation of the veins, and assessment of the patient's symptoms and history.
  4. Laboratory tests
    Although laboratory tests are not used directly to diagnose varicose veins, they may be ordered to rule out accompanying conditions such as thrombosis and to assess the patient's general health.

Treatments for varicose veins in Israel

  1. Conservative treatment:
    • Compression therapy
      Wearing specialist compression stockings.
    • Drug treatment
      Medicines to improve the tone of the veins and the flow of blood and to prevent thrombosis.
  2. Minimally invasive procedures:
    • Sclerotherapy
      Injection of a special solution into the vein, causing it to seal shut and be taken out of the circulation.
    • Endovenous laser treatment (EVLT)
      Closing the affected veins with a laser.
    • Radiofrequency ablation (RFA)
      The use of radiofrequency energy to treat varicose veins.
  3. Surgery:
    • Phlebectomy
      Removal of the affected sections of vein through small incisions under local anaesthetic.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • An individualised approach: Every patient is given a personal treatment plan that takes account of the features of their condition.
  • Advanced treatments: Access to the newest and most effective treatments for varicose veins, including laser and radiofrequency technology.
  • Highly qualified specialists: The best vein specialists and vascular surgeons, with international experience and a high level of qualification.
  • A comprehensive approach to recovery: Covers not only treating the varicose veins but also preventing them recurring and improving the overall state of the venous system.

Treatment of varicose veins of the legs in Israel gives patients the opportunity not only to be rid of the symptoms of the condition but also to improve their quality of life considerably, preventing potential complications from developing.

fields.title: Vertebroplasty
fields.bodyHtml:
Vertebroplasty is a minimally invasive surgical procedure designed to relieve pain and strengthen weak or damaged vertebrae. The technique is becoming increasingly popular thanks to its effectiveness and safety. It is particularly useful in treating osteoporosis, cancers of the spine and injuries.

Symptoms

The main symptoms indicating that vertebroplasty may be needed are:

  • Chronic back pain that worsens with movement or exertion;
  • Loss of height because of compression of the vertebrae;
  • Restricted movement and flexibility of the spine;
  • Increased pain when lying down.

Methods of diagnosis

Diagnosis involves a set of investigations, including:

  • X-rays of the spine;
  • Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI);
  • Computed tomography (CT);
  • Bone densitometry to assess bone density.

Methods of treatment

The vertebroplasty procedure involves injecting a special bone cement into the damaged vertebra under X-ray guidance. The cement sets quickly, stabilising the vertebra and considerably reducing the pain.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

Israel occupies a leading position in world medicine thanks to:

  • The use of advanced technology and innovative treatments;
  • Highly qualified medical staff;
  • An individual approach to every patient;
  • Modern diagnostic equipment;
  • Shorter recovery times and minimal complications.

Conclusion

Vertebroplasty is an effective and safe way of relieving pain and strengthening the spine. The procedure helps patients return quickly to an active life and improves their quality of life. Treatment in Israel offers advanced technology and a high standard of medical care, which makes it one of the best choices for this kind of operation.

fields.title: Stomach ulcer
fields.bodyHtml:
Stomach ulcer: advanced treatment in Israel

A stomach ulcer is a chronic condition in which deep defects (ulcers) form in the lining of the stomach, causing pain, discomfort and other serious symptoms. Israeli clinics offer a comprehensive approach to treating this condition, including modern diagnostic procedures, individualised drug treatment and, where necessary, surgery.

Diagnosis of a stomach ulcer:

  1. Gastroscopy (upper gastrointestinal endoscopy)
    The main diagnostic method, allowing the inner surface of the stomach to be seen and a biopsy taken for examination.
  2. Tests for Helicobacter pylori
    Detection of the bacterium often associated with the development of ulcers, using a breath test, a blood test or tissue taken during endoscopy.
  3. Barium X-ray of the stomach
    Used to image the stomach and identify changes in its outline and function.

Treatments for a stomach ulcer:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) and H2 receptor blockers: Reduce the production of stomach acid, creating the conditions for the ulcer to heal.
    • Medicines to eradicate Helicobacter pylori: A combination of antibiotics and a PPI to destroy the bacterium where it is present.
    • Medicines to protect the lining of the stomach: Sucralfate, for example, which creates a protective layer over the surface of the ulcer.
  2. Surgery:
    • Used where drug treatment is ineffective, or where there are complications (bleeding, perforation, narrowing of the outlet of the stomach).

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A high standard of diagnosis: The use of advanced technology and highly qualified specialists for accurate diagnosis and to establish the best treatment strategy.
  • An individual approach to treatment: Medicines and treatments are chosen according to the patient's individual circumstances and the nature of the condition.
  • Scientific advances brought into clinical practice: The use of the latest scientific developments to make treatment more effective and shorten patients' recovery time.
  • Multidisciplinary medical teams: Gastroenterologists, surgeons, infectious disease specialists and others work together to provide a comprehensive approach to treatment.
  • Modern medical facilities: Clinics are equipped with state-of-the-art technology, which allows highly accurate diagnostic and treatment procedures in comfortable conditions for patients.
  • Support and rehabilitation: As well as active treatment, considerable attention is given to the patient's recovery and continued health afterwards, including dietary advice and psychological support.

Treatment of a stomach ulcer in Israel is aimed at achieving lasting remission and the greatest possible improvement in patients' quality of life. With an individual approach and the use of innovative treatments, patients can considerably reduce the symptoms of the condition and prevent complications.

fields.title: Ankle replacement
fields.bodyHtml:
Ankle replacement: innovative approaches in Israel

Ankle replacement is a high-technology operation aimed at restoring function and relieving pain in an ankle joint damaged by arthritis, injury or other conditions. In Israel, patients have access to advanced treatments that achieve excellent results and considerably improve quality of life.

Investigations before ankle replacement

  1. Clinical examination
    Assessment of the pain, the degree of restricted movement and the effect of the state of the joint on the patient's daily life.
  2. X-rays
    Allow assessment of the degree of degenerative change in the joint and the presence of deformity and erosions.
  3. MRI and CT
    Used for detailed imaging of the soft tissues, cartilage and bones around the ankle.
  4. Laboratory tests
    May be ordered to rule out systemic inflammatory conditions.

Methods of ankle replacement in Israel

  1. Total ankle replacement
    Replacement of the damaged joint with an artificial implant that reproduces its natural function and relieves the pain.
  2. Partial replacement
    May be carried out where only one part of the joint is damaged.
  3. Minimally invasive techniques
    Used to shorten recovery time and minimise the risk of complications.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • Highly qualified specialists: Israeli orthopaedic surgeons have rich experience in joint replacement, including of the ankle.
  • Advanced medical equipment: The use of modern prostheses and technology, which makes the operation highly precise and the implant long-lasting.
  • An individualised approach: Every patient is given a personal treatment plan based on their clinical picture and particular needs.
  • Comprehensive rehabilitation: Includes individually designed physiotherapy and rehabilitation programmes to speed up recovery and the return to normal life.

Ankle replacement in Israel gives patients the chance to be rid of chronic pain, restore mobility and return to an active life. Thanks to the comprehensive approach to treatment and the use of the latest advances in medical science, ankle replacement surgery in Israel is a highly effective solution for people suffering from serious joint conditions.

fields.title: Elbow replacement
fields.bodyHtml:
Elbow replacement: innovative approaches in Israel

Elbow replacement in Israel is an advanced procedure designed to improve the quality of life of patients suffering from severe pain and restricted movement because of arthritis, injury or other conditions of the elbow. Thanks to its international standing in orthopaedics and its use of modern technology, Israel offers effective solutions for restoring the function of the elbow joint.

Investigations before elbow replacement

  1. Physical examination
    Assessment of the degree of pain, the mobility and stability of the joint, and the effect of the state of the joint on the patient's daily life.
  2. X-rays
    Allow the degree of damage to the joint and the presence of deformity or bony growths to be established.
  3. MRI and CT
    Used for more detailed imaging of the soft tissues and bones around the elbow, and help identify hidden damage.
  4. Electromyography (EMG)
    May be ordered to assess the state of the nerves passing through the elbow, where neurological problems are suspected.

Methods of elbow replacement

  1. Total elbow replacement
    Complete replacement of the elbow joint with an artificial implant; recommended for patients with serious destruction of the joint.
  2. Partial replacement
    Replacement of one component of the elbow joint; can be effective where the damage is localised.
  3. Revision replacement
    Replacement of an existing prosthesis with a new one; needed where the implant has worn out or there have been complications after a previous operation.
  4. Arthroscopy
    A minimally invasive procedure for treating damage inside the joint.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • Highly qualified specialists
    Israeli orthopaedic surgeons have extensive experience in complex operations on the elbow joint and regularly update their knowledge by taking part in international congresses and exchanges.
  • Advanced medical equipment
    The use of the most modern prostheses and replacement techniques, including minimally invasive methods that allow rapid recovery.
  • An individualised approach
    Every treatment plan is developed individually, taking account of the patient's anatomy and the demands of their life.
  • Comprehensive rehabilitation
    Multimodal rehabilitation programmes designed to speed up recovery and the return to normal life.

Elbow replacement in Israel is a modern solution for those who want to be rid of pain and restore the function of the arm. Patients can expect a high standard of medical care, attentive treatment and an individual approach.

fields.title: Shoulder replacement
fields.bodyHtml:
Shoulder replacement: advanced techniques in Israel

Shoulder replacement in Israel is an innovative area of orthopaedics that offers patients with osteoarthritis, arthritis or injuries of the shoulder the chance to improve their quality of life considerably. Using advanced technology and an individual approach, Israeli clinics deliver highly effective treatment and rapid recovery.

Investigations before shoulder replacement

  1. Physical examination
    The doctor carries out a thorough examination and takes a history in order to establish the degree of loss of function in the joint and the extent of the pain.
  2. X-rays
    Needed to assess the degree of damage to the joint and establish the form and extent of the arthritic changes.
  3. MRI
    Provides detailed images of the soft tissues of the joint, including the cartilage, tendons and ligaments.
  4. Computed tomography (CT)
    Used for a more precise assessment of the bony structures.

Methods of shoulder replacement

  1. Total shoulder replacement
    Replacement of the whole shoulder joint with an artificial one. This is the recommended method where the joint is seriously damaged.
  2. Partial replacement
    Replacement of the head of the humerus only. It can be effective where the damage is limited.
  3. Reverse shoulder replacement
    Used in patients with serious damage to the rotator cuff. This method restores the function of the joint by changing its anatomical structure.
  4. Arthroscopy
    A minimally invasive procedure for treating damage inside the joint.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • An individualised approach
    Every patient is offered treatment adapted as closely as possible to their individual needs and general health.
  • Highly qualified specialists
    Israeli orthopaedic surgeons have rich experience in joint replacement and use the most modern techniques in their practice.
  • Modern medical equipment
    Operations are carried out using the latest advances in medical technology and high-quality prostheses.
  • Minimally invasive techniques
    The use of minimally invasive methods shortens recovery time and reduces the risk of complications.

Treatment and replacement of the shoulder joint in Israel is a byword for a high standard of medical care, an individual approach and the use of innovative technology that delivers the best treatment results. Patients who choose Israel for shoulder replacement surgery can expect attentive treatment and quality medical care.

Recovery and rehabilitation after the operation

Recovery after shoulder replacement in Israel involves a comprehensive approach to rehabilitation, which begins immediately after the operation and aims at a rapid return of movement and strength in the shoulder. The rehabilitation programme usually includes:

  • Physiotherapy: Prescribed to improve the range of movement and strengthen the muscles around the new joint.
  • Occupational therapy: Helps the patient adapt to everyday tasks and return to normal life.
  • Individual exercises: Designed to restore the function of the shoulder and prevent possible complications.
  • Pain relief: Used to control pain in the period after the operation.

Innovations in treatment

Israel is actively introducing innovative approaches into the treatment of orthopaedic conditions, including the development and use of biocompatible materials for prostheses, which give the implant a longer working life and reduce the risk of rejection. Attention is also being given to the development of 3D printing technology to create individualised prostheses adapted as closely as possible to each patient's anatomy.

Choosing Israel for shoulder replacement surgery guarantees not only access to advanced medical technology and highly qualified specialists but also a comprehensive approach to treatment and rehabilitation, which aids the quickest possible recovery and return to an active life.

fields.title: Heart valve replacement
fields.bodyHtml:
Introduction

Heart valve replacement is a complex operation that can save lives and improve the quality of life of people with serious heart conditions. The heart valves play a key part in maintaining proper circulation, but they can be damaged or become leaky for various reasons. In this article we describe the methods of diagnosis and treatment and the advantages of heart valve replacement in Israel.

Methods of diagnosis

Assessing the state of the heart valves is critically important before a decision on replacement is taken. Modern diagnostic methods include:

  • Echocardiography: a non-invasive method that uses ultrasound to create an image of the heart. Echocardiography allows the structure and function of the heart valves to be assessed and any damage or leakage to be identified.
  • Computed tomography (CT): this method provides detailed slices of the heart and valves, which helps doctors assess the situation more precisely and decide whether replacement is needed.
  • Cardiac catheterisation: an invasive procedure in which a catheter is passed through the blood vessels into the heart to measure pressures and assess the working of the valves.

Methods of treatment

Treatment of heart valve disease depends on the type and extent of the damage. The main treatments include:

  • Drug therapy: doctors may prescribe medicines to improve the function of the heart and control symptoms, but where the valves are seriously damaged surgery may be required.
  • Surgical repair: in some cases, where the damage to the valve is slight, it can be repaired rather than replaced.
  • Valve replacement: the most effective treatment where the heart valves are severely damaged or leaking. The replacement may be mechanical (an artificial prosthesis) or biological (a tissue prosthesis).

Advantages of treatment in Israel

Israel is one of the world leaders in the surgical treatment of heart disease, including valve replacement. The advantages of heart valve replacement in Israel include:

  • Qualified specialists: Israeli cardiac surgeons have extensive experience and knowledge in heart valve replacement.
  • Modern technology and equipment: medical institutions in Israel are equipped with advanced devices and technology, which ensures a high level of professionalism and successful treatment results.
  • An individual approach to treatment: every patient is given an individual, comprehensive approach to treatment that takes account of their particular circumstances and needs.

Conclusion

Heart valve replacement is an effective operation that can considerably improve the quality of life of patients with serious heart conditions. It is important to seek help in good time and to choose qualified specialists. Israel, as a world leader in cardiac surgery, provides high-quality heart valve replacement using advanced technology and an individual approach to every patient. If you have problems with your heart valves, do not delay in consulting a doctor.

fields.title: Hip replacement
fields.bodyHtml:
Hip replacement: an advanced approach in Israel

Hip replacement, or hip arthroplasty, is one of the most effective operations offered in Israel for the treatment of severe osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, injuries and other conditions that destroy the hip joint. The operation restores movement in the joint, considerably reduces or completely removes the pain, and greatly improves patients' quality of life.

Investigations before hip replacement

  1. Clinical examination
    Includes assessment of the symptoms, the degree of restricted movement and general health.
  2. X-rays
    The main diagnostic method, allowing the degree of damage to the joint to be established and the right implant to be chosen.
  3. MRI and CT
    Used for a detailed assessment of the bone, cartilage and soft tissues.
  4. Laboratory tests
    May be ordered to identify signs of inflammation, infection or autoimmune conditions.

Methods of hip replacement in Israel

  1. Total hip replacement
    Complete replacement of the joint with an artificial implant that reproduces its natural function.
  2. Minimally invasive surgical methods
    Shorten recovery time and reduce the risk of complications after the operation through the use of smaller incisions.
  3. The use of high-technology implants
    The application of the latest advances in materials science and biomechanics to produce durable and reliable prostheses.
  4. Computer planning and navigation
    Improves the precision with which the prosthesis is positioned, which contributes to a better functional result and a longer-lasting implant.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

  • Highly qualified specialists: Israel is home to some of the world's leading orthopaedic surgeons, with extensive experience in hip replacement.
  • An individualised approach: Every case is considered individually, and the plan for the operation and the choice of implant take account of the patient's anatomy and way of life.
  • Advanced medical technology: The use of modern equipment and materials makes operations highly precise and prostheses long-lasting.
  • Comprehensive rehabilitation: Includes individually designed exercise programmes aimed at rapid recovery and a return to an active life.

Hip replacement in Israel gives patients the chance to return to a full life without the pain and limitations of joint disease. Thanks to the comprehensive approach to treatment, patients can expect an individualised recovery programme and high standards of medical care.

fields.title: Female infertility
fields.bodyHtml:
Female infertility: advanced treatment in Israel

Female infertility is the inability to conceive after a year of regular sexual activity without contraception. Clinics in Israel offer a comprehensive approach to the diagnosis and treatment of female infertility, using the latest scientific advances and technology to improve the chances of conceiving successfully.

Diagnosis of female infertility:

  1. Gynaecological examination and history: Important for identifying possible physical causes of infertility, such as abnormalities in the development of the reproductive organs.
  2. Ultrasound scan: Allows the state of the ovaries, womb and fallopian tubes to be assessed.
  3. Hormone profile: Measurement of the key hormones affecting reproductive function.
  4. Hysterosalpingography (HSG): A contrast X-ray examination to assess whether the fallopian tubes are open.
  5. Laparoscopy: A minimally invasive operation used for a detailed examination of the pelvic organs and to identify endometriosis or other internal problems.
  6. Endometrial biopsy: A procedure to assess the state of the lining of the womb.

Treatments for female infertility:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Hormone therapy: The use of medicines to stimulate ovulation, such as clomifene citrate or gonadotropins.
    • Treatment of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS): A combination of medication and lifestyle changes to restore the ovulatory cycle.
  2. Surgery:
    • Laparoscopic surgery: Used to remove physical obstacles such as adhesions or areas of endometriosis that may prevent conception.
    • Hysteroscopic surgery: Removal of polyps or fibroids in the womb that may prevent an embryo implanting.
  3. Assisted reproductive technology (ART):
    • Artificial insemination (IUI): Introduction of sperm into the cavity of the womb at the time of ovulation.
    • In vitro fertilisation (IVF): Collection of eggs for fertilisation in the laboratory, followed by transfer of the embryo into the womb.
  4. Egg and embryo donation: An option for women who have problems with the quality of their eggs or genetic disorders.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Close cooperation between gynaecologists, endocrinologists, fertility specialists and psychologists.
  • Advanced equipment and technology: The use of the most modern techniques and devices for diagnosis and treatment.
  • An individualised treatment plan: Every patient is given a personalised plan that takes account of every aspect of her health and her wishes.

Treatment of female infertility in Israel aims to achieve the best possible results, giving every woman the chance to experience the joy of motherhood.

fields.title: Goitre
fields.bodyHtml:
Goitre: modern treatment in Israel

A goitre is an enlargement of the thyroid gland, which can have various causes including a lack of iodine in the diet, autoimmune conditions, congenital factors and others. Israel uses a comprehensive approach to the diagnosis and treatment of goitre, combining advanced diagnostic methods, individualised treatment plans and modern surgical technology.

Diagnosis of goitre:

  1. Examination and palpation
    The doctor examines and feels the area of the neck to assess the size and consistency of the thyroid gland.
  2. Ultrasound scan
    The main diagnostic method, allowing the structure and size of the gland and the presence of nodules to be assessed.
  3. Blood tests
    Measurement of thyroid hormone levels (T3, T4) and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) to establish how the thyroid gland is functioning.
  4. Biopsy
    Carried out where there are suspicious nodules, to rule out thyroid cancer.

Treatments for goitre in Israel:

  1. Drug treatment
    The use of medicines to correct thyroid hormone levels and reduce the size of the goitre.
  2. Iodine supplements
    Prescribed where iodine deficiency is the main cause of the goitre.
  3. Surgery
    Recommended where the goitre is large, presses on the surrounding tissues, is suspected of being cancerous, or where drug treatment has not worked. Israeli surgeons use minimally invasive methods, including endoscopic techniques.
  4. Radioactive iodine therapy
    Used in overactive thyroid caused by a goitre, and in some forms of thyroid cancer.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A personalised approach
    The treatment plan is drawn up individually for every patient, taking account of the features of the condition and their general health.
  • Highly qualified specialists
    Israeli doctors are internationally recognised and have extensive experience in diagnosing and treating conditions of the thyroid gland.
  • Access to the newest technology
    The use of modern diagnostic and surgical equipment ensures accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • A comprehensive approach
    Specialists from various fields of medicine are involved in treatment, which ensures the patient's full recovery.

Treatment of goitre in Israel aims to address the causes of the condition, correct the function of the thyroid gland and prevent complications, allowing patients to lead a full life.
